## W-905: Project Review 1 budget pack

The pack is written, `node tools/ledger.mjs check` and `npm run check` pass, and it is committed and pushed as 0b6a3c1 on ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. The commit has only my four files and no [deploy]. I did not touch board.json or progress.md. Every figure is my proposal: I wrote them, so I cannot approve any of them. The founder decides at the review.

**One finding changes the unit cost.** The event log still stops at 2026-10-14 15:20. I read the 115 later finished runs (16.1M tokens) from the session transcript, read-only, and wrote them to neither the event log nor the ledger. That gives 77.4M over 588 runs and 635 published, so **122k per published lesson all-in** (it was 101k). Don't quote the 96k that `ledger.mjs report` prints today: it divides the stale 61.2M by today's 635.

### Budget table

| Project | Tranche | Tokens | Money (all unverified) | Return measure | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| first-light (Head of Strategic Initiatives; chief-of-staff until W-904) | T1 to 2026-10-23: design, EDD-007 records, a spike per workstream, the Surface Value amendment, the new role, the war room | 3.59M | Vercel Pro ~$20/mo; domain ~$10-20/yr; Postgres $0 free / ~$5-25 paid; auth $0 (Auth.js, needs a decision record) or ~$25; monitoring $0 / ~$26. Total ~$21 to ~$100 a month. Ad revenue at launch: $0 (house cards only) | Go on 2026-11-23 with an EDD-007 record on every tier-2 path and no SEV1/SEV2 open; analytics-steward's launch metrics (accounts, history kept at sign-up, 7-day return); tokens per workstream against plan | T2 is released only if the W-908 re-estimate is at or under 10.2M (1.25x) and F-01 is decided by 2026-10-23. Otherwise it comes back with cuts, in this order: ad slot, light social, challenges |
| first-light | T2: build to launch | 8.17M (program total 11.76M) | as above | as above | Ad slot and social are cut to release 2 if the privacy ruling (and, for the slot, the amendment) is not filed by 2026-11-09. A second no-go returns it to the forum. At 11.76M with no go, stop |
| ...auth/progress · personalization · mastery · social · ad slot · legal · infra · amendment · war room | T1 / T2 | 445k/1,729k · 357k/1,144k · 393k/1,221k · 259k/823k · 364k/530k · 288k/287k · 337k/950k · 429k/0 · 718k/1,485k | | | |
| ads, stage 2 (paid) | not budgeted | 0 | | | Comes back as its own project after F-17/F-20 |
| behavioral-econ | T1: DLR, rulings, sourcing note, cm-behavioral, DomainId, HQ, neighbour sign-offs, pilot of 5 | **1.83M (not 0.6M)** | $0 | Published lessons once the DomainId exists; held-claim rate; the path's commit rate and 7-day recall against the feed median | Pause if 3 of the DLR five are duplicates, held claims pass 40%, or 1.83M is spent before the five are reviewed |
| behavioral-econ | T2: 30 lessons | **4.03M (not 3.0M)** | $0 | as above | Released only on the four triggers in the vertical's §7. Fold into Economics after 60 days if recall and commit are below the feed median |
| history (F-16 (a); proposal of record is Selin's W-723) | T1: ~25 lessons (15 drafts already built) | 2.5M, counted from approval | $0 | Published History lessons; held-claim rate | Stop at the DLR five if more than 40% of claims are held or fewer than 3 reach launch |
| history | T2: ~75 lessons plus sensitive-route reviews | ~10.8M, not asked now | $0 | as above | All four F-16 triggers |
| scale-stage-1 (A1 + the A2 pilot of 50) | T1, checkpoint at 1.2M | 2.45M (yesterday: 3.0M for all of stage 1) | GitHub Pro ~$4/mo; a bigger host at $60-150/mo only if measurements still fail | `/` JS down at least 2.3 MB gz; build at most 5 min whatever the lesson count; at most 30 s QA per changed lesson; warm frame at most 300 ms | Fall back to same-origin `import()` if warm stays over 300 ms; abandon if build and QA miss those lines; revert A1 if JS does not drop; stop anything that blocks First Light |
| scale-stage-1 | T2: the other ~910 lessons | 3-4M (extrapolated), later review | | | |
| P3-P6 | maintenance line (not major, never gated) | ~0.64M | $0 | | |

### Total and what it displaces

- **W-905 first tranches:** 10.37M. Adding the items already on the agenda (wave-j 15M, lifehacks-engine-v2 3M, books-decks 1.5M, marketing 1M) brings all first tranches at Project Review 1 to **30.87M**. The W-905 programs in full come to about 36.9M.
- **Capacity:** token-budget.md sets no limit. It deliberately does not compare `subagent_tokens` with the plan's usage limit until the unit is established (item 0b). So I show measured throughput instead:
  - Under the 8-agent / 3-builder caps, one 6.75 h window ran at about 1.0M an hour (one window only, so treat the rate as an estimate). The busiest 24 h under the old caps was 44.2M.
  - At that rate, 30.87M is about 30 active hours. First Light is about 12 hours spread over six weeks.
  - In our own unit, tokens are not what binds. The caveat: on 2026-10-13 the plan's usage limit did stop builders. I added agenda question 0d: name the capacity limit.
- **What it displaces:**
  - In tokens: about 85 published-lesson equivalents (10.37M at 122k), about 250 for all first tranches, about 300 for the full programs.
  - In review: History T1 and the behavioral pilot put 30 lessons into a queue of 325 against the gate of 160, one for one against Wave J.
  - In engineering: about 40 First Light code runs, 19 PE reviews and 13 privacy-reviewer runs. That role has never run.
  - Founder decisions: at least 7.
  - If tokens must be cut, the lever is Wave J's 15M.

### How sure I am

- **High:** the measured per-role unit costs.
- **Medium-low:** run counts per workstream. They are guesses, so the first tranche buys the measurements.
- **Extrapolated:** there are no coding runs by backend-engineer and no runs at all by learner-model-engineer, personalization-lead, growth-designer, privacy-reviewer or a research lead, so those units are proxies.
- **Medium:** behavioral-econ's 0.6M undercounts set-up for any variant, even the strand one.
- Selin's W-723 proposal was not on disk yet. My History figures are check numbers for it, not a duplicate.

### Two things to know

- **History status:** History and scale-stage-1 keep their existing statuses (in-flight and proposed). I did not set History to "proposed", because that would make the gate refuse in-flight History work before its grace period ends.
- **First Light dispatches:** `ledger.mjs gate --project=first-light` now refuses tagged dispatches until the forum rules. The week-1 scoping (W-904, W-907, W-908) runs as small untagged work.

### Next moves

1. **chief-of-staff:** file a board item for the section 9 check: `ledger.mjs check` warns on initiative items in the founder inbox that have no `budget` field. It goes to you and tools-lead, since founder-inbox.json has one writer.
2. **chief-of-staff:** run `node tools/events.mjs backfill`, then I run `ledger.mjs import`.
3. **principal-pm-verticals:** reconcile W-723 with the History check figures, and confirm or re-score the behavioral-econ pre-mortem.
4. **principal-engineer:** re-score scale-stage-1 (W-727) and do the W-908 re-estimate.

body:
**Platform Engineer report: release r7 fixes (W-884/W-480, W-878, W-879)**

All three fixes are committed on `r7-fixes` as **1b7ac14** in /home/user/s3c-r7. It is not pushed and has no `[deploy]`. **It must not ship yet:** this is a tier-2 change and its readiness record has not been approved. Nothing protected was touched (`src/kit/Lesson.tsx`, `tools/company.mjs`, `tests/qa/**`). No test id was renamed. I did not edit board.json or progress.md.

**What changed**
1. **W-884/W-480, drafts.** A new file, `src/lib/visibility.ts`, decides which lessons can be shown, and `src/lib/catalog.ts` now uses it.
   - Drafts are never served when `VERCEL_ENV=production`, whatever SHOW_REVIEW or SHOW_DRAFTS say.
   - On Vercel previews they are hidden unless `SHOW_DRAFTS=on`.
   - They stay visible on the dev server and in local `next start` builds, so `npm run verify` (which runs QA over the 81 drafts) stays green.
   - `SHOW_DRAFTS=off` hides them anywhere.
   - "In review" lessons stay visible and tagged, as the founder decided.
2. **W-878, internal notes.** A new file, `src/lib/trust.ts`, builds a learner-safe copy of each lesson's meta. Both `/api/meta/<slug>` and the lesson page now send only that copy. Each claim is reduced to: text, support type, status, address, and up to 3 http(s) links taken from the source record.
   - The sheet shows the claim, "checked / not yet checked / disputed", what it rests on, "open the source" links (new tab, noopener) and the address.
   - The source notes and checkedBy/checkedOn no longer reach the browser at all, including the page's embedded data and the JSON.
   - Two test ids were added: `trust-claim` and `trust-source`. Feed.tsx was retyped to match.
3. **W-879, withdrawn claims.** `trustCounts` drops withdrawn claims from both numbers, and the sheet no longer lists them. news-comes-from-acquaintances now reads 4/4 and two-said-blue 8/8.

**Files**
- Code: `src/lib/visibility.ts`, `src/lib/trust.ts` (new); `src/lib/catalog.ts`, `src/lib/feed-index.ts`, `src/lib/feed-types.ts`, `src/app/d/[slug]/page.tsx`, `src/app/api/meta/[slug]/route.ts`, `src/components/DemoCard.tsx`, `src/components/Feed.tsx`
- Tests: `tests/platform/visibility.test.mjs`, `tests/platform/trust.test.mjs`, and a `test:platform` script in `package.json` (scripts only, no dependencies)
- Records: `company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-15-r7-drafts-trust-sheet.md` (tier 2, unapproved), changelog entry at the top of `company/ops/changelog.md`

**Test results**
- `npm run check`: passed (960 lessons, 5158 claims, 3 existing warnings about review lessons with disputed claims).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Unit suites: test:platform 13/13 (new), deploy 17/17, lifehacks 64/64, kit 97/97, hq 35/35, spike 5/5.
- QA contract against :3644 with QA_ONLY set to 10 lessons (2 draft, 2 review, 6 published): 28 passed, 2 failed. Both failures were "subject chips filter the feed" (phone and desktop). That is a harness problem, not my change: with QA_ONLY set, the test's list of allowed lessons is cut down to the 10, but the feed still shows every lesson in the subject. Without QA_ONLY, feed.spec passed 10/10.
- Production behaviour: a second dev server with `VERCEL=1 VERCEL_ENV=production` returned 404 for `/d/rome-placed-too-far-east` and `/api/meta/rome-placed-too-far-east`, and 200 tagged "In review" for patience-wins-the-split. On :3644 the draft returned 200, as builders need.
- Checked by eye at 390px: patience-wins-the-split (in review) showed the IN REVIEW tag, a 5/6 line and no notes. news-comes-from-acquaintances (published) showed no tag and 4/4. deleted-is-a-search-state showed working source links.
- Cleanup: both next-server processes stopped by PID (1948, 1955). `.next-r7`, `.next-r7b`, the generated `tsconfig.json` change, AGENTS.md and the `tsc` build-info file are all removed or reverted. The tree is clean.

**What I believe**
- High confidence that the trust sheet and trust line are fixed. A test checks every lesson's learner-safe output for leaks.
- Medium-high confidence that drafts 404 in production. It depends on Vercel setting `VERCEL`/`VERCEL_ENV` at build and at runtime. Vercel documents those variables, but I did not confirm that `vercel build --prod` (deploy.mjs's prebuilt path) sets them.

**Needs the principal engineer**
- **principal-engineer-ops:** approve the readiness record before this ships. It is tier 2 because it touches catalog.ts, `src/app/d/**` and the `/api/meta` response shape. Not a kit-contract change: nothing in `src/kit` changed.
- **principal-engineer:**
  - `/api/meta` claims no longer include `source`/`checkedBy`/`checkedOn`. No tool in the repo reads them; this is a public API shape change.
  - `test:platform` is not part of `npm run verify`. I left verify alone because it is on the deploy path; adding it is your call.

**For other roles (please add to the board)**
- **release-manager:**
  - The deploy.mjs production smoke check tests the alphabetically first unpublished lesson for a 404. That lesson may be a review lesson, which now correctly returns 200, so the check should pick a draft.
  - deploy.mjs still forces `SHOW_REVIEW=off` for production, which contradicts the founder decision.
  - After deploying, check by hand that `/d/rome-placed-too-far-east` returns 404.
- **evaluation-steward:** the QA_ONLY problem in the feed.spec "subject chips" test.
- **fact-checker / builders:** only 72 of 5158 claims have a URL, so most claims now show no openable source. Many claim texts also contain builder notes ("The stage line reads…", "on the QA path"), which is lesson content.

**Next move:** principal-engineer-ops reviews and approves the readiness record. Then release-manager ships r7 with a founder-approved deploy and checks the draft 404.

The founder has decided to create a **sibling company** for their books, starting with *System 3: Towards Fluent Autonomy*. Read the decision first: /home/user/system-3-company/company/decisions/2026-10-15-founder-press-sibling-company.md. You are the org designer for this, because you know how System 3 Company's org-as-data works (tools/org/roles.mjs, people.mjs, generate.mjs). It is not part of System 3 Company: don't add these roles to System 3 Company's roles.mjs.

The book's repo is checked out at /home/user/System3 (GitHub hanialshater/system3, branch ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1; push only there). Read its README.md, resources/editorial/working-spine.md, the existing `.claude/skills/ai-tells` skill, resources/editorial (check-eggs.sh, check-tells.py, easter-egg-register.md) and the list of resources/evaluations, so the roles use the tools and history that already exist.

In /home/user/System3, build:
1. **`press/org/roles.mjs` and `press/org/people.mjs`**, plus a small `press/org/generate.mjs` modelled on System 3 Company's generator. It writes onboarding docs to `press/roles/<id>.md` and subagents to `.claude/agents/<id>.md` in the book repo. The roles:
   - **vp-books** (reports to the founder; owns strategy, execution, vision and the portfolio across all books);
   - **head-of-book-system-3** (reports to vp-books);
   - per-book roles reporting to the head:
     - writer-system-3
     - development-editor-system-3
     - copy-editor-system-3 (proofreading and copy edit)
     - fact-checker-system-3
     - marketing-strategist-system-3
     - experiment-developer-system-3
     - swe-system-3-a and swe-system-3-b (demos and blog publishing)
   - shared roles reporting to vp-books:
     - art-director (visual concepts; book-design/ and resources/art-direction exist)
     - release-manager-press (versions and release tracking for books and blog posts)
     - a **review panel** of consultants: arc, easter eggs (uses the register and check-eggs.sh), narrative momentum, LLM tells (uses the ai-tells skill and check-tells.py), prose quality, fun, thought-provoking ideas, and comparison with other books.

   Each role has a mission, scope, out of scope, authority, inputs, outputs and hard rules. Every role must carry these rules:
   - The founder is the author. Nothing is merged into the manuscript, or published on the blog, without the founder's approval.
   - Chapter 13 is protected, and the README's notes on protected material apply.
   - Author-review comments without recorded acceptance stay.
   - Evaluators read the text before anyone's explanation of it.
   - Objections travel with decisions.
   - Reviewers never edit the manuscript; they write review records.
   - The fact-checker never verifies its own claims.

Feed usable on emulated Pixel 7 at 4x throttle in ≤ 3.0 s (16.7 s now; EDD-001's 2 s stays the engineering target). 0 overflow, 0 targets under 24 px | qa-tester |

## Process dates
- 10-21: W-906 draft goes to the founder (F-19).
- 10-22: deadline for objections and for feasibility answers from the principal engineer, the privacy reviewer and head-of-product.
- **10-23 (Fri founder review): the bar is frozen**, before the build tranche is released.

Rules:

The W-905 budget pack has **no quality line**. Amendment 1 came after it. My org needs about 64 runs, roughly 9.6M tokens. Only the fact-checker and learner-evaluator costs are measured; the rest are proxies, so I'm medium-low confident in the total. **W-906 sequencing:** W-906 goes first, then the freeze (its rows read "per W-906 as ratified"), then AMD-FL-B is written against the ratified text. If W-906 isn't ratified by 10-30, personalization and ads ship switched off under the current Surface Value.

summary: [project:review-publish] FC41 held claims with web: ## Fact-check pass 41: report
body:
## Fact-check pass 41: report

I checked all 93 open non-books claims and set each one's status in its meta.json (checkedBy fact-checker, checkedOn 2026-10-15, with a "FC pass 41" note). **Results: 57 verified, 7 disputed, 29 held as unverified with a note.** Fresh instance: I wrote, built and recorded none of these claims.

**The allow-list only partly works.** Only bare hosts get through. ourworldindata.org, cran.r-project.org and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov open. gapminder.org, census.gov, naturalearthdata.com, rug.nl, sciencedirect.com and econometricsociety.org all 301/302 to their `www.` hosts, which the proxy still blocks (403). doi.org only resolves to publisher hosts, which are blocked. cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (PMC figure images) is also blocked. WebFetch fails DNS for every host. The founder would need to add the `www.` variants, plus www.jstor.org (for Rubinstein) and cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.

### Method
- I read Demo.tsx, model.ts and the lifehacks specs before any builder notes.
- Every derivation and simulation was re-run with my own node or python scripts in the scratchpad (fc41/chk). The kit's mulberry32 is copied verbatim; everything else is re-implemented.
- Other sources opened: Heath's Euclid on Perseus (GitHub raw), OpenStax Chemistry 2e (git clone), PyPI iapws and chemicals, and the Barak TCS text.
- No search snippets and nothing from memory counted as evidence. Where a source is secondary (a PMC review describing an older paper), the note says so.
- No fetched page contained instructions aimed at an AI. I scanned every page; the only hits were package descriptions and research text.

### Counts per domain (verified / disputed / held)
| Domain | Verified | Disputed | Held |
|---|---|---|---|
| ai | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| big-ideas | 11 | 1 | 4 |
| chemistry | 12 | 0 | 0 |
| cs | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| economics | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| geography | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| history | 5 | 2 | 4 |
| life | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| lifehacks | 3 | 4 | 15 |
| math | 5 | 0 | 1 |
| physics | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| probability | 2 | 0 | 0 |

### The specific items you named
- **London Bills (W-873):** c3 and c4 verified (Lancet 2020, PMC7154511; Cureus 2026, PMC13244054; J Med Biogr). c1 is narrowed but still held: no opened source prints the 1665 yearly totals.
- **Rome c8:** still held. Friendly et al. (2010) is unreachable.
- **Gapminder children c6:** held, because Gapminder's documentation is behind the blocked www host. There is a checkable fix from OWID metadata (below).
- **Doubling c3:** still disputed. A new OWID source backs the dispute.
- **OWID:** britain c6, doubling c5 and life-expectancy c5 are now verified.
- **Rubinstein (patience c5):** held. econometricsociety.org and doi.org redirect to blocked hosts.
- **PMC psychology claims:** verified long-cord recall (Raymer & Smith 2007, the 55% is in their Table 1), spaced-beats recall, the Linda problem, Helmholtz, the positive-test strategy and the reaction-time claim.
- **fixes-2 resets (W-874):** all 29 derivation and chemistry re-checks verified.
- **Dunning-Kruger ghost line c6:** held, and c3 with it. The bottom point (about the 60th) matches the sourced 62nd percentile. No opened source gives a number for the top point (about the 75th), and the PMC figure image is on the blocked cdn host.

### Disputes and their fixes
1. **history.doubling-stopped-speeding-up.c3.** The 2023 rate uses the projected 2024 value. Fix (history-builder): use a backward rate (2.25% in 1964, 0.88% in 2023) or label the last value "2022 to 2023: 0.88%". Drop 2024 from POP and align history-cycle2-check.mjs section 15.
2. **history.income-flat-then-sixteenfold.c10.** The title, hook and question credit England with the 1700-2018 rise, but that series is Britain, then the UK. Fix (history-builder): name the entity, e.g. "...From 1700 to 2018 (Britain, then the UK)...".
3. **big-ideas.same-grey-in-shadow.c3.** A "derivation" cannot carry a perception-science cause, and the stage confounds the shadow with local contrast. J Vis 2025 (PMC12517106) supports the dispute. Fix (demo-builder): "Your eyes judged B lighter than the light it sends: the difference came from you, not the screen."
4. **lifehacks.check-confidence-with-output.recall.** Fix (cm-lifehacks, then demo-builder): "This one check is not a forecast of later recall, but it does show which step to fix."
5. **lifehacks.circle-tray-square-corners.c4.** Five discs fit, not four. Fix: ask "how many 10 cm discs fit in this square grid once each is turned 45°?"
6. **lifehacks.circle-tray-square-corners.seen.** Fix: change resultLabel to "Discs in the grid".
7. **lifehacks.cue-needs-a-boundary.seen.** The Match row pins the fixed wrong attempt's 0/3 on the cue. Fix: W-610, or drop the Match row (interaction-designer, then demo-builder).

### Claims still held, and the host each needs
- **history.london c1:** Creighton (1965) or a printed 1665 general Bill. Or reword to "yearly records of deaths ... (Creighton, 1965)".
- **history.rome c8:** datavis.ca or the American Statistician (Friendly et al. 2010). Or use the HistData-based rewording ("five of the twelve were probably read from maps").
- **history.children c6:** www.gapminder.org. Checkable fix now: "...some of its early values are guesses or modelled, not counted" (OWID child-mortality metadata).
- **history.income c9:** Broadberry et al. 2015 (www.rug.nl or CUP). Or drop "from wages, prices and output records".
- **big-ideas.earth-history c6 (Hutton):** a copy of Hutton 1788 or a reliable history. The only opened source, a Nat Commun 2026 editorial, dates Hutton to "the 1830s", which conflicts with the lesson's 1780s. Fallback: the unnamed sentence from the brief.
- **big-ideas.earth-history c9:** an NPS or USGS page for the 1.8 km depth. The roughly 6 million year timing is supported.
- **big-ideas.noise-draws c3 and c6:** Kruger & Dunning 1999 Figures 1-4 (APA), or www.cdn.ncbi. Or set the ghost to the sourced bottom value (62nd) and drop the top point.
- **cs.hailstone c4 and c5:** Springer (Barina 2021/2025) and AMS or arXiv (Lagarias).
- **cs.two-pages c5:** cs.cornell.edu (Easley & Kleinberg). Or reword to "PageRank adds these jumps to fix sinks".
- **economics.everyone-saves c4:** any text that names the paradox of thrift. Or drop the name.
- **economics.patience c5:** www.econometricsociety.org or www.jstor.org. Or use pass 40's derivation fallback (W-877).
- **math.enemy c6:** Project Euclid (Harary 1953) or cs.cornell.edu. Or drop "Harary, 1953".
- **lifehacks, unit-price c5 (×3):** nvlpubs.nist.gov. Or reword to the definition only.
- **lifehacks, "Tariffs and appliance ratings vary" (×7):** an energy regulator host, or an evaluation-steward ruling on whether a safety hedge is a factual claim.
- **lifehacks.lh-scale-recipe c5:** USDA FSIS or UK FSA.
- **lifehacks.mail-exact-phrase and mail-minus-noise recalls:** support.google.com.
- **lifehacks.square-bow c1 and recall:** fieggen.com, for which way the bow sits. Daily-Diamond et al. 2017 (PMC5415684) supports everything else, and there is a checkable reword: "lie flat / twists out of line".

### Files
- meta.json claims under /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/{ai,big-ideas,chemistry,cs,economics,geography,history,life,lifehacks,math,physics,probability}/<slug>/meta.json
- A "## Pass 41" section appended to /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-fact-check.md for all 60 lessons. deleted-column-still-there has an extra c4 addendum.
- Commits, pushed to origin ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1: 9288b7c (batch 1, 61 claims), a1e0547 (batch 2, 19 claims), ca2efa3 (batch 3, 13 claims).
- When `git pull --rebase` and push ran, they also pushed commits other sessions had already made locally on this branch, including a7b3c34. I staged only my own files. I did not touch board.json or progress.md. No [deploy].
- `npm run check` passes, with 3 expected warnings: the in-review lifehacks lessons that carry disputes.

### What I believe, and how sure I am
- **High:** every derivation and simulation verdict, because I re-ran each one independently.
- **High:** the OWID, PMC and Perseus verdicts. Each rests on quoted text from a page I opened.
- **Medium:** sudden-skill c3. The review says "evaluation granularity", not "exact match vs per-token".
- **Medium:** duck c5. The reveal would be more exact as "surface water", because of the undertow.
- Several verdicts rest on secondary sources, and each note says which.

### Next moves (I did not add board items, since that edits board.json)
- **history-builder:** the doubling c3 and income c10 disputes, plus the checkable rewordings for children c6, income c9 and rome c8.
- **demo-builder / cm-big-ideas:** the same-grey c3 rewording, the Dunning-Kruger ghost fix, and the earth-history c6/c9 wording.
- **cm-lifehacks, then demo-builder:** the 4 lifehacks disputes and the square-bow and unit-price rewordings.
- **evaluation-steward:** rule on the 7 tariff safety hedges.
- **Founder:** add the www. variants (www.econometricsociety.org, www.gapminder.org, www.rug.nl, www.sciencedirect.com, www.census.gov, www.naturalearthdata.com), plus www.jstor.org and cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, if more held claims should open.
- **A fact-checker who is not the builder:** re-checks every claim the builders change.

summary: [project:review-publish] Readiness review r7: **Verdict: approved with conditions.** I recorded it in /home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/readi…
body:
**Verdict: approved with conditions.** I recorded it in /home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-15-r7-drafts-trust-sheet.md: header lines `approved-by: principal-engineer-ops` and `approved: 2026-10-15`, plus the approval section. Commit cef5165 is pushed to ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. That is the only file I committed. No [deploy], and board.json and progress.md are untouched. `npm run check` passes.

The change makes nothing worse than production today and removes most of the leak. But it does not fully fix W-878 or W-884, so neither should be closed on this release.

**What I measured** (`test:platform` 13/13 pass; one production build with `VERCEL=1 VERCEL_ENV=production`, served with `next start`; build dir deleted afterwards):
- **Drafts at build:** none are prerendered. 879 `/d/*` and 879 `/api/meta/*` pages are built (960 lessons minus 81 drafts). `/api/meta/<draft>` returns 404 whatever the runtime environment.
- **Drafts at runtime, the main failure mode:** with VERCEL and VERCEL_ENV unset at runtime, `/d/rome-placed-too-far-east` returns **200 with the full draft page**.
  - Cause: `src/app/d/[slug]/page.tsx` has no `export const dynamicParams = false`, so unknown slugs render on demand and `findDemo` reads the env at request time.
  - The 200 is then cached for the life of the deployment (`x-nextjs-cache: HIT`, `s-maxage=31536000`).
  - With the vars set at runtime and a fresh cache, it returns 404. Hiding on `/d/` is decided by the runtime env, not the build.
- **Prebuilt path:** I read the pinned vercel@63.1.2 CLI source, because Vercel docs were blocked by the proxy and the Vercel MCP tool was not available to me. `vercel build` sets `VERCEL="1"` itself but never sets VERCEL_ENV; that comes only from the file `vercel pull` writes. So build-time hiding still holds through the `VERCEL !== "1"` fallback, and deploy.mjs also forces `SHOW_REVIEW=off` on production.
  - Production actually ships through the Git `[deploy]` integration, which runs no smoke check at all.
- **What is clean:** claim sources, `checkedBy` and withdrawn claims are gone from the prerendered HTML, RSC payloads and `/api/meta`. The only hits are the source URLs the sheet is meant to show. `/api/meta` claims are exactly `{id,text,support,status,links}`.
- **Residual leak 1, the client bundle (existed before r7):** a 5.3 MB client chunk, loaded by the feed and every lesson page, contains all 960 meta.json files. That includes drafts, about 4,560 claim source records, `checkedBy`, the per-claim fact-check `note` field and withdrawn claims.
  - Cause: `DemoHost.tsx` imports `loaders` from `registry.generated.ts`, which also imports every meta.json.
  - So the record's line "notes never reach the browser" is false.
- **Residual leak 2, the spread:** `publicMeta` uses `...meta`, so `curriculum.references[].note` gets through (e.g. "Fact-checker to confirm numbering." on `/d/earliest-finish-wins`), along with `owner` and `evidence` paths.
- **Other surfaces:** every HQ page and route checks `hqEnabled()`, `/spike` checks `spikeEnabled()`, and `/api/feed` and `/catalog` carry only the slim index.
- **Public API shape:** no in-repo consumer reads the removed fields. A tab left open across the deploy degrades harmlessly.
- **Rollback does not fix a draft leak:** the previous production deployment also serves drafts. The remedy is a roll-forward, which needs the founder's approval.

**Conditions for the release manager at deploy:**
- **C1 (W-926):** the founder approves this specific deploy. Record which path shipped it (Git `[deploy]` or deploy.mjs) and the production SHOW_REVIEW value. The founder decision wants it on; deploy.mjs forces it off.
- **C2 (W-926):** within 15 minutes of promotion, before any announcement, on the production domain, and as the first requests to these slugs (a 200 gets cached):
  - `/d/` and `/api/meta/` for rome-placed-too-far-east, deleted-column-still-there and gradient-fades-with-depth all return 404.
  - `/d/asthma-looks-safe` (review) matches the SHOW_REVIEW value from C1.
  - `/api/meta/news-comes-from-acquaintances` has 4 claims and none has a `source` or `checkedBy` key. Trust lines read 4/4, and 8/8 for two-said-blue.
  - Status codes go in the release record.
- **C3:** if any draft returns 200, it is a SEV2. Do not roll back. Roll forward with the founder's approval: either land `dynamicParams = false` and redeploy, or set SHOW_REVIEW=off and redeploy. A COE is required.
- **C4 (W-925):** releases.json known_issues states that notes are still in the client bundle and in curriculum notes. W-878 and W-884 stay open.

**What I believe, and how sure I am:**
- The runtime-env dependency and the bundle leak are measured, so I am highly confident in both.
- Whether Vercel's production runtime actually has VERCEL_ENV is not measured here. C2 measures it on production.

**Next moves.** These need new board items, which the chief of staff should add because I was told not to edit board.json:
- **F1, platform-engineer, P1, before the next release:** `dynamicParams = false` on `/d/[slug]`, plus a test over the built output. This closes the drafts half of W-884.
- **F2, platform-engineer with principal-engineer, P1:** emit `loaders` in a module that imports no meta.json. The generator is in protected `tools/company.mjs`, so this needs an amendment or a generator outside protected paths. Related to W-607, and it closes W-878.
- **F3, platform-engineer, P2:** make `publicMeta` an allow-list, and test the built RSC and `/api/meta` output.
- **F4, principal-engineer, P2:**
  - Add `src/lib/visibility.ts` and `src/lib/trust.ts` to paths.json as tier 2. The visibility rule moved out of tier-2 catalog.ts into files that default to tier 1.
  - Change this record's `paths:` entries: in a glob, `[slug]` is a character class and will not match the real files. Use `src/app/d/**` and `src/app/api/meta/**`.
- **F5, mine, P2:** a production draft-404 meter in `tools/ops-health.mjs`.
- **Risks:** I refused the proposed R-005 rescore. The R-003 drafts half waits for C2 and F1.

Deploying needs the release manager and the founder's approval.

Both fixes are done and committed on r7-fix2 as fd63b1c (not pushed, no [deploy]). They still go back to principal-engineer-ops for re-review before release: the original approval covered commit 1b7ac14 only. The 5.3 MB client chunk still leaks every meta.json (W-946, out of scope).

**What changed**
- **W-945:** added `export const dynamicParams = false` to `src/app/d/[slug]/page.tsx`. `/api/meta/[slug]` already had `dynamicParams = false` and `force-static`, so it needed nothing. A slug the build didn't list is now a plain 404, never rendered on demand and cached as 200. The plain form works in dev: `next dev` calls `generateStaticParams` on each navigation (the bundled Next docs say so) with the dev server's env, which has no VERCEL vars, so builders still get drafts.
- **W-947:** `publicMeta` in `src/lib/trust.ts` is now built field by field: `slug, title, domain, status, recall{question,options,answer,why}, claims` (claims unchanged) and `evidence{qa,simulatedLearner,humanLearners}` as counts. Owner, the learner brief fields, curriculum (including `references[].note`), keyState, interactions and evidence file paths stay on the server, and so will any field added later. `DemoCard.tsx` now renders the counts.
- **API shape change:** `/api/meta` loses those fields and `evidence.*` become numbers. A tab left open across the deploy shows empty counts but doesn't break. Nothing in `src/`, `tools/` or `tests/` reads the dropped fields. This should go in the release's `added.fixes` (W-925).
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/platform/built-output.test.mjs` (new) runs when `BUILT_DIST_DIR` points at a production build and skips otherwise. It checks that no draft is in the prerender manifest or the prerendered files, and greps every served `.html`, `.rsc` and `.body` file for the internal strings (static chunks are excluded). It then starts `next start` itself with VERCEL, VERCEL_ENV, SHOW_DRAFTS and SHOW_REVIEW removed from its env, and expects all 81 drafts on both routes to return 404 twice.
  - The internal-string list lives in `tests/platform/internal-strings.mjs` (new).

**Results**
- **Runtime-env-unset draft check:** I ran `next start -p 3655` on the production build and confirmed via `/proc/<pid>/environ` that no VERCEL or SHOW_* vars were set.
  - `/d/` and `/api/meta/` for rome-placed-too-far-east, deleted-column-still-there and gradient-fades-with-depth all returned 404 on first and repeat requests.

- **Production build:** took 4m57s. No draft in the prerender manifest. The grep of served files found 0 hits. As a check that the grep finds real strings, the same strings do turn up in the client chunk.
- **`/api/meta/news-comes-from-acquaintances`:** returns only the 7 allowed keys and 4 claims, each `{id,links,status,support,text}`. `/d/earliest-finish-wins` no longer contains "Fact-checker to confirm".
- **Dev server (:3654):** draft `/d/rome-placed-too-far-east` returns 200 ("Twelve guesses at Rome"). Its `/api/meta` returns 200 in the new shape. An unknown slug returns 404 on both.
- **Test runs:**
  - test:platform: 19/19 with the build; 16 pass and 3 skip without it.
  - `npm run check`: passed (960 lessons, 3 warnings that were already there).
  - `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
  - test:hq: 53/53.
- **QA contract, 10-lesson sample against :3654** (3 drafts, 1 review, 6 published, 7 domains): 28/30. The 2 failures are "subject chips filter the feed" on phone and desktop. The sample filter causes them: the test only allows the 10 sampled slugs, but the feed shows the whole domain. The full feed spec without the filter passed 10/10, including the trust-sheet and revisit tests.
- **Cleanup:**
  - Every server is stopped by PID. `next start` forks a `next-server` child that outlived its parent once (PID 10942), so I stopped it and made the test kill the whole process group.

body:
Fact-check pass 42 (W-950) is finished. I re-checked all 21 unverified claims in the 15 lessons: 19 verified, 1 disputed, 1 still held. Commit 0b86230 is pushed to ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1 and contains only my 30 files (15 meta.json, 15 review records). `npm run check` passes; its one warning is cue-needs-a-boundary, which is not mine. I did not touch board.json or progress.md, and there is no [deploy].

I wrote, built and recorded none of these claims, nor the 2026-10-15 rewording. For each lesson I read the learner-facing text before any builder note: Demo.tsx, plus home-lessons.ts, studyCatalog.ts, resource-specs.json and the meta.json recall card for the Life Hacks ones. I re-ran every number with my own scripts:
- the noise simulation, with mulberry32 re-implemented and checked against src/kit/random.ts
- the friend/enemy enumeration for 3 to 7 people
- the circle-grid counts, clock seconds, unit prices, savings model and breath count

I opened every source myself with curl. WebFetch fails DNS. Some PMC pages returned a reCAPTCHA page and I did not use those.

**Disputed (blocks publishing):**
- screening-survival-clock `recall`: the "why" says "deaths in randomly assigned groups do not depend on when diagnosis happened." That is false as written. If the earlier scan lets treatment work, deaths do depend on it, and that is what the trial is meant to detect. What is true is that death rates are not counted from the diagnosis date, so lead time alone cannot inflate them. "Rises whenever" also overstates it. Suggested fix: "Survival counted from diagnosis rises when diagnosis moves earlier, even if no death moves. Death rates in randomly assigned groups are not counted from diagnosis, so only a real change in deaths moves them." The keyed option itself is right.

**Held (unverified, with note):**
- earth-history-in-a-day `c9`: the depth is now sourced. PMC12130896 says Hells Canyon is about 2,400 m deep and "600 m deeper than the Grand Canyon", so about 1.8 km. The river cutting through the canyon 6–5 Ma ago is sourced too (PMC13498593). But the opened papers say older paleocanyons were cut across the Kaibab uplift before 15 Ma and later joined up (PMC13498593, PMC9343645), and PNAS 2025 calls the age "controversial". So "carved the Grand Canyon's 1.8 km in the last two minutes" and the 0.3 mm/yr rate are not supported. Fix: drop the rate and the claim that the whole depth is that young, or open Karlstrom et al. 2014.

The 19 verified claims, with the basis for the ones that might be questioned:
- circle-tray c4 and seen: the question now says "in this square grid" and the row label is "Discs in the grid". The grid counts are right at every side from 22 to 34 cm.
- check-confidence recall: the second sentence is now limited to this one check, consistent with the already-verified c2.
- same-grey c3: the cause is gone. What is left follows from the two squares being the same grey, plus the "unconscious inference" framing of c4.
- noise-DK c3 and c6: seed 42 gives 63.3. Across seeds 42 to 141 the value runs 60 to 68, so "near the 62nd" holds for any run. The 62nd comes from PMC3586194, a secondary source; I did not open the 1999 paper.
- earth-history c6.
- two-pages c5: the Page et al. paper (papers-we-love PDF) says "To overcome this problem of rank sinks, we introduce a rank source".
- everyone-saves c4.
- enemy-of-my-enemy c6: my enumeration plus the theorem name in PMC11068007.
- square-bow c1 and recall: PMC5415684 says the strong knot's second trefoil has the opposite handedness, and the granny "twist[s] instead of laying flat".
- the three unit-price c5 claims (lh-align-price-units, lh-big-pack-price, lh-count-sheets-not-rolls): definition only, and consistent with each stage.
- ethanol c2 and c3: CRC data in PyPI chemicals 1.5.2 gives 78.24 °C and −24.80 °C; OpenStax m68761 covers the hydrogen-bond rule.
- find-the-co2 c2 and c4: the NOAA 2025 global mean is 425.62 ppm; the breath count is 5.23e18; the OpenStax tidal volume is "about 500 milliliters".

How sure I am: high on the arithmetic and on the opened quotes. The noise-DK figure rests on a secondary source. The screening dispute is about wording, not facts; I am confident the clause as written says something false.

Routed, not a claim in this lesson: the /catalog map still names the everyone-saves concept "Paradox of thrift" (content/curriculum/economics.json, owner cm-economics), and that name still has no opened source.

Next moves:
- demo-builder: apply the screening-survival-clock recall "why" fix, and reword the earth-history-in-a-day c9 stage label and reveal. A fresh fact-checker then re-checks both.

summary: [project:history] FC43 History v2 re-check: ## Fact-check pass 43 (W-954): History round-1 v2
body:
## Fact-check pass 43 (W-954): History round-1 v2

I re-checked all 10 claims that commit c255d8e reset to unverified, plus income c8 and london c4, which you also asked about. That is 12 checks: **11 verified, 1 disputed, 0 held.** I'm a fresh instance and wrote or built none of these claims. I read each lesson's stage text (Demo.tsx and its v2 diff) before any builder note. Every number was re-derived with my own node scripts on artifacts/history-data, and all SHA-256 pins match.

**14 of the 15 History lessons now have every claim verified.** The only open claim is london-buried-six-times-more c4.

### The dispute
- **london-buried-six-times-more c4 (disputed):** the reveal still says "these are recorded burials", but v2 relabelled every number on the stage and in the reveal as deaths. It also dropped the Bills of Mortality, because no opened source ties these columns to the Bills. "Burials" is that same unsourced link, and it contradicts the stage. FC41's PMC sources for c4 describe what the Bills recorded, so they only apply if the file is the Bills. Search results list pages that print the 1665 bill as 97,306 buried and 68,596 of plague (worc.ox.ac.uk, britannica print 243560, pcwww.liv.ac.uk), but none opened from this host. Two possible fixes:
  - (a) A web-capable session (W-583) opens one of those pages. The lesson can then name the Bills again and keep FC41's sources.
  - (b) Cut the sentence to "Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from one later compilation (Creighton)."

### Langren Map count: resolved at 2
- The pinned Langren1644.csv has Map in 2 rows (Jansonius 1605, Mercator 1567) and Astron in 10. I re-fetched it from Rdatasets and it is byte-identical to the pin.
- The CRAN original agrees: `HistData_1.1.1.tar.gz` → `data/Langren1644.RData`, read with python `rdata`, also gives 2 Map and 10 Astron.
- The HistData doc gives only the two levels, with no counts.
- The "5" in passes 39 and 41 matches the Gap column (0 in 5 rows, 1 in 7), not the Source column, so it looks like a column mix-up.
- So rome c8 ("2 of the 12") and the new hook claim c9 are verified. I added a correction note to rome c1, whose pass-39 note still said "Astron 7 / Map 5"; its status is unchanged.

### Verified, with non-blocking advisories
- **doubling c3:** 2.24503% → 2.25 in 1963; 0.8768% → 0.88 for 2022 to 2023. Demo.tsx holds the file's 224 values for 1800–2023 with no 2024 value. Gapminder's pop data is version 8 (29 July 2024), so 2023 is the last estimate year. The 2021–22 rate was 0.84%, so the last rate is slightly up; that doesn't change the claim.
- **doubling c4:** "About as fast" is right. By interpolation the two doublings took 47.5 and 47.6 years, so "faster" would not be.
- **income c8:** the claim is still true, but its address is stale. "Income per person in England" is now in the hook; the question says "England's income per person". The builder should fix the claim text.
- **income c9 and c10:** The Maddison README marks only 1252–1700 as "(England)". For 1700–1870 it cites Broadberry et al., *British Economic Growth*, with no territory label. So "Britain, then the UK" rests on "British" plus the series name "United Kingdom". The learner text is true either way. history-data.mjs claims the README says "Britain 1700-1870", which it does not; that is cm-history's file to fix.
- **children c6:** Supported by OWID's child-mortality metadata, which says Gapminder rows labelled "Guesstimate" and "Model based on Life Expectancy" are removed. That metadata describes Gapminder's country data; applying it to the world figure is my inference, and the note says so.
- **cholera c4:** Battersea districts r = −0.680 (n = 12), Spearman −0.71, and negative whichever district is left out (−0.55 to −0.80).
- **london c1:** the numbers match both the pinned file and the CRAN data. The doc's reference is "Creighton (1965), 2nd edition", so 1965 is an edition date. "Compiled by Creighton, 1965" can read as if he compiled the figures in 1965; I suggest "(Creighton; 1965 edition)".
- **london c2:** ×6.3, 70%, 9.8 → 10, and 45% for 1636 all re-derive.

### Confidence
- High on every number and on the Langren count.
- Medium-high on income c10 and children c6, which rest on documentation that doesn't name the territory or the world figure directly.
- High that london c4 contradicts its own stage.

### Files and commit
- Six meta.json files under /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/history/: children-dying-before-five, cholera-fell-with-height, doubling-stopped-speeding-up, income-flat-then-sixteenfold, london-buried-six-times-more, rome-placed-too-far-east. Each changed claim has status, checkedBy, checkedOn 2026-10-15 and a "FC pass 43" note.
- A "## Pass 43" section appended to /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-fact-check.md for the same six slugs. The other 9 lessons had no unverified claims, so they have no Pass 43 entry.
- Commit 9c0b76e is pushed to origin ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. It contains only those 12 files; I left the other worker's uncommitted edits to history-cycle2-check.mjs and history.md alone. Its subject line wrongly says "12 verified"; the right count is 11 verified and 1 disputed of 12 checked. The review records are correct, and I did not force-push to fix the message.
- `npm run check` passes. I did not touch board.json or progress.md, and nothing was deployed.
- My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3e472d64-8589-5167-8584-c47a01ab4321/scratchpad/fc43/scripts/ (check.mjs, cholera.mjs, apply.mjs, records.mjs).

### Next moves
1. **Builder (demo-builder or the History builder):** fix london c4 with option (b), or wait for (a) via W-583. Then a fact-checker who is not the builder re-checks it. Optional at the same time: re-address income c8's claim text and soften "compiled by Creighton, 1965".
2. **cm-history:** correct "Britain 1700-1870 … per the README" in history-data.mjs, and finish W-869 (the check script still computes gr(2023)).

W-896 is done. I wrote the DLR proposal and pushed it: commit f2f94e1 on ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1, with only that one file. The pull --rebase --autostash was a no-op. I did not touch board.json or progress.md, and there is no [deploy]. I created no role, DomainId, curriculum or HQ room.

File: /home/user/system-3-company/company/domains/proposals/2026-10-15-behavioral-economics-dlr.md

**Recommendation: incubate, with a pilot of 5.** head-of-product decides, not me.
- **Why not enter:** there is no demand evidence, no replication verdict has been sourced, the fact-checker has not agreed, and the four neighbour sign-offs do not exist.
- **Why not wait:** the founder decided the category, and lessons 1-3 need no outside source.
- **A ruling is needed:** the template's "incubate = at most 2 lessons" does not fit a pilot of 5. The proposal asks head-of-product to rule on this.

**12 draft concepts**, none sharing an id with economics, probability, books or big-ideas. Demand is my own estimate on a 1-3 scale, not measured.
1. `allais-certainty-effect` (demand 3)
2. `reflection-effect` (2)
3. `probability-weighting` (2)
4. `gain-loss-framing` (3)
5. `endowment-effect` (3)
6. `present-bias-reversal` (3)
7. `commitment-devices` (2)
8. `mental-accounting` (2)
9. `dictator-giving` (2)
10. `beauty-contest-level-k` (3)
11. `interval-overconfidence` (2)
12. `money-illusion` (2)

There are also about 6 uncounted reserves. Of the 12 concepts, 5 are close calls: #7, #8, #9, #10 and #12. The proposal has a near-collision table saying who keeps what.
- **Books:** keeps loss aversion. #5 endowment is Selin's proposed exception and needs cm-books' sign-off.
- **Economics:** keeps `iterated-dominance` and `nash-equilibrium` (markets), and the money-illusion arithmetic.
- **Neighbours outside the four:** `math:transitive-preferences` and `ai:calibration` are also near. I flagged them for cm-math and cm-ai.

**Three candidate lessons** (concept → misconception → interaction)
1. **`allais-certainty-effect`**
   - Concept: no utility function fits both of your choices.
   - Misconception: "my choices are just tastes, so they can't be inconsistent."
   - Interaction: the learner picks in two pairs, and a utility-ratio slider never fits "A with D" or "B with C". The inequality is 0.11u(1M) > 0.10u(5M) in both pairs.
2. **`present-bias-reversal`**
   - Concept: a constant discounter's two choices must match.
   - Misconception: "a one-week wait costs the same whenever it happens."
   - Interaction: $100 now versus $110 in a week, and the same pair 52 weeks out, with the dates slid. Taking the money today but waiting at 52 weeks is a reversal.
3. **`beauty-contest-level-k`**
   - Concept: the best guess depends on how many steps ahead the others think.
   - Misconception: "the rational answer is 0, so I should guess 0."
   - Interaction: a learner guess, a ladder 66.7, 44.4, down to 0, and a labelled seeded simulation of a crowd.

  - Effects with known limits carry those limits in the same reveal.
  - Contested effects are taught as contested, never as a predict answer.
  - Failed effects (priming, ego depletion, power posing) are never taught as claims; Big Ideas has first refusal on any failure lesson.

## W-906: the Surface Value amendment (draft)
**File:** /home/user/system-3-company/company/constitution/amendments/AMD-008-first-light-surface-value.md. It follows the amendment template, and I added a row to /home/user/system-3-company/company/constitution/amendments/README.md. It is numbered 008 because 003, 004 and 007 are reserved and 005 and 006 are drafted. The chief of staff may renumber it.

There are 30 rules, each with a test that can fail, so AMD-FL-B can turn each one into a spec. The founder can ratify each part separately, and part A only takes effect if F-17 is decided (a).
- **F1–F4 (feed):** the default is still round-robin, published first, and every learner with no history, or with personalization off, sees it. Due revisits always come first. Nothing autoplays. At cold start the feed still says it is not "for you". With history, it names the rules that are on and gives the control to turn them off.
- **P1–P5 (personalization):**
  - P1: it reorders only by a published, deterministic rule list; a learned model would need a further amendment.
  - P2: rules may read only the learner's completions, predictions, recall results, due revisits, choices they state, and the prerequisite graph. They may never read engagement, ad data, demographics, device, or location finer than country.
  - P3: every moved card shows a true reason that names the rule that fired.
  - P4: one switch turns it off, and it never needs an account.
  - P5: each rule needs a registered experiment against a default-order holdout, on recall and completion.
- **M1–M8 (mastery):**
  - M1: mastery comes only from reveal reached, prediction made and spaced-revisit recall. The default states are seen, recalled, and held (right on 2 revisits at least 7 days apart).
  - M2: no streaks, meaning no count of consecutive days, sessions or lessons anywhere.
  - M3: a state goes down only when a recall is answered wrong, never because time passed. Nothing counts down.
  - M4: a fixed list of banned phrases ("streak", "in a row", "don't lose", "we miss you", "last chance" and others). The list can grow but never shrink.
  - M5: no leaderboards and no scoring for speed or volume.
  - M6: every challenge keeps predict-before-reveal and has no timer.
  - M7: mastery messages are verified claims that say only what was measured.
  - M8: reminders are opt-in, only about due revisits, at most one a day.
- **A1–A10 (ad slot):**
  - A1: never inside a lesson.
  - A2: only between lessons, after one; never between a prediction and its reveal, never inside a sequence.
  - A3: a separate card labelled "Ad", which can't imitate a lesson and can be swiped past at once.
  - A4: never the first card of a session, never next to a due revisit.
  - A5: static, text and one image.
  - A6: at most 1 ad per 6 lessons and none on lesson pages. An experiment may lower that; raising it needs an amendment.
  - A7: chosen only by the subject of the previous lesson. No learner data, and no personalised ads while children may be present.
  - A8: lesson order is identical with ads on and off. Sponsored lessons are not allowed until W-895 rules on them.
  - A9: served from our own origin only, with no third-party script and no ad cookies.
  - A10: a kill switch, and a guardrail breach beats revenue.
- **X1–X3 (all three surfaces):**
  - X1: engagement and revenue are reported, each labelled, and never rank lessons, drive a personalization rule or give mastery credit.
  - X2: all surface copy is a verified claim.
  - X3: every rule is reviewed for removal at the first distillation after 30 days of real-learner data.
- **Trade-offs table:** the cold-start row stays with head-of-product, and there are three new rows.

**Objections, each answered in the draft:**
- **Head-of-product (on record):** their 2026-10-12 view, "Personalisation language without signal is a lie with good typography", plus their acceptance of prerequisite-aware ordering. Both are written in through F4, P3 and P2.
- **Head-of-product (not on record):** they haven't ruled on W-891 (the slot numbers and label), and I found no record of their view on mastery. The draft says this is open; it does not assume their answer.
- **Growth-designer:** their scope lists "Recall-based streaks". M2 rules that out.
- **vp-marketing:** wanted the ad frequency "set by the experiment". Partly accepted: an experiment may lower it, not raise it.
- **Personalization team:** the founder's brief (W-091) is still pending.
- **Privacy reviewer:** the draft sets a floor and their ruling wins if it is stricter.
- **My own:** the risk of freezing the product.
- **Schedule:** ratification is on the AMD-FL-B timeline.

I wrote these rules and will judge against them, so I can't be the deciding approver. The founder ratifies.

## W-843: verdict wording ruling
**Ruling: normalise the reviews. The parser learns no synonyms.** Turning "pass" into launch, or "block" into revise or fatal, is a judgement call, and the tool must not make it silently. The only accepted words are `Verdict: launch|revise|fatal` on a line starting with "Verdict:", plus exactly one `lesson version: vN` line.

I also made the parser stricter (tools/publish-ready.mjs):
- It reads only verdict and version lines that start a line.
- A word like "pass" or "block" holds the lesson, and the hold reason names the word.
- Two different verdicts or two different version stamps in one file hold the lesson.
- **New:** an unreadable review dated after the one chosen holds the lesson. Before, a newer unstamped review was silently outranked by an older stamped one.

On today's tree the candidate list is unchanged. I diffed it against the old parser on a scratch copy, and both read all 1,475 learner reviews identically.

The 27 "pass" files and the 1 "block" file are all r10 reviews of lessons that are still drafts, so nothing is wrongly held today. They would hold once those lessons move to review.

## W-897: decision recorded (Head of Product)

I decided to incubate the category with the pilot of 5, and I'm recommending to the founder (F-22) that the slot line be 18, not 40. The decision record and an F-22 note are committed as e9ece60 and pushed to `ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1`. `npm run check` passed. **The decision**
1. **Incubate**, status `incubating`.
   - **Ruling on "≤ 2" against the pilot of 5:** a category the founder has decided, entering by the playbook, may incubate up to 5 lessons, and those 5 are the DLR five. No sixth lesson is briefed before the DLR meets again. The "≤ 2" line still applies to domains the scout proposes. The reasons are precedent (Books, Big Ideas and History all incubate to 5) and that 2 lessons cannot test the three boundary collisions.
   - **Order:** lessons 1-3 can be briefed once the gates hold. Lesson 4 waits for cm-books (fallback `reflection-effect`) and lesson 5 waits for cm-economics. The DLR's stop rules are adopted as written, including "fold if fewer than 12 clean concepts remain after sign-off".
2. **Slot line: 18 counted, all new lessons, as a ceiling.**
   - Tranche 1 is 5, taken at the next wave whose W-556 gate opens.
   - Tranche 2 is up to 13, from Wave N at the earliest. It needs the DLR five passed, a held-claim rate of 25% or lower, a Project Review, learner data at or above the feed median, and a signed boundary row for every concept briefed.
   - Nothing past 18 is funded. A bigger target comes back to the founder as a new item, and only if a scout pass of fields not yet scouted (bargaining, behavioural finance, savings and health) finds signed clean concepts.
   - The 40 doesn't hold because 5 of its 40 were Economics lessons re-tagged under the strand plan. Under a category nothing moves from a neighbour, so all 40 would have to be new, against 16-18 clean concepts.
3. **Boundaries.**
   - The rule: two lessons collide if a learner would give the same wrong predict answer for the same reason in both. The neighbour that already has the concept keeps it, and nothing is re-tagged.
   - **Economics** keeps its whole map. Its charter is not amended, because the replication rule goes in this category's charter. Close calls: #10 (the ladder only as a linked prerequisite), #8, #9, #12 (dropped first) and #7.
   - **Probability** keeps every judgement-error concept and the maths. #11 enters only if cm-probability agrees.
   - **Books** keeps everything in `books.json`. #4 framing needs cm-books' sign-off. **The endowment exception is PENDING cm-books' sign-off.** It is not in the pilot, and if refused the ceiling drops to 17.
   - **Big Ideas** keeps everything it has ranked and has first refusal on failure lessons. Nudges at scale stays a reserve until cm-big-ideas signs.
4. **Step 9 checkability: yes, required before any brief.** It gets obtained in this order:
   - The CM drafts the charter's checking section.
   - research-lead's W-902 starts with a PMC lookup of every source behind a type (d) line.
   - The fact-checker, shown only the charter section and the note, writes a dated statement for each claim type.
   - If it agrees to (a), (b) and (c) but not yet (d), lessons 1-3 may be briefed with every (d) line held and left out of the published lesson.
5. **The playbook is accepted** as the order of work. Steps 4, 5 and 7 can now run in parallel.

**F-22 recommendation (the founder's call):** option (c).
- 18 slots, pilot 5 plus up to 13 conditional, from the N-Q pool (~608 to ~590).
- cs −8, geography −5, life −5. Economics stays at 165, and Big Ideas' conditional tranche is not cut.
- The total stays 2,000, there is no W-556 exemption, and nothing in K-M moves.
- Tranche 1 stays at 1.83M. Tranche 2 is about 1.59M instead of 4.03M. That is about 190k per lesson, against the measured 122k, because the set-up cost doesn't shrink with the target. The record says this plainly.

**How sure I am:** I'm confident that 40 can't be reached from clean ground and that incubating with 5 is right. I'm moderately sure about 18: it is a ceiling, and the sign-offs may cut it to about 12. My choice of which categories pay is a judgement, and the founder may choose other cuts.

- **chief-of-staff-ceo-office:** W-899, create one CM. My recommendation is no strand managers at this size.

### What changed
1. **W-941 A1 (usage dedupe)**
   - New `tools/lib/usage.mjs` keeps one record per run: the agent label, within a 12-hour window. It keeps the record with the most tokens rather than the last one, because token counts aren't always rising. For example, c521 logged 97,794 tokens and then 13,743.
   - I checked the records before choosing the key. Every repeated label has exactly one dispatch, and the repeats are at most 30 minutes apart.

   - The log and the ledger are not rewritten.
2. **W-941 A5 (stopped events)**
   - New backfill options: `node tools/events.mjs backfill --types=stopped --since=<ISO> [--dry]`.
   - **Result: 0 stopped events after 2026-10-14 15:20, so nothing was added.**
   - The transcript has no agent notification after the cut-off with status failed or killed. The 76 failed or killed notifications after it are all background shells (ids starting with `b`). Every agent id in a notification maps to a known dispatch.
   - So WBR hypothesis (a) is wrong: the backfill already handled failed and killed runs. This answer is fairly certain for this one transcript file.
   - Two runs dispatched after the cut-off have no finish record yet: `FC41 held claims with web ·71fe` and `r7 fixes ·c9a1`. They may still be running.
   - One file read quoted at 18:17 says "All 6 agents are stopped until about 22:10". That is quoted text, and no harness stop notice backs it, so I didn't turn it into an event.
3. **W-851 (port crosstalk)**

   - **The app is not the cause.** It posts `/api/events` to its own origin, so the stray POSTs came from pages loaded from the wrong server. No change to the app.
   - **Fixes:**
     - New `tools/lib/server.mjs`.
     - `walkthrough` takes `--url` (or `WALKTHROUGH_URL`), or `--port N`, or uses a port the OS assigns. It refuses a taken port and fails loudly if its server exits.
     - `a11y-scan` now requires `--base`; it used to default to :3420.
     - `serve.sh start` refuses a port another process holds and reports a server that exited.
     - QA reuses an existing server only with `QA_REUSE_SERVER=1` (the tier-2 commit).
     - `reveal-fit` and `sequence-probe` already required `--url`.

Fact-check pass 44 (W-963) is done. The screening recall is verified. The earth-history c9 claim is disputed. Pushed to origin ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1 as commit 6b01c6e.

**Verdicts**

1. **life.screening-survival-clock.recall: verified (it is a derivation, so no web sources were needed).**
   - The why matches Pass 42's suggested wording word for word.
   - The keyed option ("Compare death rates in randomly assigned scanned and unscanned groups") is right, and both distractors are wrong.
   - First sentence of the why: moving diagnosis earlier by L, with the death date fixed, adds L to every survival time. I re-ran the count in node: 6 of 14 rises to 12 of 14 at a 3-year lead, matching c1.
   - Second sentence: a group's death rate is counted from when people were assigned to groups, never from diagnosis. So lead time cannot move it, and the sentence no longer implies a trial could never show a benefit.
   - Independence: the words came from the fact-checker role (Pass 42), though not from me. My check is independent only at the instance level. I recorded this and suggested cm-life read the why as a second reader at launch-review.
   - Every recorded claim in this lesson (c1-c4 and recall) is now verified.
   - Confidence: high.

2. **big-ideas.earth-history-in-a-day.c9: disputed.**
   - **Sources:** I opened all three myself. The PMC article pages returned a reCAPTCHA, so I got the full text from PMC's OAI service. They support what the claim cites:
     - PMC13498593: "river integration through the Grand Canyon 6–5 Ma".
     - PMC12130896: Hells Canyon is "~2,400 m deep" and "600 m deeper than the Grand Canyon", so the Grand Canyon is about 1.8 km. The paper also calls the canyon "controversial".
     - PMC9343645: the modern river "would connect several old pre-existing segments of the Grand Canyon".
   - **Stage:** 6 Ma is 23:58:05 and 5 Ma is 23:58:24.8, so the stage dot and the list line "Colorado River through Grand Canyon" are fine.
   - **Your question:** yes, the reveal can be read as saying the whole depth was cut then. It reads "even a process too slow to see can do large things: at 23:58, 6–5 million years ago, the Colorado River cut through the Grand Canyon, about 1.8 km deep." The colon presents the river as the "large thing", so the natural reading is that 1.8 km was cut at 23:58.
   - **Sources contradict that reading:** PMC13498593 says paleocanyons "had already been cut across the Kaibab uplift before 15 Ma", Marble Canyon "was incised after 5 Ma", and incision was still going on 4.6-4.3 Ma.
   - **The hedge points the wrong way:** "The age of its deepest parts is debated" is in no opened source. The debate is about older stretches along the canyon, not its bottom. A canyon cuts downward, so at any one place its deepest rock is the most recently cut.
   - **Suggested fix** (every part is in the three sources): "at 23:58, 6–5 million years ago, the Colorado River joined older stretches of canyon into one path through what is now the 1.8 km-deep Grand Canyon. How old those stretches are is debated."
   - **Not checked from the rendered lesson:** the walkthrough transcript and screenshots are from 2026-10-14, before v4, so I read the learner text from Demo.tsx.
   - Confidence: high on the sources and the clock arithmetic, medium-high on the misreading.

summary: cm-big-ideas: earth-history wording call: I ruled for option (c): the Grand Canyon example comes out of the lesson entirely (stage and reveal), and the…
body:
I ruled for option (c): the Grand Canyon example comes out of the lesson entirely (stage and reveal), and the reveal makes its point with an arithmetic example (rate × time) tied to a stage event the learner has already found. The ruling is written and pushed. I did not edit the lesson, board.json or progress.md, and there was no [deploy].

**Why not (a).** Pass 44's wording is accurate, but it no longer illustrates c6. After the colon it describes the river *joining* older stretches of canyon into one path. Nothing in it says how much rock was cut in the 6–5 Ma window, and "how old those stretches are is debated" tells the learner the large thing may be older. So the colon would introduce an example that doesn't show "a slow process did a large thing in the time shown", and a careless reader gets the old whole-depth error back. Three disputes in one day also suggest the canyon's real history is too tangled for a one-line point.

**Why not (b).** Every real slow-process example I could name (the Atlantic opening, Himalayan uplift, a measured erosion rate) would be a second held-source sentence in the reveal. c2 (Homo sapiens) is already the reveal's one allowed held citation, so that breaks the strategy's rule (D4(b)).

**Exact text for the builder**
- Reveal paragraph 2 (replaces the current one; paragraphs 1 and 3 unchanged; the reveal comes to 81 words, under the 90 limit):
  `Given this much time, even a process too slow to see can do large things: since the non-bird dinosaurs ended at 23:39, about 66 million years ago, something creeping just 1 cm a year would have moved about 660 km.`
- Stage: delete the `canyon` event from `EVENTS`, so there is no canyon stage label. The referent's label stays `Non-bird dinosaurs end` (23:39:03). The builder should confirm `EVENTS[1]` is still the dinosaurs, because the milestone check uses it.
- c6: text unchanged, `Given this much time, even a process too slow to see can do large things (reveal: '…')`, support derivation. Add a source note that its example is now c10. Reset it to unverified so a fact-checker re-reads it, as Pass 44 asked.
- c9: status `withdrawn`, with a note pointing to the ruling. Keep its text and source for the record, as was done for c4.
- New c10, derivation, unverified: `Since the non-bird dinosaurs ended at 23:39 on the clock, about 66 million years ago, something creeping just 1 cm a year would have moved about 660 km.` Working: 66e6 years × 1 cm = 660 km. The date and clock time come from c3; the rate is stated as hypothetical, so it needs no source.
- Fallbacks:
  - If c3 is ever disputed, use this paragraph instead (no dated event): `…in the clock's last hour, about 189 million years, something creeping just 1 cm a year would have moved about 1,900 km.`
  - If the example must go entirely: `Given this much time, even a process too slow to see can do large things.` (full stop instead of the colon).

summary: [project:history] Learner reviews: 13 History lessons: I reviewed all 13 History lessons as an adult beginner (the boundary each brief gives): **4 launch, 9 revise,…
body:
I reviewed all 13 History lessons as an adult beginner (the boundary each brief gives): **4 launch, 9 revise, 0 fatal**. Of the proposed launch-review five, two are launch and three are revise. This is a simulated learner, so it finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.

For each lesson I ran the walkthrough against :3590 and looked at both the transcript and `sheet.png` (screenshots seen for all 13). I wrote my findings before reading the rest of the brief and build.md. One caveat: I read each brief's learner field (knows / doesNotKnow) before walking, because it is the boundary input, and its doesNotKnow lines partly state the lesson's point.

Per slug:
- **survive-childhood-live-to-sixty: launch.** Notes only: the step-4 labels crowd each other ("from 60: 72" sits on top of the others), and "AVERAGE AGE AT DEATH FROM 30" can be misread as 30 + 58.
- **income-flat-then-sixteenfold: revise.** The reveal says "most of history looks flat on this chart" while the log-scale chart is on screen, where it doesn't look flat, and the dashed steady-rate line doesn't fit the data. Fix: end on the linear view, or name the view and explain the log scale.
- **rome-placed-too-far-east: revise.** The stage makes you ask "why were they all too far east?", but the reveal only explains why the errors were big ("longitude needs time"). Fix: one claimed sentence on why the bias ran one way, plus "AD 150" in place of the bare "150".
- **cholera-fell-with-height: revise.** Step 4's "still falls with height", inside one water company, reads to a beginner as proof that height matters, and the reveal then says the table can't tell height from water. Fix: add "but no central-Thames district is high", or cut step 4.
- **earthquakes-did-not-fall: launch.** Notes: the "1.37M" bar label overprints its panel header, and the hook "And earthquakes?" mildly signals a twist.
- **lakes-misplaced-east-west: revise.** At the reveal, the Coronelli bar label is clipped to "59 / 3(", and that is the exact number the reveal quotes. Fix: move or wrap the label (don't shrink it).
- **children-dying-before-five: launch.** Notes: "56% of the fall after 1950" is mostly down to that span being longer, and the "Out of 100 children" step changes only the readout, not the picture.
- **wages-bought-more-wheat: revise.** Yes, the walkthrough bears out your caution: "Dearer bread, poorer workers?" plus "Did that make a working man poorer?" signals "no" before the commit. The answer "2.5 times" also echoes the question's "2.4". And at the reveal the top of the stage is cut off, so the line's axis label is gone. Fix: an open title and hook, and re-check the reveal fit.
- **doubling-stopped-speeding-up: revise.** The options give it away: 24 and 96 are half and double of 48, so the oddly specific 47 stands out. The reveal never answers "but it added twice as many people". Fix: half/same/double options, plus one reveal clause on that objection.
- **italy-poorer-in-1800: revise.** The hook's "did people at least get slowly richer?" signals the answer. The comparison runs from the 1450 spike to the 1800 dip and is never defended, and "the copy we opened" is in-house wording. Fix: an open hook, show a smoothed or averaged comparison, and rewrite the limit sentence.
- **life-expectancy-gained-late: revise.** The "Years gained per century" button puts a 23-year bar beside century bars, which suggests the gains stopped. "+2.8 (30.6 → 33.5)" fails a beginner's subtraction (33.5 − 30.6 = 2.9). Fix: relabel as spans, and make the shown numbers add up.
- **coal-came-back: launch.** Notes: the coal/oil lead change is hard to see in the stacked bands, and "×3 tonnes" and "the file" are awkward wording.
- **more-boys-christened: revise.** The cause ("once the counts are in the thousands") is told in one sentence; nothing on the stage shows yearly counts or what small counts would do. Fix: show the yearly total, or add a seeded "if only 100 a year" control.

The served build looks older than meta.json on claim status. Trust sheets read 8/10 for income, 7/9 for rome, 4/5 for cholera, 6/7 for children and 4/6 for doubling, but meta.json has every claim verified. That is a rebuild issue, not a teaching one; I noted it in the affected reviews.

How sure I am:
- **Confident:** the clipped and cropped labels (lakes, wages), the doubling options, and the cholera step-4 contradiction.
- **Fairly confident:** rome, more-boys, income.
- **Judgement calls:** life-expectancy, italy, and how strongly the yes/no titles cue "no".

Next moves (I didn't touch the board or progress.md):
- **demo-builder:** fix the 9 revise lessons; cm-history rules on the title and hook rewrites for wages, italy and doubling.
- **fact-checker:** italy, whether a smoothed series also falls (it's a question, not an error I found); rome, the "2 vs 5 read from maps" count raised in its build.md.
- **Whoever owns the :3590 build:** rebuild it so the trust sheets match meta.json.

body:
Fact-check pass 45 (W-980) is done. income-flat-then-sixteenfold now has every claim verified (10 of 10). london-buried-six-times-more does not: c4 is unverified, so it has 3 of 4.

**The three verdicts**
- **london c1: VERIFIED.** The question "(Creighton; 1965 edition)" matches the claim text. I re-ran the numbers with my own script on Arbuthnot.csv (its hash matches the pin). 1664: 15,453. 1665: 97,306, with 68,596 from plague. 1666: 12,738. Christenings in 1665: 9,972. 1636: 10,400 of 23,359. BILLS in Demo.tsx matches the file in all 82 rows. I opened man/Arbuthnot.Rd from CRAN (HistData_1.1.1.tar.gz). Its reference is "Creighton, C. (1965). A History of Epidemics in Britain, 2nd edition", so "1965 edition" is right. Non-blocking advisory: the citation leaves out Campbell (2001).
- **london c4: UNVERIFIED.** The builder asked whether "one later compilation (Creighton)" is fair. Not yet. "Recorded deaths and recorded causes" and "later" are supported; the Rd says "total mortality" and "deaths from plague". "One … (Creighton)" is not supported. The Rd says the columns were "obtained by Campbell and from Creighton (1965)":
  - If that means Campbell took them from Creighton, then Creighton is the one compilation and the sentence is right.
  - If it means two separate sources, "one" is wrong.
  - The Rd doesn't settle it. Campbell's page (math.uni.edu/~campbell/arbuth.html) would, but it returned 403. archive.org, web.archive.org, JSTOR, Crossref and Gutenberg were blocked too.
  - This sentence is the wording pass 43 proposed. I'm a different instance and didn't write it, but because my role proposed it I checked it strictly.
  - Fix, either:
    - (a) Change the sentence to "Where it stops: these are recorded deaths and recorded causes, from later compilations (Creighton; Campbell)." This is true under both readings. If (a) is used, c1 should cite both names too, so the lesson stays consistent.
    - (b) A session that can open Campbell's page or Campbell 2001 confirms both columns came from Creighton. The current sentence then verifies as written.
- **income c8: VERIFIED.** All three addresses appear in the learner text: the reveal, the hook ("Income per person in England…") and the question ("England's income per person…"). I re-opened the OWID copy of the Maddison 2020 README. It marks only 1252–1700 as "(England)" and gives 1700–1870 no territory label. The corrected source note now matches it.
