body:
B3 is done, with one real defect and two unexplained contract timeouts. Of the 11 W3 records, 8 pass and 3 are `fail`. All 11 are on lhw3 in commit 99d6f2d, authored `qa-tester`.

**Changed**
- Added `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-16-qa.md` for each of the 11 W3 slugs. Each has a `target: http://localhost:3941 · mode: self-started · built from: 5d9de52d9166211d78db1714991e014889b63a21` line and a `result:` line.
- Local files, not committed: scripts and screenshots in `/home/user/s3c-lhw3/artifacts/explore/`, and the QA report in `/home/user/s3c-lhw3/artifacts/qa-lhw3/`.
- Nothing else was edited, and `tsconfig.json` was reverted after the build.

**Checked on disk**
- Build: `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-lhqa npm run build` at a clean 5d9de52.
- Contract run (`QA_ONLY=<the 11 slugs> QA_PORT=3941 QA_OUT=artifacts/qa-lhw3 npm run qa`): 28 passed, 4 failed. The harness stamp is clean (contract commit 3b97991).
- **The tip moved during the run.** lhw3 is now 4251146 (FC pass 54, B2). Its diff against 5d9de52 touches only the 11 W3 meta.json files and one fact-check file. I did not re-run on 4251146. Each record names both SHAs.
- **long-cord-knots-itself: soft lock, record `fail`.**
  - The contract run passes it, but it clicks controls in DOM order.
  - Tapping "Tumble 3 m" first fills both result rows and ticks both buttons. It then disables both buttons, and "Try it first" stays disabled for good. I saw the same lock with all three predictions, and only a reload gets out.
  - A then B (even fast) unlocks the reveal.
  - I read `src/components/lifehacks/HomeLesson.tsx` line 453 to locate it: B sets `runs` to 2 but calls only `reach('long')`. The reveal needs `short` and `long`. That is the likely cause, not a tested one.
  - Screenshot: `/home/user/s3c-lhw3/artifacts/explore/shots/cord-B-first.png`.
- **elastic-loop-release and fitted-sheet-corners-nest: phone timeouts, records `fail`.**
  - Both timed out at 45 s at `contract.spec.ts:99` in the full parallel run.
  - The failure snapshot shows Show me why already enabled, so the lesson had unlocked and the run was slow.
  - I then ran each alone three times: 3 of 3 passed in about 6 s.
  - I recorded the original result and did not convert it to a pass. The cause of the slow run is unknown.
- **feed.spec "subject chips filter the feed"** failed on phone and desktop. QA_ONLY shrinks the lesson list but the feed shows every Hacks lesson. The W3 readiness addendum records the same. I did not count it against any lesson.
- **Exploratory pass on all 11** (phone, 360×640 small phone, desktop, plus reduced-motion and dark on phone):
  - Stage controls were locked before the prediction.
  - Double-tapping the option and the commit button gave one clean commit.
  - Tab and Space select an option and enable commit.
  - Every slider step produced no NaN, undefined, Infinity, raw `{token}` or `-0`.
  - No overflow, no clipped controls, no console errors.
  - Reload returns to the predict phase.
- **Two-option lessons (5):** I committed both options in each, through to the reveal. The "Your prediction held" and "Not quite: it was “…”" lines were correct for each.
- **tote-balance-sides negative cell:** it reads `−10 cm · left of the handle` and `−13.3 cm · left of the handle` across slider steps 1 to 5. No `-0` or NaN appeared. Observation: the sign convention is never stated on the card.
- **Other observations:**
  - sock-pairing-by-pattern's options are bare `11` and `3`.
  - Its reveal reads "one of the other 1" at the slider minimum.
- `npm run check` passed, with 4 warnings (disputed claims).

**Believed, not checked**
- The two timeouts are slowness under load (the failure snapshot and 3 of 3 isolated passes point that way).
- I saw only two screenshots (tote-balance-sides small phone, cord B-first). The rest were checked by script. In the tote one the top of the drawing looks cut off. I think that is scroll position, but I did not verify it.
- Dark and reduced-motion runs were checked only for overflow and errors, not for contrast.

**Not done**
- I did not run `npm run company -- qa-record` in the worktree. It rewrites `meta.json` `evidence.qa`, which would collide with B2's edits. I ran it on a clean export of 5d9de52 instead and enriched the output. So `evidence.qa` links are not added to the 8 passing lessons, and the 3 failing ones get none anyway. Re-run it after B2 merges.
- I did not edit `board.json`, `progress.md` or any test or lesson.
- I did not give the elastic-loop-release and fitted-sheet-corners-nest timeouts a full re-run on a quiet host.

**Confidence**
- High that long-cord-knots-itself has the soft lock, because it reproduced in four runs.
- Moderate that the other ten lessons are clean. Two of them are marked `fail` only because of the timeouts.

**Next**
- cm-lifehacks: fix the long-cord-knots-itself reveal-unlock bug. After it lands, the qa-tester re-runs that lesson and the two timeout lessons.
- evaluation-steward: B4 should skip long-cord-knots-itself, elastic-loop-release and fitted-sheet-corners-nest until they are re-QA'd. Consider asking tools/evaluation-steward for a contract check that clicks controls in reverse order, since the existing contract misses the soft lock.
- Chief of staff: merge, then re-run `qa-record` for the evidence links. Close the server on 3941. I stopped PIDs 5571, 5609 and 5610 and removed `.next-lhqa`.

body:
## B5 report: FC pass 54b on the behavioral pilot (same-week-a-year-apart, sure-million-or-long-shot)

I checked all 23 claims. 21 are verified, 2 are held and none are disputed. B5's done-when is met: `npm run company -- claims --open | grep -c "behavioral\."` went from 23 claim lines (26 raw lines, because 3 source lines also match the pattern) to 2. The 2 left open are the two c6 lines, and each has a pass-54b note saying why it is held.

**Changed** (one commit by `fact-checker`, made only on the paths below, rebased and pushed; it was 8dc5b72 before the rebase and the tip is now 6ebd515)
- /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/behavioral/same-week-a-year-apart/meta.json: c1–c5 and c7–c12 verified; c6 held (status unverified).
- /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/behavioral/sure-million-or-long-shot/meta.json: c1–c5 and c7–c11 verified; c6 held.
- Every claim now has `note: "FC pass 54b (fact-checker, 2026-10-16): …"`, `checkedBy: fact-checker` and `checkedOn: 2026-10-16`.
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/same-week-a-year-apart/2026-10-16-fact-check.md
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/sure-million-or-long-shot/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

**Checked on disk**
- **I wrote none of these claims:** the git history shows only cm-behavioral and builder commits, and each source field says "Builder statement".
- **The lessons as a learner sees them come first:**
  - I made a production build into `.next-befc`, served it with `next start -p 3951`, and ran `walkthrough --url` with choose 0, 1 and 2. I cut each transcript at the trust-sheet appendix (rule R1).
  - The walkthrough only shows one branch, so I wrote my own Playwright script and drove all four choice combinations in each lesson. Every reveal matched its claim text.
  - In same-week, the near choice is disabled until the pair reaches today. In sure-million, the reveal stays locked until a card is chosen in each pair and the toggle is pressed.
  - I did not read build.md or design.md.
- **The numbers:**
  - My own node script: 200,000 random increasing utility functions gave 0 mixed pairs, both for the Allais pairs and for the recall pairs X/Y. For the time claims, the ratio 1.1·d holds at every stop with a maximum deviation of 4.4e-16. The present-bias witness (b = 0.9) gives 1.10 then 0.99, and a hyperbolic model also switches. The recall ratio is 1.2·d^10 at both dates.
  - cm-behavioral's two check scripts, re-run: "all checks pass".
- **Sources opened through PMC OAI-PMH (HTTP 200):**
  - PMC9584811 supports the term "present bias" ("common difference (we refer to this as present bias…)").
  - PMC2891015 supports the "certainty effect" naming of the 1A+2B pattern. One other source, PMC4643135, labels the patterns differently; this is noted in the record.
  - PMC10489299 and PMC9337702 are the two secondary sources behind the held lines (see below).

**Why the two c6 lines are held**
- My W-975 statement covers claim types (a)–(c) only, so type (d) lines are held by default. Both lines also rest on second-hand attributions, which W-1059 has not yet ruled on.
- Each line has its own gap as well:
  - **same-week c6:** PMC10489299 supports "clearer for effort than for money". The words "with real payments" are not in the passage I opened.
  - **sure-million c6:** PMC9337702 says Ruggeri et al. "substantially confirmed the original findings, albeit with attenuated effects" for 4,098 people in 19 countries. That refers to prospect theory's set of problems as a whole and does not name the certainty effect, so the lesson's sentence claims more than the source says.
- **Both held lines are rendered in the current build** (HELD_LINE is on), so neither lesson can publish until they are verified or the fallback text is used.

**Believed, not checked**
- That Augenblick 2015 used incentivised payments, and the item-level Ruggeri 2020 result for the certainty-effect problem. Both would need the primary papers, which are on blocked hosts, so I did not verify them from memory.

**Confidence**
- High on the 21 verified claims: each was derived independently and checked against every rendered branch.
- High that the two held lines cannot be verified on today's evidence.

**Non-blocking notes for the builder** (in the records)
- same-week, take/take branch: the "Switching to the $100 today…" sentence describes a switch this learner did not make. It is true as a conditional; rewording is the designer's call.
- same-week alt text reads "$100 at today".
- sure-million: the indifference edge case of c1/c4 is measure-zero and not a dispute.
- sure-million: pressing the toggle before choosing cards relabels the cards. This is for QA.

**Housekeeping**
- I stopped my server by exact PID (14260, then its orphaned child 14304), confirmed through its environment that it was mine (NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-befc), and deleted `.next-befc`.
- tsconfig.json is unchanged. `npm run check` passed: 965 lessons, 6 warnings, all in Life Hacks.

**Next, with owner role**
1. **cm-behavioral (lane 1):** answer both held c6 lines. Either have the builder set HELD_LINE = false (the fallback text is already in the check scripts), or bring a reachable source for the certainty-effect item and for "real payments".
2. **fact-checker:** rule W-1059 and write the dated (d) line of the W-975 statement. These are the gates for both c6 lines and for the fold-floor recount. Please put them on the board for a later pass.
3. **Chief of staff (board):** W-975 and W-1059 stay with fact-checker. Please record pass 54b against W-975.

**Not done**
- No ruling on W-1059 and no (d) statement: B5 did not ask for them, and the statement says to apply it as written.
- No edits to board.json, progress.md or events.jsonl.
- No Demo.tsx changes; that is out of my scope.

body:
**W-1238 (R1): I approved the EDD-003 "A2 pilot" addendum with changes P-1 to P-7 and passed ADR-010.** I acknowledged the esbuild dependency record with no objection. F1 does not change the direction of my item-5 re-size, but it does change the size. The record is committed and pushed (617dfdb).

**Changed**
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/reviews/2026-10-16-edd-003-a2-pilot-review.md` (new): the tier-2 review record.
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/rituals/records/2026-10-16-project-review-positions-principal-engineer.md`: I added a dated "Revision 2026-10-16" section to my own position file. The forum record itself is not edited.
- Commit 617dfdb on ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1, committed by explicit path with GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=principal-engineer, then rebased and pushed.

**Rulings**
- **ADR-010:** passes my review. It stays `proposed` until the founder decides W-485 and principal-engineer-ops approves R2.
- **Dependency record:** acknowledged. My 2026-10-14 supply-chain objection is answered for today, because the binary is already installed through `vercel`.
- **Main finding:** return line 2 ("≤ 30 s QA per changed lesson") already passes in the app today (about 3.4 s per lesson). Under the addendum's own design, a kit change re-hashes every frame document, so the pilot would re-QA everything, which is what the app already does. **P-1** therefore requires the manifest to record the lesson hash separately from the kit hash, and the checkpoint record to report how many lessons a kit change re-QAs.
- **Q1, may build runs start before W-085 reaches a phone?** Yes, after gates G2 to G5, and only up to the checkpoint (25 lessons, 1.2M). The pilot holds there until a real-device warm read exists. I accept that hold in place of my earlier proxy line (d).
- **Q2, may "migrated" mean built and QA'd but not served?** Yes. Records must say "pilot-migrated (… not served)", never "migrated" alone (P-5).
- **Q3, does 127.0.0.1 stand in for W-086?** Yes, for the pilot only. The server binds to loopback only, the CSP goes out as a header, and the pilot's probes are not W-086 evidence.
- **Q4, which route?** Reuse `/spike` with one added guard-test case. No new route.
- **Q5, Life Hacks engines as a bundle?** Not before tranche 2, and not ruled out. It reopens only when the W1 to W9 engines have stopped changing and a Life Hacks lesson is published. Tranche 2 should be sized at about 715 lessons, not about 910.
- **F1 and my item-5 position:** release 1.2M now, with 1.89M as the ceiling. The other 0.69M waits for both the checkpoint record and a W-085 phone read. The checkpoint is 1.2M (costed), not my 1.0M. The case for stage 1 now rests on the 55-minute re-QA after a kit change and on the 1,000-lesson trigger.

**Checked on disk**
- esbuild is already installed and MIT → `npm ls esbuild` and reading its package.json → `esbuild@0.27.0 deduped` under `vercel@63.1.2`; licence MIT. `package.json` does not declare it.
- Audit → `npm audit --omit=dev` gives "found 0 vulnerabilities". Full `npm audit` gives "33 vulnerabilities (8 moderate, 24 high, 1 critical)", none naming esbuild.
- Slug file → count lines and look up each `meta.json` → 50 slugs, 25 marked checkpoint, 0 duplicates, 0 missing, all published, per-domain counts as stated.
- Stop rule → compared with agenda line 168 → word for word.
- F1 baseline → read the readiness record → 751 to 1 stylesheets, 230,185 B gz first-load JS, 2m27 and 3m19 builds, 1930 tests passed in 55.1 m.
- F2 counts → grep of `src/demos` → 965 lessons, 200 import Life Hacks engines, 10 import d3-geo or geojson.
- `/spike` guard → read `src/app/spike/page.tsx` → `notFound()` unless dev or `SPIKE_ENABLED=1`, origin from a server-side allow-list. `tests/spike/spike-guard.test.mjs` exists.
- `npm run check` → "check passed: 965 lessons, 5252 claims, 99 roles, 6 warning(s)".

**Believed, not checked**
- That esbuild's `local-css` handles the 522 `:global` lessons and builds deterministically. ADR-010 condition 5 tests this at R3.
- The per-lesson app-build cost of about 0.5 s, which is my arithmetic from the addendum's figures.
- That the 1,000-lesson trigger fires soon because of Wave J.
- The baseline timings, which are principal-engineer-ops' measurements and which I did not re-run.

**Confidence**
- High on the conditions and on Q2 to Q4.
- Medium-high on finding 1 (P-1), read from the addendum §7.3 design, not run.
- Medium on Q5, which depends on how the Life Hacks engines settle.

**Next, with owner role**
- platform-engineer: write P-1, P-2 and P-5 into the addendum (that clears G1), then R2, the readiness record for the dependency.
- principal-engineer-ops: approve R2 (G4); put the 33 dev-only `vercel` advisories on the risk register.
- founder, through chief-of-staff: W-485 (G2).
- portfolio-manager: carry "release 1.2M of the 1.89M ceiling" and the "pilot-migrated" wording into the register and the forum's item-5 line.
- chief-of-staff, board asks: move W-1238 to done. Add one item for platform-engineer (P-1, P-2, P-5 in the addendum) and one for principal-engineer-ops (vercel advisories, risk register).

**Not done**

- Kudos for platform-engineer are written in the record but not harvested. `node tools/kudos.mjs harvest` writes to `company/ops/events.jsonl`, which only the chief of staff writes. I ran it by mistake, reverted those 5 lines with `git checkout`, and did not commit them. The chief of staff should run the harvest.

body:
## B1 report (backend-engineer, W-966): accounts readiness gaps, author's part

I closed A-5, A-6 and F-f in code, each with a test, re-measured C9, and wrote readiness sections 1 to 7. The full accounts suite passes. One finding matters for the privacy re-read: switching off Better Auth's logger alone would not have stopped the email leak (see A-6 below).

### Changed
Worktree /home/user/s3c-acct, branch `accounts`. Seven commits after 6ff15ba, committed locally, not pushed, merged or deployed:
- **217414b, A-6:** Better Auth's `logger.log` now prints only `{level, kind, code}` (`libraryLogLine`). `onAPIError: { throw: true }` sends router errors to our `failed()`, which logs the error class only.
- **11da999, A-5:** `createAuth` refuses to construct if any `BETTER_AUTH_TELEMETRY*` variable is set, to anything including empty, either in the env passed in or in `process.env`. It checks names only and never reads a value.
  - I chose the prefix so it also covers `_DEBUG` and `_ID`. That is my own call, beyond the brief's two names.
  - `AccountsConfigError` now takes an optional reason.
- **ae30e38, F-f:** `rateLimit.customRules["/magic-link/verify"]` is now 30 per 60 s per IP. `start` stays at 5 per IP and per email. The new test replaces the old 5-per-minute FINDING test.
- **be40769, C9:** `tests/accounts/firstload.mjs`, a script anyone can re-run for the measurement.
- **0a0ee5b, readiness record:** sections 1 to 7 written into /home/user/s3c-acct/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-accounts.md.
  - Covers the A-3 kill-switch text, the A-7 smoke line (for W-1150), the A-8 go-live order with the A-4 check as step 4, A-10's section 4 and 5 lines, A-11's data links, and a status row for every gap.
  - Also two edits to /home/user/s3c-acct/company/engineering/edd/EDD-008-accounts-and-server-progress.md: the readiness draft now points to the record, and the §9 Vercel row is corrected.
- **1ab28b9 and 00bf9b7:** fix the SHAs the record cites.

The three new A-6, A-5 and F-f test titles were added to `tests/accounts/better-auth-regression.json`, so the M5 bump guard re-checks them on every library upgrade.

### Checked on disk
- **Suite passes.** `TEST_DATABASE_URL=<throwaway local PG16> npm run test:accounts` at 00bf9b7: 41 tests, 38 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. The skipped three are in built-routes and need `ACCOUNTS_BASE_URL`. The new tests:
  - "F-f: /magic-link/verify allows 30 per 60 s per IP (shared school addresses), then 429; start stays at 5"
  - "A-6: a constraint violation through a library route logs no email and no token (stderr and console)"
  - "A-6: libraryLogLine prints the level, the error class and its code, never a message, detail or argument"
  - "A-5: createAuth refuses to construct while any BETTER_AUTH_TELEMETRY* variable is set (any value, empty included)"
  - The other 37 titles are unchanged from M1 to M6.
- **The A-6 test catches the leak.** I reverted the fix and re-ran it:
  - With 6ff15ba's config, it fails and the log contains `ERROR [Better Auth]: new row for relation "auth_user" violates check constraint…`, with the pg detail holding the email.
  - With only the logger fixed, it still fails. better-call's router has its own `console.error("# SERVER_ERROR: ", error)` (`node_modules/better-call/dist/router.mjs:93`) that ignores the logger setting. Both halves of the fix are needed.
- **C9 is under the ceiling.** I built two trees: main at 49aea2e (the main commit merged into accounts), from `git archive`, and accounts at ae30e38.
  - `/`: 781,131 B raw / 231,514 B gzip before, 782,356 / 231,964 after. That is +1,225 raw and **+450 B gzip, under the 1,024 B ceiling.**
  - `/d/a-birthday-like-mine`: +449 B gzip.
  - No library string in any first-load script.
  - All of the growth is the Turbopack runtime chunk (it gains `turbopack queues`). The other two changed chunks differ only in module ids. This matches SPIKE-002 R2.
- **Rest is clean.** `npm run typecheck` exits 0. `npm run check` passes. `db-migrate down 001` then `up` leaves 1 table, then 9. The tsconfig edit made by `next build` was reverted. The Postgres cluster under /tmp/acctb1 is stopped and deleted, and the dist dirs and the baseline tree are deleted.

### Believed, not checked
- The library has a few other direct `console` calls I could not configure away. The one in core's fallback-join catch (`factory.mjs:392`) prints a read error, which I believe carries no row data (about 80%).
- The smoke line was not run against production. Accounts are not on main yet, so production would answer 404 anyway.
- Kill-switch time to off is not measured on Vercel. The only number is a local build, about 2.5 minutes on a loaded host.
- The Vercel log retention figure is from memory.

### Confidence
- A-5, A-6 and F-f are correct as built: 90%.
- C9 is within the ceiling on the merged tree: 95%. On current main it is not measured. Main is at 88c4bb7, 31 commits past 49aea2e.

### Next, with owner
1. **Chief of staff:** rebase `accounts` onto current main, run `npm run verify`, and re-run `firstload.mjs` before and after (A-13, C9).
2. **Privacy-reviewer, through evaluation-steward (lane 10):** read the diff from 6ff15ba, especially the A-6 log content, plus the earlier `2f5c500..6ff15ba` re-read and the M2 ruling.
3. **Principal-engineer-ops (lane 8):** the readiness approval pass, plus scoring my R-a proposal (§7).
4. **Release-manager:** put the §2 smoke text and the §3 kill-switch text into the runbook (W-1150), and measure time to off on the first approved preview.
5. **Board asks:** none. W-966 stays open for lane 8.

### Not done
- The `dispatch-check --worktree` command named in the item does not exist in either checkout's company CLI. Running it prints the usage list, so it was not run.

**Run estimate:** this was one run, at about 1.4 of the tech lead's 110k units. Two `next build`s and slow tests on a contended host made up most of the overrun.

B3 is done: commit-own.sh, the explicit-path pre-commit guard and the no-pkill hook, with bare-stash rules added. All three are shipped unwired and uninstalled, on branch tools-guards in /home/user/s3c-tools3, commits ba0af0d and 8d3fbff, not pushed. One thing to know first: by paths.json the readiness record is **tier 2, not the tier-1 self-check the batch asked for**, so nothing here should be wired until principal-engineer-ops approves it.

**Changed** (author tools-lead, both commits made by explicit path with commit-own.sh)
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/tools/commit-own.sh`
  - Refuses options where the message or a path should be.
  - Refuses if any staged path is outside the list you name. During a merge, paths changed on the merged branch (`HEAD...MERGE_HEAD`) also count as allowed. A refusal leaves the index exactly as it was.
  - Otherwise it stages the named paths and runs `git commit -m <msg> -- <paths>`, or the merge commit. It sets `S3_COMMIT_PATHS` so the hook checks the same list.
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/tools/git-hooks/pre-commit` (node, **not installed**)
  - Applies only in the main checkout. Linked worktrees, partial commits (`-- <paths>`) and empty commits pass.
  - Refuses a bare commit, `-a` and `-i`.
  - Refuses a merge commit that would include staged paths the merged branch did not change and `S3_COMMIT_PATHS` does not list. That is the 2e2ccd9 case.
  - Refuses staged paths outside `S3_COMMIT_PATHS`.
  - If the guard itself errors, it warns and lets the commit through.
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/.claude/hooks/no-pkill.mjs` (Bash PreToolUse, **unwired**)
  - It only looks at the command word of each command, so `git commit -m "add pkill -f hook"` and `grep "pkill -f"` pass.
  - Refuses `pkill` in any form, `pgrep -f`, `killall <name>`, `kill $(pgrep|pidof …)`, `xargs kill` and `kill -1`. The message points to `tools/serve.sh stop <port>` or `kill <pid>`.
  - Stash rules, from your note: it refuses bare `git stash`, `push` without `-m`, `save`, any `pop`, `apply`/`drop`/`branch` without a ref, and `clear`. It applies in every checkout, because the stash stack is shared by all worktrees and git has no stash hook. The file name stays as specified because B1's merged record and F-31 already name it.
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/tests/dispatch/guards.test.mjs`: 16 tests, run only in temp git repos, which they delete afterwards.
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-commit-and-process-guards.md` holds the install command (not run), the combined F-31 settings.json snippet (B1's entries plus no-pkill), rollback steps and the approval section, left blank.
- `/home/user/s3c-tools3/company/ops/changelog.md`: one entry.
- Before my first commit I fast-forwarded the branch onto origin c030715, which already contains B1's merge 39f22c3.

**Checked on disk**
- `npm run test:dispatch`: 45/45 (16 of them are B3's). `npm run check`: passed (965 lessons, 8 warnings).
- I probed git 2.43.0's index files in a scratch repo:
  - a partial commit uses `next-index-*.lock`;
  - `-a` and `-i` use `index.lock`;
  - a bare commit uses `.git/index`.
  - A clean `merge --no-ff` with a staged path aborts on its own. The gap is the conflicted merge, which the hook covers.
- No-pkill hook cost: 172 ms average per Bash call over 10 runs on this host.
- `core.hooksPath` is unset in the shared repo, and `.claude/settings.json` is unchanged.
- B2's slot files are gitignored on tools-ledger.

**Where it meets B1 and B2**
- **B1 (merged):** one F-31 change wires both hooks; the snippet in my record covers both.
- **B2 (c73ddb9):** the only shared file is changelog.md, where both add a top entry, so expect a trivial conflict. The stash rules are the answer to B2's stray `git stash`, once wired.
- **`tools/snapshot.sh`:** it is a whole-tree sweep (bare `git commit`), so once the guard is installed it will be refused in the main checkout. My recommendation is to retire it. I did not edit it: it is deploy-class tier 2 and outside this item.

**Believed, not checked**
- The live Bash payload fields are `tool_name` and `tool_input.command` (about 95%; protect-constitution.mjs reads the same ones).
- Other git versions name the partial-commit index the same way. If not, the hook refuses rather than lets a sweep through.

**Gaps**
- Neither CI nor `npm run verify` runs test:dispatch, so these tests run only when someone runs them by hand.
- The hook cannot see pattern kills hidden in `eval` or in script files.

**Confidence:** high that the scripts behave as tested; medium on how strict commit-own.sh should be. It refuses even outside merges, where plain `git commit -- <paths>` could not sweep anything. I kept it strict, as the item asks, and plain `git commit -- <paths>` remains a fallback that never blocks.

**Next, with owner**
- principal-engineer (lane 7): check B3.
- principal-engineer-ops: tier-2 approval of the record.
- chief of staff:
  - merge tools-guards;
  - rule on snapshot.sh;
  - install the guard with `git -C /home/user/system-3-company config core.hooksPath tools/git-hooks`, only after approval;
  - fold no-pkill into F-31.
- Founder: F-31, to wire no-pkill.

body:
I've made the ruling on how the stage word budget counts, for the whole company. Brief 4 (saved-or-die-same-600) is unblocked once cm-behavioral adds one line to its brief. Brief 3 (zero-loses-to-this-crowd) passes at exactly 25 and doesn't change. It is pushed as commit 9b8bce0.

**The ruling:**
- **What the stage is:** everything the kit renders inside `data-testid="stage"`, counted at the frame with the most text, from the locked frame to the open reveal. A word is any space-separated token with a letter in it; "1-in-3" counts as one word.
- **Numbers count 0.** That covers numerals, amounts, percentages, and numbers joined to a unit ("$1M", "10m"). The words around a number still count ("$100 at week 52" is 2). This holds in legends, readouts and sentences alike. It confirms cm-behavioral's points 2 and 3 as a single rule.
- **Stage button, toggle and slider labels count**, as do captions, readout labels, keys, covers and glosses.
- **Kit text outside the stage does not count toward the 25:** title, hook, the predict question and its options, the explore hint and the verdict line. The reveal keeps its 90-word limit, counted the way `tools/reveal-fit.mjs` counts it (numerals included).
- **The text a lesson manipulates (e.g. the two framings) is exempt from the 25, with conditions:**
  - The category manager must list it word for word in the brief; a builder can't declare it.
  - The test: would different wording change the reveal's claim?
  - Everything else on the stage stays at 25 or under, and the whole stage stays at 50 or under.
  - The phone-fit rule and the 10 px text floor still apply.
- **When a brief is over budget:** the builder counts before building and puts a table in build.md. It may shorten only its own wording that carries no claim. It never trims claim-bearing text, the manipulated text or anything the brief fixes, and never shrinks type. If the stage is still over, it writes "Stage over budget: N words", stops, and routes it: cm-<domain> decides what goes, the learning designer re-lays out if cutting isn't enough, then a revision build follows. Evaluators count from the artifact, and an over-budget stage is a finding.

**Changed**

At the hook's real rate of a few writes an hour this is negligible, and a lost event can still be recovered from the transcript by the backfill. body:
F1 and F2 are done in tools/events.mjs, and S2 is done too. Two folds at once now leave no duplicate id: in PE-ops' writers-plus-two-fold-loops reproduction, the old code gave 19,133 duplicates and 6 lost, and the new code gives 0 and 0. Committed on branch tools-f1 in /home/user/s3c-tools5, not pushed.

**Changed** (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=tools-lead, committed by explicit path)
- 1d1998a, F1 + F2:
  - `tools/events.mjs`:
    - `acquireFoldLock` creates `<spool>/fold.lock` exclusively, holding the pid. If a live pid holds it, the fold stops with exit 2 and the message `fold: a fold is already running (pid N, …)`.
    - A lock left by a dead pid, or holding no pid, is taken over only through a second exclusive file, `fold.lock.takeover`. The lock is removed only if it still holds the stale pid, so two folds can't both take the same dead lock.
    - `fold` takes over a `*.folding-<pid>` file only when that pid is dead (ESRCH = dead, EPERM = alive). A live fold's file is left alone and counted.
    - F2, fold side: after the append, each renamed file is re-read once its size has been stable for 100 ms, and any late ids are folded before the file is removed.
    - F2, writer side: `add --spool` now goes through a new `spoolAppend`. If the file it wrote was renamed during the write, it appends the line again to the current file (the fold dedupes by id).
  - New `tests/dispatch/fold-lock.test.mjs`, 6 tests: live lock refused; dead or garbled lock taken over and released; folding file of a dead vs live pid; two folds started together on 20,000 events; the two fold loops with 2 raw and 2 `spoolAppend` writers (0 duplicates, 0 lost); and the F2 race, an fd opened before the rename and written after it.
  - `tests/dispatch/agent-events.test.mjs`: the `folding-999` fixture now uses a pid that is certainly dead.
  - Also updated: the fold paragraph in `company/ops/events.md`, a line in `company/ops/changelog.md`, and a short pointer section ("Change notes for F1 + F2") in `company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-agent-events-hook.md`. That section is not a new record.
- c449e23, S2 (tier 1, self-check): `tools/ops-health.mjs` and `tools/rituals-due.mjs` read events.jsonl through `readJsonlFile`. Unreadable lines are skipped and counted on stderr instead of throwing.

**For PE-ops to read:**
`git -C /home/user/s3c-tools5 diff 23c6255 tools-f1 -- tools/events.mjs tests/dispatch/fold-lock.test.mjs tests/dispatch/agent-events.test.mjs`
(S2 alone: `git -C /home/user/s3c-tools5 diff 1d1998a c449e23`)

**Checked on disk**
- Tests: `npm run test:dispatch` gives 61/61, three runs in a row.
- `npm run check` passed (966 lessons, 8 warnings, none of them mine).
- Old vs new under load: the scratchpad stress script runs 2 raw `appendFileSync` writers × 20,000 plus two fold loops for 6 s.
  - Old code: 59,127 lines, 39,994 distinct, **19,133 duplicates**.
  - New code: 40,000 lines and 40,000 distinct, 0 duplicates and 0 lost. Also 0/0 with the 100 ms settle turned off, and 0/0 with 2 × 5,000 `spoolAppend` writers.
- S2: on a log copy with a `<<<<<<< HEAD` line, the new ops-health prints `ops-health: 1 unreadable line(s) skipped…` and then its table. The old ops-health throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'`. rituals-due runs normally on the real log.

**Believed, not checked**
- I didn't run the 6 new tests against the old code (they import `pidAlive`, which the old file doesn't export). Only the stress script was compared old vs new.
- A raw `appendFileSync` writer that stalls between opening the file and writing for longer than the settle time can still be lost. The real hook goes through `add --spool` → `spoolAppend`, which closes that gap unless the writer dies between its two appends.
- rituals-due was not run on a conflicted log: it always reads the real log, and I didn't touch that. It uses the same reader as ops-health.

**Confidence:** high on F1, which is sound by construction and gives 0 duplicates across every run. Medium-high on F2: 0 lost in every run, with the residual raw-writer window described above.

**F1 is met, and so is F2.** Once the founder approves F-31 and H1 runs, the agent-events hook can be wired without another readiness round from me. **Checked on disk**
I ran everything in a detached worktree of c449e23 under my scratchpad, against sandbox logs and spools only. The worktree is now removed.
- Tests: `npm run test:dispatch` gives 61/61 (the 55 from before plus 6 new fold-lock tests).
- My two-fold reproduction: 2 writers × 20,000 raw appends, two `fold()` loops in parallel, 3 runs. Each run: 40,000/40,000 in the log, 0 duplicates, 0 lost.
- Variations: 2 × 50,000 with 2 folds and with 1 fold, 2 × 40,000 with 4 folds, and 2 × 20,000 through `spoolAppend` (the hook's real write path). All 0/0.
- A 6-second run with two throttled writers: 87,470 events, 0/0, 35 folds; the other fold attempts were refused on the lock.
- A crash test the author's tests don't cover: for 8 seconds I killed a fold process every 150–350 ms by its exact handle and started a new one, 30 kills per run, 2 runs. 103,470 and 108,550 events, 0/0, spool empty at the end. Stale locks and dead folds' files were taken over and picked up correctly.
- Code reading: I followed the case where two folds find the same dead lock at once. Either way it ends with one fold holding the lock and the other refusing.
- S2 is a read-only change to `tools/ops-health.mjs` and `tools/rituals-due.mjs`, outside the hook's files. No objection.
- Real files: the worktree's events.jsonl stayed at 4,591,568 bytes, and no real `company/ops/events-spool/` was created. The main checkout's log grew while I worked, but from other sessions (latest commit 885f5c2), not from my processes.
- `npm run check`: passed (8 warnings, none from my file).

**F5, new, not gating (tools-lead)**
`fold` crashes with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" when one spool file holds more than about 120,000 events. The cause is `events.push(...r.events)` and `bad.push(...)` at tools/events.mjs lines 194, 195 and 218. `tools/lib/events-spool.mjs` line 75 (`readSpool`, used by fold --dry, metrics and dispatch-check) has the same pattern. It was already there at 23c6255.
- I hit it at 2 × 200,000 events. It fails safe: it throws before writing anything, the lock is released, and the log plus the left-over file held all 400,000 ids exactly once.
- But every later fold would hit the same file and crash again, so folding stays stuck until the code changes.
- It can't happen at the hook's rate of a few events an hour.
- Fix: replace the spreads with loops and add a test with a 200,000-line spool file.

**Believed, not checked**
- Every session that might run a fold shares one process-ID space on this host. The lock depends on this to tell a dead fold from a live one; a fold in another container on the same filesystem would look dead. F3 (fold only in the integration worktree) limits this.
- A raw appender that stalls between opening and writing the file can still lose a line, as the author says. The hook writes through `spoolAppend`, which covers that case. I did not try to force it.

**Confidence**
- High that F1 holds on this host: about 13 runs with no duplicate, including folds killed mid-fold.
- High that F2 holds for the hook's write path.
- Medium on the process-ID-space assumption.

body:
## B1 (W-1206) report: research-scientist

I pinned the current OWID series and re-ran brief 11's numbers on both series. On the current series the fall is ×9.75 in recorded deaths and ×36.5 per million people. The ×15 and ×57 in the draft only hold if epidemics are counted as disasters. No stop rule was triggered.

**Changed**

- The fetched files are in /home/user/system-3-company/artifacts/history-data/ (gitignored, not committed):

  - `owid-zip/natural-disasters-deaths.zip`
- I did not touch history-data.mjs, history-cycle1-check.mjs, the brief, or the board, progress or events files.

**Checked on disk**
- **Fetch.** `curl` of the plain CSV URL at 12:19:41Z returned 200, 275,205 bytes, sha256 `244aaa43368253a975e9cda6e9200bad1ba60fd78a70a602c2e20f777e129d6a`. The CSV inside the OWID zip has the same bytes and hash.
- **Yesterday's hash 3059d030… is not an upstream change.** Fetching `?useColumnShortNames=true` today still gives `3059d0307d099f80…`. That was just another URL for the same data.
- **The metadata JSON should not be pinned by hash.** It contains `"dateDownloaded": "2026-10-16"`, so its bytes change daily (today: sha `8b78b297…`, 15,488 bytes).
- **Columns and the world total match the note's description.** There are 8 disaster types plus an "All disasters" total, and no epidemic column. In all 126 World rows (1900-2025), the total equals the sum of the 8 types. World also equals the sum of every country and historical state in every year.
- **Decade means and ratios** (computed with a Python script against the fetched files):

| | 1920s mean a year | 2010-2017 mean a year | Fall | Per million people |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current series | 523,941.5 | 53,719.75 | ×9.75 | ×36.5 |
| Pinned vega file, epidemics removed | 540,329 | 52,670 | ×10.26 | ×38.4 |
| Pinned vega file, all types (brief as drafted) | 872,629 | 56,869 | ×15.34 | ×57.4 |

- **Population ratio** is ×3.7415. It is the gmpop (Gapminder) value for 2014 over 1925, the same method the check script uses at lines 346-347. Using decade-average populations instead gives ×36.4, so the method choice does not move the headline.
- **1931:** the current series records 3,718,976 deaths, 3,700,000 of them floods (China). It is the biggest single year on both series.
- **1918 influenza:** the current series has no epidemics, and its 1918 world total is 11,250. The vega file's 1918 epidemic figure is 449,700.
- **Not reachable:** api.ourworldindata.org (the full-metadata link) and doc.emdat.be (EM-DAT's terms of use) both returned proxy 403.

**Believed, not checked**
- **Licence.** The zip's readme says "License: UCLouvain 2026" and points to EM-DAT's terms. That means it is not CC BY. I could not open the terms, so we don't know whether a public lesson may show these numbers. That is for W-745 to settle.
- **EM-DAT version.** The files give no release number, only "Published 2026-04-28, Retrieved on 2026-04-30".
- **1918 pandemic death toll.** We don't know it from anything opened here. "Tens of millions" is still from memory and unverified.
- **What "recorded" covers.** The fall is in recorded deaths, partly a change in who got counted (medium). The metadata's own chart note says longer trends "may partly reflect reporting improvements".

**Confidence**
- High for the hashes, columns, means, ratios, 1931 and the 1918 absence: all were re-computed from the fetched files.
- Medium for what the numbers mean, as above.
- The headline the data support: about 10 times fewer recorded deaths a year, and about 36 times fewer per million. That gives the cultural reviewer's option C ("Fell more than 30-fold") as the single right answer.

body:
I found nothing reachable from this sandbox that says why all 12 of van Langren's estimates were too far east. The verdict is "we don't know from this sandbox", dated 2026-10-16. I tried 31 routes, which passes the batch's 30-route stop, so no wording goes to cm-history and c10 stays cut.

**Changed**

It holds the host table (this run's rows with UTC times; pass 53's and the manager probe's hosts are marked "per pass 53" or "per manager probe" and were not retried), the routes not yet tried, the verdict, the founder ask word for word, and who acts next.
- Commit a078e55, committed by explicit path, rebased onto origin/ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1 and pushed. I did not touch the board, progress.md or any protected path.

**Checked on disk**
- CRAN HistData_1.1.1.tar.gz: 200, sha256 b602f00c…. I unpacked it and ran `grep -rli ptolem` over the whole package: no hits. Its Langren.Rd (sha256 2034983b…) and the HistData-Challenge vignette give no cause.
- GitHub raw paths that the package names exactly all opened with 200: sandbox/Langren-graph.R, R/data-concepts.R, man/Langren.Rd, issues/TASKS.md, and the friendly.github.io blog .qmd. man/Langren.Rd still has pass 53's hash d365d87d…, and the blog .qmd still has 5eb33e84…. None mentions Ptolemy or a cause. The blog's only nearby mention is the Alfonsine Tables, and that is about van Langren's cipher, not the longitude error.
- Crossref record for 10.1198/tast.2010.09154: 200, metadata only, pp. 174-184, 9 citing works. Its 7 reference DOIs resolve to titles. The only cartography one (Keuning 1956, *Imago Mundi*) is on tandfonline, which is blocked.
- PMC: 5 searches gave 6 hits, and I fetched all 6 through the OAI endpoint (200 each). PMC10960004 cites the paper only in its reference list, which also gives 174-184. PMC9286359 mentions "redrafted Ptolemaic mappae" in an Atlantic context. Neither states the eastward error or that later tables inherited it, and the other 4 hits are unrelated.
- datavis.ca: DNS failure. www.datavis.ca, including verdadera.pdf: proxy 403. 15 more archive and library hosts: proxy 403 each.
- Langren1644.csv has Ptolemy's own value, 27.787. Under the stop rule that counts as "Ptolemy's own value only", not evidence that later tables inherited it.

**Believed, not checked**
- From memory and unverified: Friendly et al. 2010 discusses where the error came from. If the founder supplies the PDF and it gives no cause, the answer is "our sources don't say", which is what c11 already tells the learner.
- The CRAN and GitHub copies of Langren.Rd have different hashes. I did not diff them, but neither gives a cause.

**Confidence**
- High that none of the 31 routes has the sentence.
- Low on whether the sentence exists anywhere.
- The lesson needs no change: c11 is verified and honest as it stands.

**Side findings**
- The batch file gives the wrong citation. It says "Friendly, Valdez-Rodríguez & Valero-Mora"; Crossref says Friendly, Valero-Mora & Ibáñez Ulargui. The founder ask in the note uses the Crossref form.
- Pages 174-184 now come from two sources (Crossref and PMC10960004's reference list), against 185-191 in the HistData Rd. This backs pass 53's advisory on c7.

**Next, with owner role**
- Chief of staff: record W-1045 and W-1026's rome item as "blocked on founder ask F-<n>", not as open retries. File the ask text from the note, together with B2's if B2 also ends "not reachable". The ask offers two options: (a) put the PDFs of the 2010 paper and the 1644 *Verdadera* translation in the repo; (b) allow-list www.tandfonline.com, tandfonline.com, datavis.ca and www.datavis.ca. The note only lists the options and does not ask for the permission change itself.

- **a2f14c3 (engine change), in `src/components/lifehacks/HomeLesson.tsx`:**

    - coiled-cord "r=10cm" and "3.18 turns of 200cm"
    - shoes "24 cm"
    - fitted-sheet "32 cm"
    - socks "600 cm³ empty"
  - **Jacket picture (W-1299).** With no mode in effect, jacket-last-first now draws an empty bag with the items beside it in use order, with no arrows and no highlight.
  - **Cord fix (W-1241).** "Tumble 3 m" now reaches both the `short` and `long` milestones, so either press order unlocks the reveal.

- **1b5fa53:** group-cables loose ends are drawn as plain dots instead of highlighted targets while locked. It is its own commit so it can be reverted alone (see the safety point below).
- **110ac21 (tests):**
  - **New locked-stage test.** `tests/lifehacks/home-locked.test.mjs` renders the real stages with react-dom/server (test-only `render-loader.mjs` and `render-spies.mjs`), so it checks the actual markup rather than a copy of the strings. It covers the locked-picture rule, the jacket and group-cables pictures, and the cord press order.
  - **W-1247.** `engines-v2.test.mjs` now checks the Home answer is in range. `home-v2.test.mjs` adds a W3 every-step sweep over 10 slugs; long-cord is pinned to its own stage.
- **387ab8c:** the readiness addendum `/home/user/s3c-eng1/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-lh-home-locked-stage-addendum.md` (rollback is one revert of the `--no-ff` merge), plus a line in `company/ops/changelog.md`.

- **No v1 lesson changed.** I rendered all 69 Home lessons in 5 states (345 snapshots) before and after. 12 changed, all of them the locked or pre-press states of the 6 lessons above. 0 of the 41 v1 lessons changed, and no A, B or reveal state changed.
- **Tests:** `npm run test:lifehacks` gives 130/130. Against the old HomeLesson.tsx, the new test file fails 7 of 9.
- **Mutations** (each failed the suite, then was reverted):

- **Typecheck and check:** `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. `npm run check` passes (969 lessons, 5295 claims, 3 unrelated disputed-claim warnings).
- **Build:** `tools/serve.sh` has no `build` subcommand, so I ran `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-eng1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 npx next build`. It exited 0 in 4m41s at load about 13 on 4 cores, with 969 of 969 lesson pages. The build rewrote tsconfig.json; I reverted it and the tree is clean.

  - box "42 cm opening"
  - desk "4m one-way"
  - cord "0.3 m strings" and "3 m strings"

  If PE-ops counts those as givens, the total is 6 and the stop-if fires. The addendum puts that question to PE-ops.

It asks for 2 agents, both builders, running in parallel. All five behavioral check scripts pass, and `npm run check` passes with 4 warnings. One of them is saved-or-die's disputed claim, which B1 fixes.

**Scope note:** mgr4 said to write only the batch file. Your message said to write the decisions in my own files, so I also edited, inside my scope: `company/domains/briefs/behavioral.md`, `company/domains/behavioral.md` and three check scripts (`company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-gain-loss-framing.mjs`, `-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs`, `-allais-certainty-effect.mjs`). Everything went in one commit by explicit path. I did not touch board.json, progress.md, events.jsonl or founder-inbox.json.

**Decisions (each is written in the brief or charter):**
- **W-1315 and W-1306, saved-or-die (accepted).** The fact-checker's tie finding is right: both programmes have the same expected value, so the old wording proved nothing.
  - The predict now gives someone's two choices with "prefers" and asks whether one outcome model fits both. The misconception is option 1, nothing in the question rules it out, and the answer is listed last.
  - The mixed reveal branches start "Unless the two were a toss-up for you…".
  - The consistent branches now name the framing effect, and the recall is rebuilt the same way.
  - The key becomes "■ = alive · □ = die", and the lesson goes to version 2.
  - The "people do switch" sentence (c5) stays cut: there is no type (d) statement yet, and it would push the reveal to 109 words.
- **W-1306, zero-loses (accepted; this reverses my round-3 decision).** "Between the other two" is a middle-option cue, and option C's stated average let a learner compute the answer. The fix:
  - Neither the predict nor the recall options carry a gloss now.
  - "Equilibrium" moves into the question.
  - The answer is listed last.
  - The lesson goes to version 2.
  - "seed 2" stays on the stage because the fact-checker requires it for seeded simulations.
- **New finding (mine).** Once the kit's longer "Not quite: it was …" verdict is counted, sure-million's matched reveal branches come to 95 and 93 words, over the 90 limit. The earlier QA path only saw "Your prediction held." I shortened both branches to 89 and 87. Rule 7 is sharpened, and the scripts now add the longer verdict to every branch.
- **W-1321.** Same-week's objective drops its "real payments" sentence.
- **W-1293.** Neither held c6 line returns in any form. No opened source supports the certainty-effect line, and same-week's longest branch already measures 90.
- **W-1304.** The fold floor stays at 14 on sourcing, since none of the three newly sourced concepts is contested. It is final only after the fact-checker's type (d) statement (W-975). The automatic-escalation reserve can meet the Books sign-off condition (B6) by saying neither opt-in nor default.

How sure I am: high on the tie fix, the word counts and the held-line decisions, which are all script-checked. Medium that the new predicts close the giveaways; learner review round 2 will test that.

**Items, in run order:**
1. **B1, demo-builder, build, worktree:** saved-or-die v2 (W-1315, W-1306).
2. **B2, demo-builder, build, worktree, parallel with B1:** zero-loses v2 predict and recall; sure-million matched branches shortened; same-week objective (W-1306, W-1321).

Both carry `[project:behavioral-econ]`, are checked by lane 10, and do their own production build.

**Standing orders:** SO-1beh-1 renewed unchanged (expires 2026-10-20). No new one, because revision builds are not standing-order work.

**Asks to other lanes:**
- **Chief of staff:** rebuild the shared review server after B1 and B2 merge. 5b2fee7 predates the pilot revisions merged at 716cb5a. On the board: W-1293 and W-1304 to done; W-1306, W-1315 and W-1321 to done as decisions (their builds are B1 and B2).
- **Lane 10:** fact-check the changed claims plus same-week c3, run learner review r2 on saved-or-die and zero-loses, and QA all four lessons. All are walkthrough-first on the shared server, and SO-10-1/2/3 trigger (b) should cover them. Also learner review r1 for briefs 1-2 if not yet done. The fact-checker should write the W-975 type (d) statement, covering W-1059 and W-1316, and spot-open the W-1063 passages.

Both lessons are revised to v2 and set back to draft, in the same commit as the version bump. Both fit the 390x844 phone (crop 0, phoneFit true) and pass local contract QA, 4/4. For cut-the-busiest-link I took the item's fallback: no network can show the "stale list" claim while keeping the prediction and the lesson's ending. **Changed** (worktree /home/user/s3c-wj3, branch wj-rev-r3, not pushed)
- Commit 5d86720: both Demo.tsx, styles.module.css and meta.json files (version 2, status draft, claim resets). The commit body maps each r14 finding to fixed or departure-for-cm.
- Commit 3c6f206: changes to pass the phone-fit check, and dated v2 entries in both build.md files. Each entry has a finding table, Pre-flight v2, the reveal-fit output and the QA result.
- Files:
  - /home/user/s3c-wj3/src/demos/ai/calibrated-but-unequal-alarms/{Demo.tsx,styles.module.css,meta.json}
  - /home/user/s3c-wj3/src/demos/cs/cut-the-busiest-link/{Demo.tsx,styles.module.css,meta.json}

  - /home/user/s3c-wj3/company/reviews/cut-the-busiest-link/build.md
- Released both queue claims with `claim.mjs release --done` (lock files in the main checkout).

**calibrated-but-unequal-alarms**
- Finding 1 (slider), fixed: the slider is now labelled "Reoffenders in B" and reads B's base rate (23/32/41/50). The ringed count follows in the group header. I relabelled rather than splitting the control because a separate ringing control would break the score's 80/20 rule. That would change what the lesson teaches, so relabelling is the smaller change. The reason is recorded in build.md.
- Finding 2 (counts in words), fixed: the headers say "A: 50 ringed" / "B: 20 ringed", and the reoffender counts show from the locked frame.
- Finding 3 ("imperfect score"), fixed: the reveal now says "Otherwise no score that makes mistakes is calibrated with equal errors." It also adds "The slider changed B's people, not the score."
- Ring colours note, fixed: a key under the picture explains both rings.
- Middle-value note (optional), not done.
- Claims: c1–c4 reset to unverified, c6 is new and unverified, c5 is unchanged and still verified.

**cut-the-busiest-link**
- Finding 1, fixed: every node shows its number.
- Finding 2, fixed: whenever a count is fractional, the stage says "Each pair counts 1, split evenly over its tied shortest paths." This puts c5's second clause on screen.
- Finding 3, departure-for-cm: in my node script the once-ranked list and the recount make the same first two cuts (5-6, then 3-7). The first difference is at cut 3, after the split: the recount picks 0-1 at 3.5, while the stale list picks 0-3, which now carries 2.5.
  - Any network that keeps two bridges at 12 either agrees with the recount up to the split, or the recount cuts inside a group first, which changes the lesson's ending. So I made no network change and cut the sentence instead.
  - The reveal now says "The Girvan–Newman method cuts the busiest link, recounts every link, and repeats."
  - The numbers and this reasoning are in build.md.
- Claims: c4 and c5 reset to unverified; c1–c3 are unchanged and still verified.

**Checked on disk**
- Phone fit: `node tools/reveal-fit.mjs --url http://localhost:4111 <both> --shots --out …` gave pass 2, thumb 0, cropped 0, phoneFit 2.
  - calibrated: fit, crop 0, 85 words.
  - cut: fit, crop 0, 72 words.
- QA: `QA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4111 QA_ONLY=… npx playwright test tests/qa/contract.spec.ts --workers=2` gave 4 passed.
- `npm run check`: passed (969 lessons, 3 warnings, none from these two lessons). `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The production build (NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-wj3) exited 0.
- My node port of rates() matches the verified c2/c3 numbers, so no verified number changed.
- The meta.json files show version 2 and draft, and the claim statuses are as listed above.
- Stage word count is at most 25 in calibrated (25 at the busiest frame) and at most 18 in cut.
- tsconfig.json is reverted, the server is stopped, the dist dir is deleted and the working tree is clean.

**Believed, not checked**
- A beginner will now read the slider as changing group B rather than a flagging choice.
- The 11-unit SVG labels in calibrated land at about 10 px when the card fits the picture to 190 px at the reveal. That is at the 10 px floor; I judged it from the screenshot only.
- The first cut of the reveal-fit runs came back at crop 37 px and 103 words. My reveal word cuts in calibrated removed no idea, but cm-ai may want to look at them.
- reveal-fit counted a 16 px key icon as "the picture" (thumb), because it skips the main svg once the card marks it data-reveal-fit. I removed the viewBox from the icons. That tool behaviour may be worth a platform-engineer note.

**Confidence:** high on the mechanics, fit and QA. Medium that the r15 re-walk passes calibrated. Medium-low that cut fully answers the misconception, given the departure.

**Next, with owner role** (please add these to the board)
1. learner-evaluator: r15 re-walk of both v2 lessons, artifact first (ask A1).
2. fact-checker: calibrated c1–c4 and c6, cut c4 and c5 (lane 10).
3. cm-cs (ask A4): decide on the departure. Either accept the narrower lesson, or add a third-cut step after the split; the numbers are in build.md.
4. Chief of staff: merge wj-rev-r3 and move W-1265.

**Not done:** the optional middle-value visit in calibrated. No push, no deploy. I did not edit the board, progress.md or events (single writer is the chief of staff).

- **Server:** BUILT_FROM and `git -C /home/user/s3c-qa rev-parse HEAD` were both 5b2fee71701e8645e3cd6e2fde60bcea004833e8 at start and end, and :3591 returned HTTP 200.

- **Tag:** asthma is in the `ai` domain, and none of its commit subjects match wave-j's patterns (checked case-sensitive and case-insensitive), so it is `[project:catalog]`.
- **After my commit:** the selector no longer prints asthma (grep exit 1). The record has exactly one `Verdict:` line, `Verdict: revise`. `npm run check` passed (969 lessons, 4 warnings, none mine).

- I read meta.json `learner` and `version` before walking, then wrote the findings from the transcript (cut at the appendix) and sheet.png.

- **Blocking finding:** the predict card says outright that asthma patients all got intensive care and that the model sends low-risk patients to the ward. So a learner who reasons well rules out 4% and picks "About 8%, like others". The reveal tells them "Not quite: it was 20%" and explains only why the answer is not 4%. Nothing seen in the walk says why asthma patients die more than the others once they are on the ward.
- **From the code, not seen on screen:** Demo.tsx (lines 76-80) does have a line, "Ward risk: asthma 20%, others 8%. Intensive care: asthma 4%." body:
## B1 report (cm-history): done, pushed

B1 is complete. Briefs 5, 3, 4 and 12 are released in that order. Brief 11 is re-scripted but still skipped. Briefs 23 and 24 have their v2 specs, so B4 can start. One problem in the shared checkout needs the chief of staff: another session's crashed rebase reverted the whole `company/domains/briefs/checks/` directory and left a stale `.git/rebase-merge/`. Details under "Shared checkout incident".

### Changed
One commit in the main checkout, **8bdf821** (b60450b before the rebase), pushed to origin/ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. Author cm-history, committed by explicit path.

- `company/domains/briefs/history.md`:

  - Sections 5, 3, 4 and 12 carry "Ready to claim (cm-history, 2026-10-16)". Section 5 states the priority order and is moved before section 3.
  - Section 11 is rewritten and the old draft removed.
  - Section 12 is renamed, with a pointer.
  - Sections 23 and 24 have v2 specs edited in place, and 23 lists the v1 to v2 differences.
- `content/curriculum/history.json`: brief 4's concept is now named "Disease killed about eight times as many as wounds: deaths in British army hospitals in the East".
- `company/ops/brief-skips.json`: the skip lines for 5, 3, 4 and 12 are removed. The disaster-deaths-fell line is re-worded to name its three conditions. The britain line stays, because B2 has not merged.

### Checked on disk
- `history-cycle1-check.mjs`: all checks pass. Section 11 gives 523,942 and 53,720 a year, ×9.75, ×3.74, ×36.5, droughts 90%, and 1931 at 3,718,976. These are all P5's numbers.
- `history-cycle2-check.mjs` for 23, for 24, and for the full run: all pass, with letters A6 B6 C6.

- `npm run check` passes (969 lessons, 4 warnings, none of them History).

### Decisions and findings beyond the item (all recorded in r15)
- **Literacy question.** "Around 1830, French army conscripts who could read and write averaged 39% across 86 departments. How many departments were within 5 points of 39%?" Options: A) About 3 in 4 / B) About 1 in 6 / C) About 1 in 50. Answer B.
  - 15 of 86 departments are within the band (14 against the unrounded 39.26), so the stop-if did not fire.
  - A new first preset, "Within 5 points of 39%", replaces Seine, so there are still four presets.
- **Schooling outlier.** Department 75 sits at 73.1 per 100,000. Without it, the most-literate quarter is ×1.44 the least literate, not ×1.7, and r = 0.35.
  - I kept ×1.7 and answer C, because the direction holds without it.
  - I made the outlier label required.
  - Confidence: medium.
- **Brief 11 wording.** The question is trimmed from 28 to 24 words. In the reveal, "population grew 3.7 times" is replaced by "Per million people, that is about 36 times fewer" (93 words would have broken the cap; now 88). The cultural reviewer has to confirm this.

### Believed, not checked

**The board's W-1337 fix would cause the same wipe again.** I tested it in a scratch repo with the host's git 2.43.0. Git creates the autostash *before* it runs the pre-rebase hook. When a refusing hook exits 1, the edits go into the autostash (in `.git/rebase-merge/autostash`) and the working tree is reset. That stash is not on `git stash list`, and `git rebase --abort` fails. `git pull --rebase` with `rebase.autoStash` set behaves the same way. The main checkout's `stash@{0}` ("orphaned-autostash-1306-rebase-merge") fits this. In the same scratch repo, a hook that refuses but first runs `git stash store` and `git stash apply --index` on that autostash sha, then removes the state dir, got back both staged and unstaged edits. B1 is written that way, and the objection is in the batch header.

**Items in run order.** All are tools-lead, kind `other`, worktree yes, `[project:maintenance]`, and none is a builder (6 agents, 0 builders).

**Changed:** I added a "Fold toggle look" subsection at the end of company/design/system.md, under "Fold at the reveal". It is committed as b9e2312, by explicit path only. I did not pull, rebase, stash or push, and I did not touch the B1 spec, code or any single-writer files.

**What the subsection says:**
- **Base:** kit `.control` styling, border `--line`, fill `--bg-2`.
- **Colours:** label and chevron are `--fg` (no hex anywhere), and `--domain` is used for the focus ring.
- **Size:** full stage width, min-height 44 px.
- **Chevron:** a 12x8 inline SVG that replaces the "▾" glyph. It points down when collapsed and rotates 180° to point up when expanded. The rotation takes 150 ms, with no transition under reduced motion.
- **Labels:** "Show more controls", "Show controls" and "Hide controls".
- **Versus a caption:** a caption is muted text with no box and about 20 px tall. The toggle has a boundary, is 44 px tall, spans the stage and uses `--fg`. It is the only full-width single button, so it can't be read as a Row option.
- **Mockup:** one inline SVG and one ASCII drawing, both at 390 px.
- **Note to platform-engineer:** the changes to `FoldToggle` in controls.tsx and to globals.css.

**Checked on disk:**
- The check command `npm run check` passed: "check passed: 969 lessons, 5297 claims, 99 roles, 6 warning(s)". The warnings are disputed claims on lifehacks lessons, not mine.

body:
The quality team is now part of First Light and holds its own go/no-go key. I've added this as Amendment 1 to the First Light decision record, and it's in the charter and the war room.
- **Who:** Hilde, the evaluation steward, with QA testing, accessibility, fact-checking, learner review and pedagogy critique.
- **Two keys at go/no-go:** Hilde's **quality** go/no-go, and Beatriz's recommendation on scope, schedule and readiness. A quality no-go stops the launch. Only you can overrule it, in writing, with the objection on record.
- **What the bar covers:**
  - full QA on the exact release build, including the new parts: accounts, progress, personalization, mastery, social and the ad slot;
  - accessibility;
  - every claim in the launch lessons verified, with no internal notes visible;
  - learner reviews of the new parts;
  - the phone-fit and page-weight budgets;
  - no open serious incidents.

  Privacy stays its own gate, and so does engineering readiness.
- **Deadlock objection:** two keys could deadlock on launch day. The answer is to fix the bar early, and to run a quality dry run at T-7 (16 Nov) so failures show while there's time to fix them.

Hilde is now writing the bar (`company/initiatives/first-light/quality-bar.md`). She'll set the date it freezes, list the tests she'll need and the review capacity, and give her written view on Beatriz's role. She was only informed about that role before, and the go/no-go now touches her gates.

**The Project Review 1 budget pack is ready** (Odette). Headlines:
- **First Light:** 3.6M tokens to 23 Oct for design and estimates, then 8.2M to launch, 11.8M in total. Money is about $21–100 a month: Vercel Pro, the domain, and the database, auth and monitoring tiers, all unverified until we have quotes. The second tranche is released only if Kenji's re-estimate comes in under 10.2M. If not, cuts come in this order: ad slot, then social, then challenges.
- **Behavioral economics:** 1.8M for the pilot and 4.0M for the 30 lessons after it, about 2.5× Selin's figure for the pilot. Odette says category set-up costs more than Selin counted.
- **History:** 2.5M for tranche 1 now, with tranche 2 not asked yet.
- **Scaling pilot:** 2.45M, plus GitHub Pro at about $4 a month.
- **Cost per lesson:** a correction. It's 122k tokens per published lesson, not 101k, because the event log had missed 115 runs.

The First Light budget isn't approved yet, so the tools won't let First Light build work start until Project Review 1 decides. Today's work is scoping only.

body:
I've recorded the new org as your decision (`company/decisions/2026-10-15-founder-press-sibling-company.md`), and Leonie is now building it. She runs org design in the CEO office.

**The structure, as you described it:**
- **VP of Books**, reporting to you. Owns strategy, execution, vision and the portfolio directly, for every book you write.
  - **Head of Book: *System 3*.** Each future book gets its own head, managed by the VP. Reporting to this head:
    - writer
    - development editor
    - copy editor and proofreader
    - fact-checker
    - marketing strategist
    - experiment developer
    - two software engineers (the demos, and publishing on your blog)
  - **Shared across all books, under the VP:**
    - art director
    - release manager (versions r1, r2, …)
    - a **review panel**: arc, easter eggs, narrative momentum, LLM tells, prose quality, fun, thought-provoking ideas, and comparison with other books
- **A floor in HQ** for it.

**Choices I made for you, which you can change:**
1. **Working name: "System 3 Press".** You choose the real name.
2. **The agents live in your book's repo** (`hanialshater/system3`), next to the manuscript and the editorial tools already there: the `ai-tells` skill, the easter-egg register and its check script, the LLM-tell checker, the working spine and your past evaluations. HQ in System 3 Company shows the floor from a snapshot, so the two companies stay separate.
3. **It doesn't inherit System 3 Company's constitution, lesson gates or board.** It gets its own short operating rules. Two of your rules still apply: nothing is published to your blog without your approval, and objections travel with decisions.
4. **You are the author.** The writer and editors propose, and you accept. Nothing is merged into the manuscript without you. Chapter 13 stays protected, and your unaccepted review comments stay. Reviewers write review records; they never edit chapters.

**Objections recorded with the decision:**
- Both companies share this 4-CPU machine and one token pool. Until the press has its own limits, its agents count toward the same caps.
- Some roles exist on both sides, such as the fact-checker and release manager. They share tools but stay separate roles, because the products and the gates differ.

When Leonie reports, the HQ engineer builds the floor, and I'll show you the org chart and anything to rename.

The **AMD-001 (c2) amendment is ready for your signature**. It's the fix that cuts the feed's first-load JavaScript from 2.7 MB to about 230 KB and stops internal notes reaching browsers. Hilde, the evaluation steward, re-tested it on today's 960 lessons and found two gaps:

**What you'd be signing:**
1. **You ratify part (c2) only, with the six safeguards.** The registry generator moves to `tools/registry.mjs`, and `check` enforces the safeguards. Parts (a), (b), (c1) and (d) stay unratified.

3. **The remaining objections stay open on record,** each with a trigger that would bring it back. The main one, O3: once AMD-001 reads "ratified", the commit label that marks an AMD-001 change would also count as permission for its unratified parts. Hilde's mitigation:
   - you write the status line yourself;
   - she audits the commit that applies it;
   - the status then changes to "applied in part".

   The real fix is a later amendment, AMD-003.
4. **Deploying the result needs your separate approval.**

The signature block is under "Decision" in `company/constitution/amendments/AMD-001-earn-the-reveal-and-tooling.md`. Hilde verified the safeguards by testing them. - It uses a throwaway local database. No real email is sent, because the sign-in link is captured in the test instead.
- It has to build and run with **sign-in switched off and no account settings at all**, which is how production stays until you approve go-live.

body:
Some of each. The agents are real, separate runs, but the org around them is thinner than the HQ floor plan suggests. Every agent is the same underlying AI model, and I'm the one who starts them all.

**What's real**
- **Separate runs.** Each agent (the fact-checker, a builder, Leonie and so on) is its own run of the model, with its own fresh context. It starts from its role file, the brief I write, and whatever it reads in the repository.
- **Real work on disk.** The lessons, code, reviews and commits are actually written by those runs, and they cost real tokens. Last night alone was dozens of runs.
- **Genuine independence of context.** An evaluator never sees the builder's reasoning, and a checker re-derives the numbers itself. The independence is real in that sense.
- **They catch real mistakes, including mine.** Tonight: the wrong verdict word in my brief, my wrong Neon setup step, a builder's stray config edit, and the accidental r7 deploy marker.

**What's thinner than the org chart suggests**
- **One model, many hats.** "Leonie", "Beatriz" and "Rasmus" are role files with names, not different minds. Mistakes can be correlated, because the same model is reviewing its own kind of work. The structure helps, but it isn't the same as independent people.
- **I'm the hub.** Agents can't talk to each other or start each other. Every handoff goes through files, or through me relaying a report. Your new rule is right about this: I've been choosing most of the work. "Asking the manager" now means a real manager run decides, but I still carry the request.
- **No memory between runs.** A role remembers nothing except what's written in the repository.
- **Some rituals are really me.** I write the founder digests, the board updates, many decision records, and much of the merging myself, "as" the chief of staff. Project Review 1 had no real quorum; the record says so. Earlier I ran two roles through a generic agent because their agent types didn't exist yet.
- **The only human is you.** "Founder approval" is the one real external check.

**What would make it more real**
- **Let managers dispatch their own teams.** Leonie is designing this now, so I stop being the bottleneck.
- **Use different models for checking.** Checkers and evaluators could run on a different model than builders, to cut correlated errors.
- **Get real learners.** No real learner has used a lesson yet (that experiment, EXP-002, hasn't run). Until then, "a lesson teaches well" means simulated learners think so.

Would you like me to have Leonie include the different-models-for-checking idea in her proposal?

**Social: the "prediction swap".** A signed-in learner aged 16 or over can send a friend a lesson with their own first guess sealed inside it.
- The friend plays the lesson normally, and sees the sender's guess only after their own reveal. They can send one back with a single tap.

Its learning prediction: lessons played through a swap should be remembered at least 4 points better at the first revisit. The designer is only about 35% confident of that, and says plainly that share links alone might be the better release 1.

**Challenges.** A challenge is 3 to 5 related lessons from one category. It counts as finished only when each lesson's recall question has been answered at least a day later. There's no timer, no points and no streaks. If it isn't working on a preview by 6 Nov, it's cut automatically.

Then the most valuable thing we made overnight may not be lessons. It may be evidence for the book. Several things happened that fit the fallible-agents thesis directly:

| What happened | The book's idea it tests | The mechanism that caught it |
|---|---|---|
| A stray "[deploy]" in a commit body shipped r7 before your approval | Good intentions don't work, mechanisms do: the rule "never write the marker" lived only in memory | The correction of error (COE) traced it to the trigger design, not the agent. Now there's a structural fix and a guard. |
| I briefed six reviewers with a verdict word the tools don't accept | The coordinator is as fallible as the workers | One reviewer read its own role file, not my brief, and corrected me |
| I told you to connect Neon to Development and Preview | The authority is fallible too | The backend engineer's independent read caught it before any data existed |
| A builder said it had reverted a config edit, but it hadn't | Agent testimony isn't truth | Checking the diff on disk, not the report |
| The test author wrote tests, then the ops reviewer planted 12 bugs of its own | Falsification over confirmation | Separate contexts, adversarial checks |
| A two-layout highlight looked like a bug | Conjecture, then test | QA clicked the buttons and found the state was right and only the styling wrong |
| You saw that I'd become the bottleneck | Scalable oversight needs single-threaded owners, as at Amazon | Your new rule: managers decide each lane, and Leonie owns the org |

The off-boarding summaries you mention are what make "same model, different rules" work. Each agent dies, but its report, records and the board carry its context to the next role. Without them the org would just be one model forgetting.

Under your new rule, that goes to the Press's VP of Books, who decides whether the System 3 book's experiment developer writes it up. body:
The mastery design (EDD-009) is drafted, and it adds no new data: mastery is worked out in the browser from what's already stored. A lesson moves through five states:

| State | What the learner sees |
|---|---|
| Not played | "Not played yet" |
| Played | "Played" |
| Recalled | "Recalled N days later" |
| Held | "Recalled twice, D days apart": two correct recalls at least a week apart |
| Look again | "Revisited, worth another look", after a wrong recall |

It sticks to the no-streaks rule. Time passing never drops a lesson's state; only a wrong answer does. Making a prediction earns no credit.

body:
I've put that at the centre of the System 3 Meta brief as its thesis. It's a new section 1a in `company/sibling/system3-meta/founder-brief.md`, quoted in your words.

Science works without trusting any one scientist, and System 3 borrows that machinery so fallible agents can produce reliable work together. The brief maps each part of science to what this company already does:

| Science | Here |
|---|---|
| Public, citable claims | Every sentence a learner sees is a claim with a source |
| Peer review | Builders never verify their own work; reviewers see the lesson before the builder's notes |
| Falsification | Reviewers plant bugs to test the tests; every decision says what would prove it wrong |
| Open criticism | Objections travel with decisions; "noted" isn't an answer |
| The literature | The disk is the memory: decisions, handoffs, the progress log |
| Error correction | Post-incident reviews fix the mechanism, not the person; each retro checks whether the last one's changes worked |
| Independent observers | Separate roles today; separate models next |

The test it sets for any new role, rule or generated company: does it make errors easier to find and cheaper to correct, without relying on anyone being right?

By that standard, two institutions are still weak here:
- **Independent observers.** Every agent is the same model, so they can share the same mistakes. This is why the brief makes running checkers on another model the first step of decoupling from Claude.
- **Contact with reality.** Science works because experiments can come out the way nobody expected. We have no real learners yet, so every signal is our own judgement. That's the strongest case for First Light, and for requiring each generated company to fix an outside measure of success before it starts.

The evaluation steward's audit has turned up a problem I caused. **Of the 217 lessons marked "Ready to publish", 197 have a latest QA record that the QA tester didn't demonstrably make.**
- **155 came from my own integration run on one build** (de22974). The tool stamped every record "recorded by: qa-tester" whoever ran it, so they looked independent.
- **40 can't be attributed either way**, because the dispatch log was dark at the time.

That breaks our rule that work is checked by someone other than whoever produced it. No unchecked lesson has reached learners, since nothing has been published since r7. But "Ready to publish" overstates what has really been checked.

What I've put in motion:
- **Re-QA by the QA tester:** the 197, then 32 more blocked on other gates, under the quality lane's standing order (W-1235). Until that's done, no publish relies on integration-only QA, including the 15 Wave J and 7 History lessons that just moved to review. That rule is now the release manager's to confirm (W-1237).
- **The tool fix is drafted as amendment AMD-010.** The record is stamped from the real author; integration runs get their own label and don't count as QA evidence. It goes to constitutional review (W-1236). The steward who wrote it can't approve it, and nor can I, the QA tester or the release manager.
- **Kudos to the QA tester.** It flagged its own tool mistake on 10-14, and that's what exposed the stamp defect.

**Capacity:** the next builder (behavioral brief 3) is still held by the load guard, at 9.8 against a limit of 8, and starts when the current builds finish. Eight agents are running. The rebuilt re-QA queue is about 15 runs, so QA capacity is now the real limit on publishing.
