body:
I ruled on EDD-009 Q1 and Q3, gave each ruling a testable fixture, and committed and pushed the record (d3e78e7). `npm run check` passed.

**Rulings**
- **Q1: strict.** `held` now needs two right answers at least 7 days apart, and both must come after the latest wrong recall. A wrong answer breaks the pair. `recalled` still comes back on the next right answer.
  - Why: the wrong answer is evidence against the span, and the revisit card shows the right answer and the `why` line after a wrong pick. So the lenient "Recalled twice, 10 days apart" says more than was measured. It rests on AMD-008 M7; M3 still holds.
  - Fixture Q1-a (completedAt = 0): recalls day 1 right, day 4 wrong, day 11 right → `recalled`, "Recalled 11 days later". The draft would give `held`, "Recalled twice, 10 days apart".
- **Q3: keep both.** The internal id `held` is acceptable only if it never reaches learner copy: no rendered text may contain "held", "mastered" or "mastery". "Recalled twice, {D} days apart" stays as the learner sentence, with D measured on the post-wrong pair. I rejected a "{k} times" count because a number that rises with visits reads as a score (M5, Q4.2). It rests on M7 and X2/Q3.4.
  - Fixture Q3-a: recalls day 1, 4, 11 and 32, all right → `held`, exactly "Recalled twice, 31 days apart", with none of the three words in the rendered string.

**Changed**
- One new file, `/home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/_pedagogy/2026-10-16-edd-009-q1-q3.md`. It holds both ruling lines, a replacement `held` row for §3.3, the two fixtures and findings F1 and F2.
- Commit d3e78e7 (75187ba before the rebase), author pedagogy-critic, committed by explicit path, rebased and pushed to ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1.

**Checked on disk**
- The revisit card shows the right answer after a wrong pick: `src/components/Feed.tsx`, lines 271 and 279-283.
- The schedule: `src/kit/progress.ts`, lines 48-57. It waits `REVISIT_SCHEDULE_DAYS[successes]` after the last recall, a wrong answer does not add to `successes`, and revisits stop at 4 right answers. I played this through by hand: after day 1 right and day 4 wrong, both rules reach `held` on day 14.
- The B4 stop condition was not met. The ruling uses only `recalls[].at` and `.correct`, which EDD-009 already reads, so nothing goes to B3's §5 question.

**Believed, not checked**
- That learners read "Recalled twice, D days apart" as a true statement of what happened and not as a score. Only the learner-evaluator's Q4.2 probe can test that.
- I did not read principal-engineer's review, as the brief said. There is no walkthrough for a design document, so the evidence was the table and the code.

**Confidence**

- About 70% that the Q3 sentence survives as written.

  - F1: after a wrong answer, "Recalled N days later" still counts N from first play, although the learner was re-shown the answer. In Q1-a the copy says 11 days when the learner last saw the answer on day 4.
  - F2: under the strict rule, a wrong answer after the third right one can cap a lesson at `recalled` for good, because no further revisits are scheduled. Changing that means changing `revisitDue` in `src/kit/progress.ts`, which is protected, so it needs an amendment.

I couldn't find an item-level source for either line. Both are partly sourced at best. For line one, the item-level source I did find points against it. Both lines stay cut; this run changed no claim's status.

**Changed**
- New note: /home/user/system-3-company/company/research/notes/2026-10-16-w902-item-level-sources.md

**Checked on disk**
- **PMC's open-access full-text service still works.** Every paper I asked for came back with status 200 between 12:19 and 12:25Z. The one exception was PMC13428879, which returned 400 because it is not in that set.
- **The file hashes in the note will reproduce, with one step.** Each response carries a timestamp that changes on every fetch. I fetched PMC9337702 twice and the two files were identical once that timestamp was removed. The note's hashes are taken with it removed and give the command.
- **Line one (Ruggeri 2020, certainty effect; c6 in sure-million-or-long-shot):**
  - Cicerale 2022 (PMC9337702), Discussion: Ruggeri "completely replicated Prospects A-A’ and B-B’" (sure versus probable), but "in Prospect C Ruggeri could not replicate the effect originally found by K&T in the gain domain".
  - Their Table 1 defines Prospect C as 20% of €4000 against 25% of €3000. That is half of Kahneman and Tversky's common-ratio certainty-effect pair.
  - The lesson's own pair (Allais common-consequence) does not appear in their problem set.
  - Tan 2021 (PMC7929998) gives only "94% of the items" replicated, without saying which.
  - Binz & Schulz 2023 (PMC9963545) plots Ruggeri's certainty-effect result for humans, but only as a figure. The image host returned 403.
  - Verdict: partly sourced, and the item-level part cuts against the line.
- **Line two (Augenblick 2015, "with real payments"; c6 in same-week-a-year-apart):**
  - I read all 9 mentions in Cohen 2020 (PMC10489299) plus footnote 17. None says the money was really paid.
  - Chakraborty 2017 (PMC5545082) says "monetary payments" and subjects "allocate both cash and units of effort". It also says "present bias is found only in the effort domain", which is stronger than Cohen's "much weaker (but still statistically significant)".
  - Verdict: partly sourced. Effort clearer than money is supported; the words "real payments" are not.
- **Blocked routes, each with its status and time in the note:**
  - OSF preprint 2nyd6: it redirects to files.osf.io, which returned 403.
  - nature.com: redirects to idp.nature.com, 403.
  - Also 403: academic.oup.com, cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, zenodo, api.osf.io, pubmed.
  - GitHub repo marcelbinz/GPT3goesPsychology: the README opens (200) but lists no file paths, and the GitHub API refused access for this session. I did not guess file paths.
  - Crossref answered (200) but lists no supplementary file for either paper.

**Believed, not checked**
- That Cicerale's Prospect C matches Kahneman and Tversky 1979 Problem 4, and A/B match Problems 11/12 and 14. I matched the numbers from memory and marked it so in the note.
- That Augenblick 2015 paid real money. This is also from memory and marked; I did not open the paper.

**Confidence**
- High that no opened passage supports either line as worded.
- Medium on the Prospect C mapping.
- We don't know whether Ruggeri's own certainty-effect contrast was positive.

**Stop-if triggered.** This counts as a finding against the 2026-10-15 note's "robust" verdict for the certainty effect, so I wrote it up in section 3 and stopped the Ruggeri sweep. Before that, all 12 routes for line one had been tried.

**Next, with owner**

- **Fact-checker (routed by evaluation-steward):** open the quoted passages, confirm or reject the Prospect C mapping, and record c6 in both lessons as not checkable as worded.
- **cm-behavioral:** decide under brief rule 6 whether either line returns in another form. One candidate is "real effort" for present bias, as reported by the opened reviews.
- **Board (chief of staff):** W-902 can carry this note as the B2 result. The conditional founder ask now has an exact list in section 5, with two hosts added to the batch's list: files.osf.io and cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. No agent may make that ask on the founder's behalf.
- **B4:** can go ahead. PMC is reachable, so B4's "PMC unreachable" stop does not fire. Figure images in PMC papers can't be read, though.

One existing fold-lock test failed in two of three full `npm run test:dispatch` runs while host load was 14 to 18, and passed on the third.

**Changed** (all in commit 27d7e08, committed by explicit path as tools-lead):
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/tools/dispatch-check.mjs`:
  - New flag `--next-build`, usable with any kind, under a new rule P1. With the flag, a non-build kind gets C2: a dispatch that would make a 4th builder fails with `C2 builders (P1 --next-build): …`.
  - The `isBuilder` check that counts from the event log now also counts a dispatch whose summary contains `[next-build]` or whose subjects include `next-build`. I chose a bracketed marker so that prose mentioning the flag is not counted.
  - The result carries `nextBuild`, and the header and usage line are updated. Plain `--kind=check` behaves as before.
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/tools/build-slot.mjs` (new), with `acquire|release|status|run`:
  - A host-wide lock directory, `/tmp/s3c-build-slots` (override with `S3_BUILD_SLOTS`), holding `slot-1.json` to `slot-3.json`.
  - A slot is taken with `link(2)` of a fully written temp file, which gives the O_EXCL guarantee.
  - Each holder records its pid, the pid's start time, the command's pid, a label, cwd and start time. Holders whose pids are dead or reused are reaped.
  - When all 3 slots are held, it waits up to 20 minutes, then exits 1 listing the holders. It never signals another process.
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/tools/serve.sh`:
  - New `build <dist> [ENV=VAL…]`, which runs `npm run build` inside a slot. The CoS's :3591 rebuild becomes `tools/serve.sh build .next-3591 && tools/serve.sh start 3591 .next-3591`.
  - `S3_BUILD_CMD` swaps in a stand-in build command, for tests only.
  - `status` also lists the build slots.
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/tests/dispatch/build-slot.test.mjs` (new, 9 cases).
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-build-slot-guard.md`: the tier-1 self-check. It holds the CoS checklist line, the options paragraph for lane 10 on QA_ONLY, and where this branch meets the others.
- `/home/user/s3c-tg3/company/ops/changelog.md`: one new section at the top.

**Checked on disk:**
- New tests → `node --test tests/dispatch/build-slot.test.mjs` → 9/9 pass. They cover:
  - `--kind=check --next-build` refused with 3 builders in the fixture log, and plain `--kind=check` not refused.
  - With 3 stand-in holders, a 4th acquire waits at least 1 s, then fails listing all three.
  - A waiting acquire gets a slot when one is released.
  - A dead-pid holder is reported stale and reaped, with no leftover files.
  - A reused pid counts as stale.
  - `release --slot` refuses a live holder that belongs to someone else.
  - `serve.sh build` holds one slot during a stand-in build, passes the env and dist dir through, and releases after.
  - A `[next-build]` summary counts as a builder, and prose naming the flag does not.
- Full suite → `npm run test:dispatch` → 70/70 on the third run. The first two runs each had one failure, the existing test "F1 + F2: two fold loops in parallel…" in `fold-lock.test.mjs`. That file passes alone, 6/6, both with my change and with it stashed. My file is not involved, but its subprocesses add load while that test runs.
- Status command → `node tools/build-slot.mjs status` → "build slots: 0/3 held (/tmp/s3c-build-slots)".
- `npm run check` → "check passed: 969 lessons, 5293 claims, 99 roles, 8 warning(s)".
- No real `next build` was run. All builds in tests were stand-ins.

**Where the branches meet:**
- **tools-ledger (c73ddb9), unmerged:** both edit `tools/dispatch-check.mjs`. The conflicts are in the header comment, the usage line and `const result = …`; whichever branch merges second rebases. There is also one meaning-level conflict, written up for lane 10 in the record:
  - The ledger's `isBuilderSlot` (in `tools/lib/slots.mjs`) does not count `--next-build`.
  - The fix is two lines: record `nextBuild` on the slot draft and count it in `isBuilderSlot`.
  - C2 is never weakened in the meantime, because the S3 rule takes the largest of the three counts.
- **B1 (s3c-tg1) and B2 (s3c-tg2):** the only shared file is `changelog.md`, where all three branches add a top section, so expect a trivial conflict. B2 changes the internals of `events-spool.mjs`, which dispatch-check imports; I did not change those calls.

- The rule is named P1, so it does not clash with the batch's item B1.
- The lock directory is a fixed path, so every session sees the same lock whatever its TMPDIR.

- I left `npm run build` in package.json untouched. That is tier 2; it is listed in the record as an option for principal-engineer-ops.

**Believed, not checked:**
- Reaping is safe when two acquirers race. It is reasoned through in the code and tested only for a single reaper.
- The CoS can start an Agent description with `[next-build]` and it will reach the summary the hook writes. The hook keeps the first 100 characters of the description.

body:
**B4 (W-1063) is done.** All three topics have a verdict backed by at least one opened PMC source with an address, and none of the three is contested. On sourcing alone, the fold-floor evidence points to 14, not 10. That number is for cm-behavioral to decide; this note does not decide it.

**Changed**
- New note: /home/user/system-3-company/company/research/notes/2026-10-16-w1063-commitment-escalation-disposition.md
- Commit 508fada in the main checkout, committed by path with author research-scientist, rebased and pushed to ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1. The first push lost a race to another agent's push; the retry went through.
- Fetched files are in /home/user/system-3-company/artifacts/research-w1063/ (gitignored, not committed).
- No claim's status changed. No brief or lesson text was drafted.

**Checked on disk**
- PMC was reachable, so B4's stop-if did not fire. The OAI endpoint returned 200 for every id asked, 12:29-12:33Z. Four ids came back as 478-byte error records because they are not in the OAI set. All 15 PMC searches returned 200.
- The anchor primaries are not reachable. Crossref returns 200 for Ashraf, Karlan & Yin 2006, Thaler & Benartzi 2004 and Odean 1998, but it links only to publisher sites. The proxy refused all three publishers with 403: academic.oup.com, www.journals.uchicago.edu and onlinelibrary.wiley.com.
- For each of the 16 opened files used, the note records the sha256 (computed with `<responseDate>` removed, the same method as B2) and the byte size. Every quoted passage was copied from the fetched text.
- `npm run check`: passed (969 lessons, 5295 claims, 3 warnings that predate this run).

**Verdicts**
- **Commitment devices: with limits.**
  - The SEED headline (28% take-up, +411 pesos or 82% after one year, no longer significant at 2.5 years) is second-hand only, as reported by Karlan, Ratan & Zinman 2014 (PMC4358152).
  - Opened primaries: Beshears et al. 2020 (PMC7079766), Karlan & Linden 2025 (PMC11894509, abstract only: in Uganda the weaker commitment did better) and Derksen et al. 2025 (PMC12687577: in Malawi, "most men who take up hard commitments lose their investments"). Laibson 2015 (PMC4957524) says only a minority of subjects choose to bind themselves.
- **Automatic escalation: with limits.** I am least sure of this one.
  - The 3.5% → 13.6% figure is second-hand only (Cardella et al., PMC10704390; Mertens et al., PMC8740589; Madrian 2014, PMC4265800).
  - These secondary sources describe the programme's design in conflicting ways: Cardella says it defaulted people in, Mertens says employees committed in advance, Madrian says people were enrolled in a programme. This matters for line B6 (no opt-in/opt-out contrast).
  - One opened primary cuts against it: Choi et al. 2017 (PMC5739328) found a company's 1% auto-escalation "begins to be reversed immediately".
- **Disposition effect: robust as a behaviour; with limits on whether it is a mistake.**
  - Odean's 10,000 households and PGR 0.148 vs PLR 0.098 are second-hand, as reported by Frydman et al. 2014 (PMC4357577).
  - Opened lab and field studies all show it: Frydman et al. 2014, Frydman & Rangel 2014, and Prates et al. 2019 (Brazil, smaller in professionals).
  - Guenther & Lordan 2023 (PMC9996105) found it rational for mean-reverting assets. I found no opened paper where the effect fails to appear.

**Believed, not checked**
- From memory, marked in the note: Thaler & Benartzi's first site was opt-in and not randomised.
- Whether the Beshears 2020 endowments and the lab subjects' rewards were actually paid out is marked "we don't know".
- The search was a keyword scan of about 75 PMC papers, not a systematic review.

**Confidence**
- High that the quoted passages are in the named files.
- Medium on the verdict words.
- Medium-low on automatic escalation: one site's headline, known only second-hand.

**Next, with owner role**
- fact-checker (lane 10, routed by evaluation-steward): spot-open the quoted passages, and settle under W-975 whether "as reported by" attributions are enough. If they are not, each topic still has opened primaries, but the famous anchor numbers could not be used.
- cm-behavioral: recount the fold floor using this note (14 vs 10), and decide whether the escalation line can be written without stating opt-in or default (B6).
- Chief of staff, board: W-1063 can move to "in review" with the fact-checker. Please also note in company/domains/behavioral.md that the claim "no opened source" for these three is out of date. That edit belongs to cm-behavioral, not me.
- Founder, optional: nothing is blocked. PDFs of the three anchors would make the second-hand numbers primary. The DOIs are in the note.

**Not done**
- No anchor primary was opened (publisher 403s).
- Figures were not read, because the PMC CDN is blocked, as B2 found.
- No board or progress.md edits, by the single-writer rule.
- One procedural note: in one probe I used `curl -o /dev/null`, which is a curl output flag rather than a shell redirect. It was harmless, but strictly outside the /dev/null rule.

body:
I walked both lessons and gave both a **Verdict: revise**. To cm-behavioral's question: yes, "between the other two" acts as a cue to pick the middle option. It is the only one of the three option glosses that gives a position rather than a concept. On top of that, the predict card states both numbers needed to work out the answer.

Run: SO-10-3 `[project:behavioral-econ]`, artifact first, adult-beginner boundary using each lesson's own meta.json learner field.

**What each lesson needs fixed**

- **zero-loses-to-this-crowd:**
  - **The cue.** Options A and C name concepts ("0, the equilibrium guess", "About 35, the crowd's average"). Option B names only where it sits, so a test-wise adult can pick it on position alone. The gloss also says nothing about why 23 would win.
  - **The answer can be worked out from the card.** The hook gives the rule (two thirds of the average). Option C gives the average (about 35). Two thirds of 35 is about 23, so a learner who still believes 0 wins can get the predict right without giving that belief up.
  - **The recall has the same pattern.** Its answer is "About 30, between the other two", with the target given as half of 60.
  - **The reveal itself is good.** It says the right sentence and the histogram makes it concrete. The problem is the predict card.
  - **Minor:**
    - A learner who predicted 0 is told "your guess" is the slider value (52 in the recorded path).
    - "seed 2" is jargon for this learner.
- **saved-or-die-same-600:**
  - **The predict question gives the answer away.** It opens "Judged by outcomes, not wording", which rules out option 3. Option 3 is exactly the misconception meta.json names. The right answer can then be picked by matching "sure" to "sure".
  - **The reveal on the consistent path never says people actually switch.** That line (c5) is held and cut. If a learner answers both wordings the same way, they never see "framing effect" either, because those words appear only in the inconsistent branches (c3/c4).
  - **Wording quiz or one decision (the SO-10-3 question)?** The predict card reads as a quiz about wording. The stage reads as two decisions that the "Say both in the same words" toggle collapses into one. That toggle moment is the lesson's best moment.
  - **Minor:** the number next to each bar is the count alive in the saved row but the count dead in the die row.

**Changed** (main checkout, records only, author learner-evaluator, pushed to origin ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1)

B2 (F5, W-1278) is done on branch tools-f5 in /home/user/s3c-tg2, in two commits, not pushed. Large spool files now fold without a stack overflow and the new 200,000-line test passes. One done-when line holds only on a quiet host: the full `npm run test:dispatch` took 23 s and 30 s at load ~7, but 34–69 s while this 4-core host was at load ~15.

**Changed**
- Before starting I fast-forwarded the branch to origin/ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1 at 2f4e9e2. It was 3 commits behind, all records from other lanes.
- **Commit 14699dd:**
  - `/home/user/s3c-tg2/tools/events.mjs`: in `fold`, three call spreads became loops (`events.push(...r.events)`, `bad.push(...r.bad)`, and the F2 re-read's `bad.push(...again.bad.filter(…))`). `dedent`'s `Math.min(...lines…)` became a loop too; nobody had flagged that one, the grep found it.
  - `/home/user/s3c-tg2/tools/lib/events-spool.mjs`: in `readSpool`, `events.push(...r.events)` became a loop.
  - `/home/user/s3c-tg2/tests/dispatch/fold-lock.test.mjs`: one new test, added as the file's last test.
  - `/home/user/s3c-tg2/company/ops/changelog.md`: one entry at the top.
- **Commit 94f6d9b:** an addendum appended under a dated heading to `/home/user/s3c-tg2/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-e1n1-approval.md`. It holds the before/after table, the test, the timings and the commit sha. Nothing above the heading was changed.
- Decision within my role: I left the array-literal spreads alone (`append`, `mergeById`, backfill's `all`). They walk the array rather than pass it as arguments, so they have no stack limit.
- Decision within my role: I first wrote the test as its own file, `fold-large.test.mjs`. Running in parallel with the timing-bound "two fold loops" test, it made that test fail once under load (exit 3, a folder never got the lock in its 3.5 s window). I moved it to the end of fold-lock.test.mjs, where tests run one after another. The addendum explains why.

**Checked on disk**
- **Spread forms on Node 22.22.0:** a quick node script showed `[].push(...a)` and `Math.min(...a)` throw RangeError at 500k elements, while `[...a, ...a]` works. For `push(...)` the limit sits between 125k (works) and 130k (fails).
- **No call spreads left:** grepping for `(push|min|max|apply)(...` in both files finds only my comments.
- **The test catches the bug:** on the old code it fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`; with the fix it passes in 8–9 s on its own.
- **The test checks:**
  - `fold --dry` reports 200,000 would-be-folded and 1 already in the log.
  - `fold` reports 200,000 folded and keeps the 130,000 bad lines in one `unparsed-*.txt`.
  - The log ends with 200,001 unique ids and the spool is empty.
  - A second fold folds 0, so folding is not stuck.
- **Real log and spool untouched:** everything ran in temp `S3_EVENTS`/`S3_SPOOL`, and the test itself asserts the real log size and spool listing do not change.
- **Full suite:** 62/62 in five runs after the move, at the timings above. Without the new test it took 24 s at load ~11.
- **`npm run check`:** passed (969 lessons, 8 existing warnings).

**Believed, not checked**
- Fold output and the lock behaviour (F1, settle re-read F2) are unchanged. Only the three collect loops changed, and the existing fold-lock tests pass.
- `dedent`'s loop has no test at scale. It isn't exported, and only a single transcript message over about 125k lines could hit the limit.

**Confidence:** High that F5 is fixed. Medium on the 30 s budget, which depends on host load.

body:
## Fact-check FC pass 57: saved-or-die-same-600 and zero-loses-to-this-crowd (SO-10-2, `[project:behavioral-econ]`)

Both lessons are checked. 15 of 19 claims are now verified. Two saved-or-die claims are **disputed**, so that lesson cannot publish until the builder fixes the wording. The two held lines stay held, and neither renders.

**Changed.** One commit, pushed to origin/ccr-4c6c7654-ew9ko1 as 662ebbb (local 1e8c8a0 before rebase), author fact-checker:
- /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/behavioral/saved-or-die-same-600/meta.json
- /home/user/system-3-company/src/demos/behavioral/zero-loses-to-this-crowd/meta.json
  - In both files only `status`, `note`, `checkedBy` and `checkedOn` changed (19 claims each way, checked in the diff).
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/saved-or-die-same-600/2026-10-16-fact-check.md
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/zero-loses-to-this-crowd/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

**Checked on disk**
- **Server:** BUILT_FROM and `git -C /home/user/s3c-qa rev-parse HEAD` both read bc0edc0ebf45 at the start and at the end. Porcelain was empty and the server returned 200. Both lesson dirs pass the ancestor test (9d75fb3 and 379a759) and are identical on main.
  - main's newer src/components and src/lib commit (483a52b) touches Life Hacks only.
- **Walkthrough first:** `npm run walkthrough -- … --url http://localhost:3591`, transcripts cut at the appendix (R1). The walkthrough drives only one branch, so I drove the rest with my own Playwright script on :3591:
  - saved-or-die: all four answer combinations.
  - zero-loses: guesses 0, 23, 35, 52 and 100.
- **zero-loses is v2:** the "250 real players" line (c6) is in no reveal. It appears only in the trust-sheet appendix, after transcript line 106, and in the page's serialized claim list.
- **saved-or-die c5** (the 88,181-people line) renders nowhere either.
- **Busiest saved-or-die stage, counted from the screenshots:** 47 words (stimulus 30, other 17), in the toggle-on and reveal frames. The locked frame is 36 (15/21) and the explore frames are 45 (28/17). Both limits hold (other ≤ 25, total ≤ 50).
  - The decision record's estimate of 44 (other 20) left out the key word "alive" and counted the cover, which is gone at the busiest frame.
- **Brief 4 stimulus, word for word:** all six declared strings match the rendered lines exactly. The restatements replace the "die" texts in place, not beside them.
- **Independent numbers:** my own mulberry32 (no imports) for zero-loses gives seed 2 sum 3,463; best guess 2S/301 = 23.010; guessing 0 misses by 22.9 with 84 simulated guesses closer; a guess of 52 gives 34.8 / 23.2 / 28.8 / 86. The seed disclosure holds (seed 1 averages 33.57 and fails the test). These agree with the screen and with cm-behavioral's script.
- **Sources opened** through PMC OAI-PMH (HTTP 200):
  - PMC8432807 (Rachev 2021) supports the name "framing effect" (saved-or-die c4).
  - PMC5303671 (Pantelis & Kennedy 2017) supports "equilibrium" for 0 (zero-loses c5).
- `npm run check` passes. Its one new warning is the expected "in review with a disputed claim". `claims --open` shows behavioral at 6 open lines; these two lessons account for 4, each with a note saying why.

**Why c2 and c3 are disputed.** The two saved-or-die programmes have the same expected value (200 lives each). A risk-neutral rule therefore ties them, and with a tie a learner can pick the sure option in one wording and the chance in the other without breaking an outcome-based model.
- That makes "No model that judges only outcomes fits both of your choices" false in 2 of the 4 reveal branches.
- It also makes the predict question's "must" false for that learner.
- The builder's check script treats the tie as consistent (it compares `Math.sign`, so 0 === 0), so the script never catches it.
- Fix: make the wording strict ("prefers"; "Unless the two were a toss-up for you, …"). The exact wording is cm-behavioral's call.

**Believed, not checked**
- How serious the dispute is. The logic is certain; that it should block publishing is my judgement, because the sentence is false for the standard benchmark model on exactly this problem.
- I verified zero-loses c5 although the same paper notes that, with whole-number guesses, everyone guessing 1 is also an equilibrium. I treated "the equilibrium" as the paper's standard name and recorded it as a finding, not a dispute.
- "FC pass 57" was free on origin when I checked. A parallel SO-10-2 run could still have taken the same number.
- One builder count reached me before I had read builder notes: the commit subject of 9d75fb3 says "stage 47". It surfaced while I checked authorship, after my own count was done, and the two agree.

**Confidence:** high on the numbers, the stimulus match, the held lines being cut, and the word counts. Medium-high that a dispute, rather than a wording note, is the right call for c2 and c3.

**Next, with owner role**
- **demo-builder, with cm-behavioral choosing the words:** fix c2 and c3 in saved-or-die-same-600 (predict premise, mixed-branch reveal sentence, claim text). The fact-check of the two new behavioral lessons is back: 15 of their 19 claims are verified. Two claims in `saved-or-die-same-600` are disputed, so that lesson can't publish yet.

**The dispute.** Both programmes in that lesson have the same expected outcome: 200 lives saved either way. So someone who judges only by outcomes has no reason to prefer either one. They could fairly pick the sure option under one wording and the gamble under the other. That makes the reveal's line "no model that judges only outcomes fits both of your choices" false in 2 of the 4 paths a learner can take. The builder's check script missed it because it counts a tie as consistent.

**The fix** is stricter wording: "prefers", or "unless the two were a toss-up for you". The exact words are the behavioral manager's call. I folded it into the prediction rework already queued from the learner review (W-1315).

**The rest checks out:**
- The two held lines still don't appear in either lesson.
- The busiest stage frame of `saved-or-die-same-600` is 47 words, within both limits.
- The fact-checker independently re-derived the numbers in `zero-loses-to-this-crowd`, and they match the screen.

R3a replaces R3's ancestor clause for every SHA from now on. The "strict" test (every commit an ancestor) stops working with the first record filed on the new server, so it can't be the rule. The test now asks whether the lesson renders as it did on the server, in three parts:
1. Every lesson file except meta.json is byte-identical between the server SHA and the tip.
2. meta.json differs only in record fields:
   - `evidence.*`;
   - on existing claims (matched by id): `status`, `note`, `checkedBy`, `checkedOn`;
   - claims an evaluator appended as `unverified` (the committer is not the builder).
   Any other change counts as lesson content: `title`, `hook`, `question`, `reveal`, `recall`, `version`, `brief`, or a claim's `text`/`support`/`source`.
3. Shared files:
   - Every changed file under kit, components, lib, app, public, content, next.config or package-lock must be outside the lesson's import closure.
   - Shell files always fail: `src/kit/**`, `src/app/**` except `api/**`, and top-level `src/components/*.tsx`.
   - A change under `api/**` passes only if no lesson reads that route's response.
   - A `package.json` change passes only if it touches nothing but `scripts`.

This needs no change to `qa-record` (W-1314), so the protected tools/company.mjs stays untouched. The rule today's runs used ("newest non-evidence commit") is close to R3a, but it ignores `src/app` and mishandles FC verdict commits. None of those gaps fired today.

**Ruling 2 (R4): I agree with the two QA runs.** R4 now fails a record only on a dead end: after the reverse pass the reveal is locked, nothing unlocks within 8 s, and no usable control changes the stage. Step (ii) is withdrawn. An unlock that needs a value or sequence nothing on screen points to is a note to the CM, not a fail. The fold-in text for AMD-011 part 2 is in the ruling. It makes best-of-twenty-on-one-test, two-cells-sum-any-range and order-of-the-bad-year part 2's "false-dead-end controls": they must pass on today's main, or prediction (a) is refuted.

- No lesson file other than meta.json changed for any of the 40: `git diff --name-only bc0edc0 origin -- src/demos | grep -v meta.json` is empty.
- check.sh passes all 40 lessons, both at 5b2fee7 and at b9f22f6.

- `npm run check` passed: 969 lessons, 4 warnings.

**Believed, not checked**
- A claim `note` changing only the trust sheet doesn't affect what QA or the learner judge. The learner transcripts are cut before the trust sheet, and the QA feed spec only checks that the sheet opens.
- The literacy-split-france trust sheet now differs from the bc0edc0 build: it shows c4 and new status pills. The incoming commit 5e54e8c cuts 'young men' (W-1317). Once that change reaches the reveal text, R3a requires a fresh record for that lesson.

## Report: r5 B1 (W-1337), shared-checkout git guard. Built and committed on branch tools-r5-b1. Not pushed, not merged.

**Changed.** One commit, `3ce2528`, on branch tools-r5-b1 in /home/user/s3c-t5b1. I committed by explicit paths with author tools-lead.
- `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/tools/git-hooks/pre-rebase` (new, mode 755). It refuses every rebase in the main checkout and lets linked worktrees through.
  - Before refusing, it handles any `rebase-merge/autostash` or `rebase-apply/autostash` file: it runs `git stash store -m "pre-rebase guard: autostash kept <ISO>"`, then `git stash apply --index` (falling back to a plain apply), then removes the state dir.
  - It prints the files it restored, the stash ref and the s3c-int line.
  - On an internal error it still refuses and prints the autostash sha.
- `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/.claude/hooks/no-pkill.mjs`. It judges the checkout from the payload `cwd`, then any `cd`/`pushd` in the command, then `git -C` and `--git-dir`. It finds the main checkout from the filesystem, so it starts no git process.
  - Refused in the main checkout: `git rebase` (any flags), `git pull` with `--rebase`/`-r`/`--autostash` or a rebase `-c` config, `git stash` other than list/show, `reset --hard|--merge|--keep`, `checkout -f`, whole-tree `checkout`/`restore`, and `clean -f`. Each refusal names s3c-int and `git pull --ff-only`.
  - Everything passes in a linked worktree. The old call `verdict(cmd)` with no context behaves as before.
- `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/.claude/hooks/agent-events.mjs`. At dispatch it records a stash baseline read from `.git/logs/refs/stash`.
  - At SubagentStop, and at a foreground report, it writes one event when the main checkout is mid-rebase, mid-merge or has a new stash entry. The event names the agent label and the state.
  - The event id is a hash of the state, so one state is written once. It still exits 0 on any error.
- Tests: `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/tests/dispatch/guards.test.mjs` (+7 cases) and `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/tests/dispatch/agent-events.test.mjs` (+3 cases). Both test helpers now point at sandbox paths (`S3_GUARD_MAIN`, `S3_MAIN_CHECKOUT`), so no test reads or runs git in /home/user/system-3-company.
- `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-shared-checkout-git-guard.md` (tier 2, status "awaiting principal-engineer-ops"). It holds the repro, the git-version dependency, the permanent brief sentence for the CoS and Leonie, a recovery note for W-1338 and the objections with what happened to each.
- `/home/user/s3c-t5b1/company/ops/changelog.md`: changelog line at the top.

**Checked on disk.**
- **Repro of the hazard** (scratch repo, git 2.43.0, a pre-rebase hook that only exits 1): git printed "Created autostash" before the hook ran, the work tree was already reset inside the hook, `rebase-merge/autostash` was left behind and `stash list` was empty. Objection (1) is confirmed.
- **The new hook, same scratch repo:** the rebase was refused, `M b` and ` M c` came back as they were, one listed stash was kept, and no rebase-merge dir was left. The same held for `pull --rebase` with `rebase.autoStash=true` and for the `--apply` backend. In a worktree the rebase succeeded.
- **guards file:** `node --test tests/dispatch/guards.test.mjs` gives 31/31 in 9.8 s at load 4.5.
- **agent-events file:** `node --test tests/dispatch/agent-events.test.mjs` gives 18/18.
- **Full suite:** `npm run test:dispatch` gives 96 pass, 1 skipped (G5-a), 0 fail. It took 3m48s at load 11, and most of that is slots.test.mjs, the known G5-d problem.
- **check:** `npm run check` passed (969 lessons, 6 warnings, none of them mine).

**Decisions I made within my role** (each is answered in the record):
- **Plain `git pull` with no flags is refused in the main checkout.** Config can make it rebase; only `--ff-only` or `--no-rebase` passes. This goes beyond the brief and is a one-line change if PE-ops disagrees.
- **Event type:** there is no `incident-note` type, so I did not invent one. A stuck rebase is an `incident`; MERGE_HEAD alone, or a stash gain, is a `note` in room incident, so the CoS's own merge cannot trigger a retro.
- **`rebase --abort`/`--continue` in the main checkout are refused too.** The message says to report a stuck rebase with its autostash sha instead.

**Method.** I re-derived every number in my own node ports of the lesson code, with independent brute-force checks. Verdicts went into each claim's `note`, as you asked. I did not touch any `source` field. On verified claims I set `checkedBy: fact-checker` and `checkedOn: 2026-10-16`.

**calibrated-but-unequal-alarms (ai)**
- c1, c2, c3, c6: **verified.**
  - The 80%/20% split is exact at every slider value (h = 5, 20, 35, 50).
  - A's errors are 10/50 and 10/50. B's at h = 20 are 4/68 (5.88%) and 16/32.
  - The sweep gives B false alarms 1.30/5.88/11.86/20.00% and misses 82.61/50.00/31.71/20.00%. Errors are equal only at 50.
  - Reoffenders in B = 20 + 0.6h, which gives 23/32/41/50.
- c4: **disputed.**
  - The sentence is true for the toy's kind of score: a high/low label with the same two reoffend rates in both groups. There, equal errors force equal base rates unless the score is perfect.
  - As written ("Otherwise no score that makes mistakes is calibrated with equal errors"), it is false for a calibrated score with more than two levels and one cut-off.
  - Counterexample, exact in node: score levels 0.1 and 0.3 not flagged, 0.6 and 0.9 flagged. Group 1 has 100/100/100/100 people at those levels (base rate 47.5%). Group 2 has 0/320/90/340 (base rate 60.8%). Both have FPR 23.81% and FNR 21.05%.
  - The published results are narrower. Chouldechova 2017 assumes equal PPV. Kleinberg et al. 2017 is about balance (average scores), not error rates at a cut-off. Neither paper could be opened (proxy 403).
  - **Fix (demo-builder; cm-ai owns the text):** scope the reveal to this kind of score, e.g. "Otherwise no high/low label that makes mistakes can be equally honest in both groups and have equal errors." Scope the claim text the same way.
- **Unrecorded claim, and it is false:** the recall card's `why` is learner-visible but is not a claim in meta.json. Its sentence "With different base rates a calibrated score cannot also equalise false alarms" is false for the question's own multi-level "30% risk" score; the counterexample has equal false-alarm rates. I did not add it to meta.json, because this run changes claim statuses only. **Owner: demo-builder** records it as a claim and rewords or scopes it.

**cut-the-busiest-link (cs)**
- c4: **verified.**
  - I opened two separate implementations on raw.githubusercontent.com. NetworkX `girvan_newman()` re-runs `edge_betweenness_centrality` on the cut graph before every removal. igraph `igraph_community_edge_betweenness` says "removes edges with the highest betweenness, recalculating betweenness values after each removal" and cites Girvan and Newman, PNAS 2002.
  - The primary paper itself was not opened: pnas, ncbi and ebi return 403, and PMC returns a CAPTCHA.
- c5: **verified.**
  - My shortest-path enumeration matches the lesson's loads() on 18,725 cut sets, with 0 mismatches.
  - Non-blocking nit (claim text only, demo-builder): "while any count is fractional" should read "while the network is whole and any count is fractional". Frozen states, including the final split showing 3.5/2.5/1.5, have fractions without the tie-rule message. Learners are not misled: every one of the 17 first cuts gives fractional counts, so the message always appears before any frozen state.

- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/cut-the-busiest-link/2026-10-16-fact-check.md

  - 13:06:30: autostash 166ee49 (author `Claude`, parent qa-tester's 2d6b4d5). The qa-tester report tx-3ab44009de says its "`rebase --autostash` step refused because the shared tree is dirty". It was that run's own push step.

**Changed**
- **B1 (W-1337), `0dd0abc`**
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b1/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-shared-checkout-git-guard.md: C1 is a new paragraph at the end of §0, plus a bullet in §1 and a qualifier in §2. It says pre-rebase covers only the path on which git runs the hook. On three other exits the hook never runs:
    - a dirty tree: git autostashes, then fails with "cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes";
    - a failed reset: "could not reset --hard";
    - `--no-verify`, which skips the hook.
  - On those exits, prevention is only the Bash-layer refusal (`verdict()` in no-pkill.mjs) and detection is only the SubagentStop detector. Neither is live while H1/W-1280 is open, so nothing live covers the path behind the 10:50 and 13:06 wipes. A C2 paragraph is also in §0.
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b1/tests/dispatch/guards.test.mjs: the new C2 test. Instead of racing a background writer, it uses a `post-index-change` hook, in the test's own temporary hooks dir, that writes to a tracked file once while `rebase-merge/autostash` exists. That reaches the "unstaged changes" exit every time. The test asserts:
    - the hook printed nothing, and the work is off the tree, the index and `git stash list`;
    - (i) the SubagentStop handler writes exactly one `incident` naming the autostash;
    - (ii) `verdict()` refuses the command, the 13:06 brief command and `--no-verify` when run from the main checkout.
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b1/company/ops/changelog.md: one line.
- **B2 (W-1350), `012e71f`**
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b2/tools/lib/inflight.mjs: rule 3 now closes a run by batch item only when exactly one run seen so far in the replay, open or closed, carries that item. With two or more carriers the report closes nothing and is kept in `replay().held`. `match()` never returns an ambiguous hit.
  - The held report is shown on the item's open runs as "possibly finished" evidence (`possiblyFinished` → `heldReport`). /home/user/s3c-t5b2/tools/dispatch-check.mjs passes `held` and prints that evidence.
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b2/tests/dispatch/inflight.test.mjs:
    - New test with PE-ops' fixture: X ·1111 and Y ·2222 are both live; Y is reported twice; both orders are run. It asserts X stays open, only Y closes (by key), the hand report is unmatched and held, and a third report naming only the batch item closes nothing.
    - It also asserts that a batch item with exactly one run still closes by batch item (the 9-of-11 shape), and that an already-closed run still counts toward the "exactly one" rule, so a rerun is not closed by a batch-only report.
    - Changed test: the old test asserting that a hand twin's report closes the tx- twin by batch item now asserts the twin stays counted, with the report held as evidence. This is a behaviour change C1 requires.
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b2/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-inflight-key-match.md: a new C1 section, plus fixes to the description of rule 3, to "what can fail (i)" and to the test count.
  - /home/user/s3c-t5b2/company/ops/changelog.md: one line.

**Checked on disk**
- Dirty-tree autostash exit, reproduced first in a scratch repo: "Created autostash: bb8a3f7 / error: cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes"; `rebase-merge/` holds only `autostash`, and the stash list is empty.

- B2: `npm run test:dispatch` gave 99 tests, 98 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the slow test).

**Investigation for C2 (report only, nothing built):** `post-index-change` does fire on the dirty-tree path, after the autostash reset and before git's clean-tree check, with `rebase-merge/autostash` already on disk. So a git hook can see the moment the work gets stranded, which pre-rebase cannot. Two open problems for any restore built on it:
- It fires on every index write, so it would need cheap gating.
- git has not failed yet when it fires, so a restore there would dirty the tree and cause the failure itself.

Building it needs a new readiness record.

**Confidence:** high that both conditions are met as written; medium-high that the post-index-change writer gives the same result on other git versions (only 2.43.0 was tested).

body:
I registered both experiments: EXP-004 for PRD-003 (the swap) and EXP-005 for PRD-004 (challenges). C3, W-1283, W-1309 and W-1140 now each have a dated answer. Commit **f0aea9911932b769688e837c30658abdf3d55f4a**, in the main checkout, author analytics-steward, committed by explicit path. Nothing pulled, rebased, stashed or pushed.

Part of B3 is blocked. Three things the PRDs ask for cannot be measured with the event the privacy review passed. Following the stop-if, I registered them as written, marked them "blocked" and routed them. I did not choose substitutes, and no PRD metric changed.

**Changed**
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/experiments/EXP-004-first-light-prediction-swap-recall.md` (new). The PRD-003 prediction is quoted, with metric definition, period, groups and `would_be_wrong_if`. It also holds the W-1140 answer and blocked parts B1 to B3.
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/experiments/EXP-005-first-light-challenges-recall.md` (new). The PRD-004 prediction, holdout, arm assignment, cohort split, period and checks before reading. Its "Registration answers (2026-10-16)" section holds C3, W-1283, W-1309 and the server list.
- `/home/user/system-3-company/company/experiments/README.md`: two table rows added.

**Answers**
- **C3:** one `exp` event per lesson per browser, sent on the first revisit only, never two.
  - Browsers with an arm send EXP-005 with `arm`. Swap-marked browsers without an arm send EXP-004. Everyone else sends nothing.
  - Volume: every browser that loads the site with challenges on gets an arm, so the "only when a marker or arm exists" rule removes nothing. Every first revisit sends one event, almost all `origin: "none"`. That is at most one per lesson per browser, ever, and never more than the number of `recall` events. I can't give an absolute count: there is no traffic data and I read none.
  - Why the "none" copy is needed:
    1. The holdout is all `none` events, and it is the only randomised comparison.
    2. The `recall` event's `spacedDays` is days elapsed since play (Feed.tsx:258), so it can't pick out first revisits.
    3. `recall` is sent even under GPC/DNT and `exp` is not, so "recalls minus marked" would mix two populations.
- **W-1283:** drop `spacedDays`. It is always 1 under this send rule. The event becomes `{type, exp, origin, arm?, slug, correct}`. backend-engineer must change the validator in `src/lib/events-intake.ts` first; the current one requires `spacedDays`, so a sender without it would be dropped silently.
- **W-1309:** draft and retired slugs count as catalog slugs. `isCatalogSlug` stays matching the whole registry (`allDemos`), with no code change. The reasoning and the rule for analysis are in EXP-005.
- **W-1140:** the EDD-008 Q5 aggregate is defined: first-revisit recall rate by week and by schedule step, from the `recall` table. Cells under 20 learners are suppressed, there is no `user_id` in the output, and it is never joined to `exp` rows. The query text goes to privacy-reviewer before it runs.
- **Server list, exactly:** `[{ id: "EXP-004", closes: "2027-01-01" }, { id: "EXP-005", closes: "2027-01-01" }]`. The close date moves only before an experiment's first row exists.

**Blocked, routed**
- **EXP-004 B1:** PRD-003's comparison group (signed-in 16+ learners who played from the feed) can't be isolated, because the passed event must look the same signed-in or anonymous (C5). There are three options, set out in the file. I recommend the Q5 server-side aggregate. Owners: head-of-product for the group, privacy-reviewer for using Q5 this way.
- **EXP-004 B2:** "recipients whose prediction differed" needs a field the review did not pass. Owners: privacy-reviewer and growth-designer.
- **EXP-004 B3 and EXP-005 B1:** neither guardrail (prediction-to-reveal completion) can tell a swap or challenge play from a feed play. One design should fix both. Owners: privacy-reviewer for a new send moment, principal-engineer for where it sits (C9). This does not block the challenges build, but it must be answered before launch, or the guardrails are reported as "not measured".

**Decided within my role**
- No randomised arm for PRD-003: it would halve a small sample and needs new learner-visible copy.
- PRD-004's "overall" holdout comparison read as all lessons.
- Holdout browsers must behave as if challenges were off, with `/challenge/<id>` returning 404 (a build requirement for growth-designer and platform-engineer).

**Checked on disk**
- No other EXP-004 or EXP-005 exists on any branch.
- `REGISTERED_EXPERIMENTS` is empty today, so no data exists.
- `track()` has no GPC/DNT check.
- `npm run check` passes (969 lessons, 5 unrelated warnings).

**Believed, not checked:** the noise numbers assume a recall rate near 65%. On that assumption, at 150 recalls a feature with no effect still passes PRD-004's bar about 40% of the time and PRD-003's about 30%, and trips the harm line about 22%. This is recorded as objection 1 in each file. I kept the thresholds as written.

**Confidence:** high on the C3 reasoning and the field decisions; medium that head-of-product accepts the literal "overall" reading; low that EXP-004 resolves in 30 days (my committed forecast is 75% "unresolved").

- **backend-engineer:** the server list plus the validator change, in one reviewed change.

**Checked in node (scratchpad script `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3e472d64-8589-5167-8584-c47a01ab4321/scratchpad/s.mjs`; the one-liner is pasted in the brief):**
- **#71 figures reproduce.**
  - P(blue | blue, blue, red) = q exactly: 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99.
  - With one blue pick and your red clue it is 0.5 at every q.
  - A second route, enumerating the true colour and the clues, gives the same four numbers.
  - The odds steps are 1.5, 3, 9 and 99, so the reveal's "9 × 9 ÷ 9 = 9 to 1" is right.
- **#71 stage budget is 12 words** under Ruling 2: "blue" "blue" "red" 3, "chance blue" 2, "Combine the clues" 3, "One pick before you" 4, and the chips count 0. The builder will need a word or two saying the chips set clue accuracy, which still leaves it well under 25.
- **#72 final picture and links reproduce.** Two groups of four give 12 links. Town 1's start has 12 links, 3 of them cross links. The colour string `11100001` becomes `11110000` after 2 switches.
- **#72 step wording does not reproduce as briefed.** If everyone updates at once, both wrong colours flip in 1 round, not 2. The brief's "2 steps" only holds if one person switches per step. I wrote that fix into the re-check line (one switch or swap per step, captions "step k of 2" and "step k of 3").

I looked this up by listing the lesson directories; I did not run `node tools/overlap.mjs` on these two briefs.

**Ruling on #72 "The picture can't tell":**
- **The answer is correct and the stage can show it.** The replays end on identical frames, so C is a demonstrated claim about what a snapshot can't separate, not "nothing can be known". The reveal's "needs data over time" gives the way out, so it doesn't teach hopelessness.
- **The option text is a hedge in form, and the question can be answered without the idea.** "Town 1" and "Town 2" are arbitrary labels on one picture, so C is the only non-arbitrary pick. - **Replacement text** (answer stays C, equal length, A is the tempting misconception; the stage, controls and QA path are unchanged):
  - Question: "Two towns end in this same picture: all 12 friendships join same colours. Did people choose friends like themselves?"
  - A: "Yes: they picked friends of their own colour"
  - B: "No: they became like their friends"
  - C: "Either: a picking town and a copying town can both end here"

**Believed, not checked:** the E&K section numbers stay unconfirmed, as the brief already says, and I did not check claim 3's attribution. The fact-checker does that at build.

**Confidence:** high on the figures and the step finding. Medium on the replacement wording: it is my judgement call, and the brief's owner or the learning designer may prefer other words.

body:
**Verdict: MERGE.** I checked the in-flight matching rule on tools-r5-b2 at 012e71f and wrote the check. It is committed at **7df2448** in the main checkout. That commit holds only the one file, added by explicit path. I did not pull, rebase, stash, reset or push, and I did not touch board.json, progress.md, events.jsonl or the branch.

File: /home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-inflight-key-match-steward-check.md

**What I did:** I read the record in a detached scratch worktree of 012e71f and removed the worktree afterwards. The 12 tests in tests/dispatch/inflight.test.mjs all pass. I read tools/lib/inflight.mjs in full, along with the part of dispatch-check.mjs that uses it. I ran six of my own replay probes (P1-P6). I also scanned the main events.jsonl read-only:
- 1,007 dispatches in total. 907 have no batch reference, 69 have one only in the prompt, and 0 have one in `source`.
- 9 batch items are carried by more than one label. 8 of them are hand twins of a tx- dispatch, 14-30 s apart. The other one is two separate runs of `r5-ops.md#B1`, 8 min apart.

**Rulings:**
1. **Should a twin dispatched within 60 s auto-close? No.** Matching runs by timing alone is a guess. A legitimate relaunch 40 s after the first launch looks exactly like a twin, and my probe P2 shows a 60 s rule would close the live relaunch. The real cause is the chief of staff hand-writing dispatches, which approval C2 already fixes. The cost of not closing is bounded and visible: a twin stays in the count until it is listed (2 h) or goes stale (6 h).
2. **Is label-before-batch-item order acceptable? Yes.** A label can only ever match one open run, because a dispatch with an open label joins that run. A batch item can match several runs, so the unique match has to come first. Probe P6 shows this order picks the right run where the brief's batch-first order would not.
3. **Is C1 acceptable for the hand-twin shape? Yes.** In the 2 of 11 hand twins (#5 and #11), C1 changes nothing: the tx- run closes on its own report, and the hand twin stays counted either way. What C1 does change is the beacon #1 shape. There, a tx- run whose report the backfill missed is now listed as "possibly finished", with the report that closed nothing attached as evidence, instead of being closed. I accept that: it closes by key once the backfill fills the gap. An item that ever had two runs can never close by batch again; I accept that too.

**One residual risk, recorded but not blocking (S1):** C1 only counts runs whose dispatch shows a batch reference. Say the worker's dispatch has none, but a reviewer's prompt cites the item. A hand report that names only the batch then closes the reviewer while it is still working. If the worker's own tx- report also lands, both runs are closed (probe P3b). That is the same unsafe direction PE-ops' C1 was meant to stop. It needs four things to coincide, and none of today's cases has that shape. It shows up on the `in-flight matching:` line, and passing `--key` on hand reports removes it.

**What I believe:** I am highly confident in rulings 1 and 2 and the C1 acceptance, since they are tested and probed. I am only moderately confident that S1 is rare, because that rests on one day's log.

**Next moves:**
- **Chief of staff:** merge tools-r5-b2. The only conflict is company/ops/changelog.md; keep both sides. Then set the record's status as the check file says.
- **Chief of staff, board items I am requesting** (I did not edit the board):
  - T1, tools-lead, P3: list a run as possibly finished right away when there is twin evidence, without lowering the count.
  - T2, tools-lead, P3: add P3b as a test, then decide whether a batch key taken only from the prompt can close a run.
  - T3, chief-of-staff, P2: always pass `--key` on hand reports too; this folds into approval C2.

No protected path is touched, so no amendment is needed.

**Verdict: merge int-tools-r5-b3.** The git stub does not hide a difference in C1, S1-S4 or R2 for anything the stubbed tests assert. I'm highly confident of this.

**What I checked**
- **Where git runs.** I read the tests/ diff and searched every module that tools/dispatch-check.mjs imports. The checker calls git in only two places:
  - R1, through rituals-due.mjs: one `git log -1` per ritual record.
  - C3: `git worktree list`, and only for build/wave runs given `--worktree`.
  - C1, C2, C4, I1, the slot ledger (S1-S4), in-flight and R2 never start a child process.
- **slots.test.mjs.** Every run is `--kind=other`, so C3 never runs and R1 can only add warnings, never failures. Every assertion on warnings filters to `^S[1-4]`, so the stub's side effect (rituals look overdue) is invisible to them.
- **r2-coe.test.mjs.** Wave/build runs can pick up extra R1 failures under the stub, but every assertion filters to lines starting with `R2`, and R2 reads COE files and the event log, not git.
- **Fixture fix.** The `later = now` change in the "release on report" test repairs a fixture that only worked while a check run took more than 1 s. The assertion is not weaker: a slot is released only by a report dated at or after the slot (`ts <= report ts`), and the re-dispatch comes at least one node startup after `later`.
- **guards.test.mjs.** The `commit.gpgsign=false` setting applies only to that test's temporary repos. No guard rule reads signing.

**Slow cross-checks.** I ran them myself in a scratch detached worktree of c002153, since removed. `S3_SLOW_TESTS=1` on slots and r2-coe gave 43 pass, 0 fail, 37.6 s. Both G5-d cross-checks passed: real git and the stub gave the same exit codes, failures and R2 lines.

**Timings.** The full `node --test tests/dispatch/*.test.mjs` run gave 109 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped, 38.3 s at load 4.4-5.5. That matches the chief of staff's 40 s; the ~27 s figure is an idle-host number. The 1-minute load never reached 10 during my run (highest seen 5.46), so I did not do the three timed runs. Those stay open, as be8d5f2 says.

**Gap that predates this change.** R1 and C3 have no tests in tests/dispatch/, before or after this change. Any future R1 or C3 test must not use `stubGitPath()`. This does not block the merge.

Tranche 2 is the second, larger block of First Light's token budget. Project Review 1 approved First Light in tranches, so the money is released in stages:

- **Tranche 1: 3.59M tokens.** Approved and running now.
- **Tranche 2: 8.17M tokens as approved.** It is released only at the 2026-10-23 checkpoint, and it funds the rest of release 1: building the workstreams, the stand-ups and founder reviews, and the work up to launch. Its stop rule is 1.25 × 8.17M ≈ **10.2M**. If tranche 2 is going to exceed that, it stops and comes back to you and the review forum.

**The problem:** the principal engineer re-estimated release 1 at full scope (the ad slot and social back in, as you decided on 10-15). Tranche 2 then comes to:

| Part | Tokens |
|---|---|
| Engineering | about 8.5M |
| Stand-ups and founder reviews | 1.49M (already in the 8.17M) |
| Quality checks: reviews, fact-checks, QA, privacy reads | about 9.2M (6.3M minimum); **never in the 8.17M** |
| **Total** | **about 19.2M** (16.3M at the quality minimum) |

The approved figure left out the quality checks entirely. Both totals are well over the 10.2M stop rule, so **on these numbers it trips on 10-23 regardless of how this week goes.**

**At the 10-23 checkpoint you choose one of:**
1. **Re-base:** tranche 2 becomes about 19.2M, with the stop rule at about 24M. First Light would then cost about 22.8M in total, against 11.76M today.
2. **Cut scope, priced:**
   - without the prediction swap: about 16.5M;
   - without the swap and the ad slot: about 14.6M.
   
   Neither gets back under 10.2M.

One more way it could change: if the quality checks were funded outside First Light, tranche 2 would come to about 10.0M and could pass. These figures are the principal engineer's estimate, not a measurement, and carry a stated error of 1.25x to 1.5x.

## SO-10-3 run, batch SO-10-3, tag [project:behavioral-econ]

I walked the three lessons on the shared review server at http://localhost:3591. BUILT_FROM was 6838dbac0613a3d1f2f5353e83b27d5c0dbf4f2c at both start and end, and the server answered 200 throughout. The selector, run at the server SHA, printed sure-million-or-long-shot (it had no learner record), so I walked it too. It also printed **same-week-a-year-apart**, which was outside this brief, so I did not walk it.

### Verdicts
I wrote and committed the findings first (28fe139) and only then read meta.json; I did not read build.md, the CM notes or the r1 learner records. All three records are in template form.

- **saved-or-die-same-600 v2: revise.** Owner: cm-behavioral.
  - **Blocking:** option 3, "No: same programmes, two wordings", repeats the title ("two wordings") and the hook, so a learner can pick it by matching words. The "Say both in the same words" button is on screen before commit and also gives the answer away.
  - Also: the question uses "one model that judges outcomes", which an adult beginner cannot read. The recall has the same cue pattern ("same outcome, two descriptions").
  - **Lane 10 question (quiz about wording or one decision): it reads as a quiz about wording.** The hook and title announce the second wording, and both wordings sit on screen together. The question is about "someone" else, not the learner. The learner checks a rewording rather than making a framed decision. The reveal's "you saw both wordings back to back" admits this but does not fix it.
  - Smaller: the legend says □ = die, but the dead are drawn as grey filled bars.
- **zero-loses-to-this-crowd v2: launch, with notes.** Is any option still a cue?
  - **Position: no.** The options sit in one row as 0 | About 35 | About 23, so the answer is last, not in the middle.
  - **"Between the other two": weak only.** In number order 23 is between 0 and 35, so a "pick the middle number" guess passes. The recall has the same shape (0 / 60 / 30, answer between). If cm-behavioral wants to remove this, put one distractor on the far side of the answer.
  - Notes: the wording of the question makes 0 an easy option to drop. A guess near 23 is never shown winning unless the learner moves the slider there; this is a note to the CM under R4 corrected, not a fail. "Equilibrium" is unexplained, but that only matters for learners who skip the prerequisite lesson.
- **sure-million-or-long-shot v1: revise.** Owner: cm-behavioral.

FC pass 64 is done for britain-made-most-fossil-co2-in-1850 v3 (SO-10-2 trigger d, [project:history]). Of the 5 claims in scope, 3 are verified and 2 are disputed (c2, c8), so the lesson is blocked until the builder fixes them. Nothing is held.

- Server: 6838dbac0613a3d1f2f5353e83b27d5c0dbf4f2c. BUILT_FROM read the same at start and end, and the R3a check passed (exit 0).

- `npm run check` passes. 2 claims on this lesson are still open, both disputed.

**Verdicts**
- **c1 verified.** The UK made 62.155% of world fossil CO2 in 1850, shown as 62%.
- **c3 verified.** The UK's share in 1900 was 21.384%, and its emissions rose from 122 to 420 Mt.
- **c6 verified** ("fuel burned … not land clearing"). The series does include CO2 from making cement, but that is zero in 1850, 0.07% in 1900, and at most 1.13% of world CO2 in any year from 1750 to 1950 (1.76% at most for any of the four countries). Sources opened today: OWID's co2-dataset-sources page and lines 3 and 162 of OWID's GCB metadata file.
- **c2 disputed.**
  - At 1800 the stage shows "UK 95%", but the claim and history-cycle1-check.mjs section 9 say 96%, and the file gives 95.55%. The stage divides two numbers that were each rounded to 0.1 Mt (31.3/32.8 = 95.43%).
  - The label was already 95% in v2. FC pass 39 wrongly said it matched because it worked the shares from the file, not from the stage's own sums. That was a fact-checker error, and I've recorded it. No COE is needed because the lesson is a draft.
  - Also, "France 0%" at 1800 shows a gap in the data as zero. The file has no France row before 1802 (first row 2.239 Mt), and the years 1803 and 1805–1809 are also missing but drawn as zero.
  - **Fix (history-builder-3):** compute the shares from unrounded values (keep the file's 0.001 Mt precision). Label missing years as "no data", not 0%, and don't draw them as zero. Then reset c2.
- **c8 disputed.** The 4.527% number holds, but the wording doesn't.
  - "Under 5%" is too sharp. OWID's own page says land-use emissions carry "significant uncertainty … significantly more than emissions from fossil fuels". Land-use CO2 is 93% of the world total that year, so a world land-use estimate about 10% lower would put the UK at 5.0%.
  - No source I opened says "for farms". The research note's "mostly clearing forests and grasslands" cites no source either.
  - **Fix (history-builder-3, wording by cm-history):** "counting land clearing too, the United Kingdom's 1850 share was roughly 5%". If "for farms" has to stay, research-lead needs to find and open a source for it.

**Your three questions**
- **The id move for c4, c5 and c7 is not a change.** Their text, support, source and status are byte-identical to v2. In Demo.tsx the data array and the sentences each claim points to are unchanged. FC pass 39 stands. I re-worked the numbers anyway, got the same results, and updated checkedOn.
- **The cultural reviewer's 95% vs 96%** is a real mismatch, not fair rounding (c2 above). The labels summing to 99% at 1800 and 101% at 1900 is a separate rounding effect and doesn't block.
- **Whether "roughly" is warranted for c8:** yes, for the reasons under c8 above.

**For the board (I did not edit it)**
1. history-builder-3: c2 and c8 fixes.
2. cm-history: c8 wording, and whether "roughly 5%" in the reveal reads as confirming the predict option "About 5%" (a teaching call, not mine).
3. research-lead: a source for "for farms", only if that phrase is kept.
4. Non-blocking, history-builder-3: re-cite c6 to the OWID pages instead of the research note.

I'm highly confident in all the numbers, since each was re-worked from the pinned file and the stage's own data. I'm moderately to highly confident that c6's "fuel burned" is fair; that is a judgement on a cement share under 2%.

body:
**Verdict on W-1335 (tools-r5-b6 at e6ea58f): (a) PASS, (b) the code works but the count it gives is too low, (c) CONDITIONAL fit for W-556.** I committed the verdict file in the main checkout as **c48f0c9**.

File: /home/user/system-3-company/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-blocked-hosts-steward-check.md (committed by explicit path; I did not pull, rebase, stash, reset or push).

**What I did:** I read the branch in a scratch detached worktree and removed it afterwards. The 4 tests pass with no network. I ran `list` and a read-only script that uses the module's own matching over all 88 unverified claims. I did not run `probe`. No protected path is touched.

**(a) Probe: PASS.**
- It sends one HEAD per host per run: 33 targets, no duplicates, no redirects, no retries, 10 s cap. Only the status class is recorded.
- It refuses to run and writes nothing if HTTPS_PROXY is unset, the status endpoint is unreachable or returns non-JSON, the proxy reports `enabled=false`, or any status key or state contains "degrad".
- The two probe commits change only `lastProbe` (plus trailing commas).
- Minor notes, none blocking:
  - The "degraded" check is a pattern match, so it lets the probe run if the status format is unfamiliar. Harm is low because the policy is enforced upstream.
  - Proxy health is checked once, before the run, not between HEADs.
  - A curl killed by the 15 s timeout is recorded as `error--1`.
  - The proxy README says not to retry policy denials, so re-probes should run at most once per wave.

**(b) Held-claims count: works as described, and 3 distinct held claims is correct for the hosts listed.** The problem is that the 31-host list is hand-picked and misses hosts that fact-check notes already name as blocked. At least 8 more claims are held on such hosts:
- cs.hailstone-27-climbs.c4 (Springer, fit.vut.cz)
- three energy-tariff c6 claims (ofgem.gov.uk, eia.gov, energy.gov)
- lifehacks.lh-scale-recipe-portions.c5 (fsis.usda.gov, food.gov.uk, cdc.gov, who.int, arxiv.org and others)
- lifehacks.mail-exact-phrase.recall and lifehacks.mail-minus-noise.recall (support.google.com)
- lifehacks.tote-balance-sides.c1 (www.rei.com)

So the real figure is **at least 11 held claims across roughly 45 or more hosts**, not 3 across 31. Two further problems:
- Two French history notes each name about 20 hosts, so 20 hosts show "claims 2" and the ranking can't tell them apart. Per-host counts can't be added up.
- en.wikipedia.org's 151 records are inflated by bare "Wikipedia" mentions; treat that number as an upper bound.

**(c) Fit for W-556: fit as a host ledger and re-probe tool.** It should not be the claim count the decision quotes until:
- **C1:** tools-lead adds the missing hosts and re-runs `scan`.
- **C2:** W-556 quotes distinct held-claim ids, not per-host sums.
- **C3:** probe cadence is at most once per wave, written in the knowledge README.

The rule that the list only informs and never sets a claim's status holds.

**Confidence:** high on (a), from reading the code and diffs. High that 3 undercounts, because I read the notes. Medium on the exact "at least 11": some of those claims also have a fix that needs no web access (a derivation or a reword).

**Next move:** tools-lead fixes C1 (a data change in company/knowledge/blocked-hosts.json, not a protected path). The owner of the W-556 decision answers C1 and C2 where that decision is recorded. I did not touch board.json or progress.md, so whoever dispatched this check should add the board item and the handoff.

**File written**
- /home/user/system-3-company/company/reviews/same-week-a-year-apart/2026-10-16-learner-no-econ-adult-r1.md (author learner-evaluator)

**Blocking finding (owner: cm-behavioral, content)**
1. **The reveal never says "whatever the rate".**
   - The reveal is the same text whatever the learner predicted. Only the kit's verdict line changes.
   - The lesson's own learner profile and misconception describe the option-3 chooser ("Either, depending on their discount rate").
   - The reveal never says the rate cannot change the answer. The recall's `why` does say it ("whatever the rate"), but the reveal does not.
   - So the learner the lesson was built for leaves knowing only "it was wait", with no reason they could repeat.
2. **The hook and the question ask different things, and some paths contradict the stage.**
   - The hook and the explore ask about the learner ("would you?"). The prediction asks about a model ("someone prefers ... they must").
   - A learner who takes $100 at week 52 sees "Steady model: take $100" on the stage. The reveal then says the answer was "Wait a week again", without the condition "for someone who waits at week 52".
   - A learner who predicts option 2 and then really does switch gets "Not quite", even though the reveal calls their own behaviour present bias.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Option 2 is ruled out by its own wording, and the caption almost states option 1.
- "Each week counts the same" can read to a lay adult as "time doesn't matter".
- The strip never says what it forecasts, and it shows nothing when the learner's today choice differs from it.
- Dragging the slider right moves the pair left on the timeline.
- At "today" the two leader lines land on one point.
- Present bias is told, not shown, for learners who choose the same way twice.
- No dead end.
- Claim c3 is unverified but is on screen. The held line c6 did not render, as intended.

**What I believe:** I'm moderately sure of the revise. It rests on reading the reveal strings for paths the walker did not take, not on rendering those paths. As always, this review cannot show that anyone learned.

- **Link the record.** Add it to `evidence.simulatedLearner` in src/demos/behavioral/same-week-a-year-apart/meta.json. This is the same "meta.json collision" class already on the board. The selector will keep printing this lesson until the link lands.

You're right. Today we added 9 lessons (960 → 969) and published 9 (675 → 684), out of about 570 commits. Almost none of today's work turned into lessons you can see. And nothing has been deployed since r7, so the live site hasn't changed at all.

**Where the day went**
1. **Most new building was stopped.**
   - History and behavioral economics hit their budget stops.
   - The token ledger hadn't been updated since 10-14. Once it was, other projects showed overspending, so I told the managers to hold builds.
   - Builds were also frozen for about an hour while the two incident reviews (the deleted system file and the wiped shared checkout) were written and accepted.
   - That left at most 3 builders running at a time, mostly on rework.
2. **Agent time went to checking and fixing.** Fact checks, QA runs, simulated-learner walks and revisions all took slots. They found real errors, but they don't add lessons, and the review queue grew from 242 to 260.
3. **Publishing is the real bottleneck.** About 250 finished lessons are being held:

| Held lessons | Why | What releases them |
|---|---|---|
| 200 Life Hacks | Waiting on Life Hacks' category launch review (it's new, so it is reviewed as a whole) | One launch review |
| 15 Wave J | The simulated learner wrote "pass" instead of "launch", so the publish tool won't take them. A ruling on this has been open with the evaluation steward for 2 days. | One ruling from the evaluation steward |
| 27 | Reviewers asked for revisions | Revision work |
| 8 History, plus 5 for small rulings | Category holds and ruling holds | Head-of-product and launch reviews |

4. **I spent time on process.** Two incidents, the briefs that caused one of them, and the bookkeeping. That's coordinator overhead, not output.

**What would move the number fastest**
- **Publish the 5 lessons that are clear now:** head-on-is-a-wall, electron-speed-in-a-wire, second-speaker-decibels, what-pushes-the-car and zero-loses-to-this-crowd. Today's fact checks, QA and learner walks cover them. This doesn't need you.
- **Get the evaluation steward to rule on "pass"** and run a Wave J launch review, which releases the 15.
- **Run the Life Hacks launch review on the 200.** It's the biggest lever, and it needs the head of product, the release manager and the safety reviewer.
- **Deploy** so you can see any of this. That needs your approval each time.

Leonie is still drafting the floor proposal.

Shall I start the first three now? None of them needs your approval, and I'll come back to you for the deploy.

**Your question on what-pushes-the-car: the Seen row keeps the "wheels slipped" thread only partly.** The row reads "dry: 2,400 N · ice: 1,177 N · frictionless: 0 N", which is forces only. The learner saw it seconds earlier, so this is not a break, but the row on its own reads "ice: 1,177 N" as just a smaller force, not as the road's limit. This is a note to the CM, not a block. Writing "ice: 1,177 N max" or "…, slipping" in the row would carry the thread.

**How sure I am:** moderate to high on the 5 launch verdicts and on the tug-of-war finding. Moderate on secret-in-the-counts (a): a beginner who doesn't read the question closely may still be surprised. These are a borrowed mind's criticisms and hypotheses, not evidence that anyone learned.

**Board asks** (for the chief of staff to file; I did not edit board.json, progress.md or events.jsonl):

summary: decision: founder F-39, agent onboarding, offboarding and personal memory
Dispatch tools-lead: F-39: agent memory mechanism
body:
[project:ops] Founder directive F-39 (company/decisions/2026-10-16-founder-agent-memory-basics.md, commit 4b1eb81). Read it first. Slot: tools-f39-agent-memory.

Build the mechanism so every agent has onboarding, a personal memory and offboarding:
1. tools/org/generate.mjs (agent template around line 92–100): the start step becomes "read your onboarding doc company/roles/<role>.md, then your memory company/roles/memory/<role>.md (testimony, not truth)". The finish step adds "append a dated offboarding entry (≤ 12 lines: did, learned, next holder should know, open) to your memory file; compact it past ~150 lines". Regenerate .claude/agents and any onboarding docs with `node tools/org/generate.mjs`.
2. Create company/roles/memory/<role>.md for all 99 roles, with a short header (owner, rules from F-39) and a seed: up to 5 bullets of real context per role, pulled from records on disk that name the role (latest retros, COEs, rulings, their own review records). Cite a file for every seed bullet; leave the seed empty rather than guess.
3. Solve the parallel-write objection (builders/checkers run many at once): choose and document an append-safe method (e.g. per-run files company/roles/memory/<role>/<date>-<runkey>.md merged by a small `node tools/memory.mjs compact <role>` command). Keep it dependency-free.

I've added the compaction threshold to the memory rule (pushed), and the tools lead is building it.

- **One threshold for every agent:** a memory file is compacted once it passes 150 lines or 12 KB, whichever comes first. It's set in one place, not in each role's file.
