body:
The diagnosis is clear from git and the token ledger, and I don't need to wait for the principal engineer's report to give it to you. That report will check my reading independently.

## Diagnosis: two days ago the company stopped making lessons and started governing them

| | 10-13 + 10-14 | 10-15 + 10-16 |
|---|---|---|
| New lessons | **852** | **10** |
| Published | **641** | **53** (13 today, plus 15 in launch review now) |
| Tokens (agents only) | 72.7M | 30.7M (today counted only to 14:23) |
| Tokens per published lesson | **~115k** | **~580k** |

Today only 15% of agent tokens went to building (2.8M of 18.6M). The rest went to checking, rework, managers, tooling, incidents and budgets. 57% of today's commits are mine: bookkeeping, not lessons.

**Root causes**

1. **We stopped building and kept polishing the same lessons.** After 10-14, every review finding started another version: v2, v3, a new fact check, new QA and a new learner walk each time. Today about 30 lessons went round that loop, some three times. There's no limit on revision rounds.
2. **Every gate is applied to every lesson, one at a time.** These were added after 10-14:
   - a stage word budget;
   - learner verdicts tied to each version;
   - launch reviews;
   - category incubation holds;
   - manager batches before any dispatch;
   - budget STOPs;
   - incident and ritual gates.

   Each makes sense on its own. Together, a 60-second lesson about towels gets the same scrutiny as a medical one. 200 finished Life Hacks lessons are waiting on one review.
3. **Everything goes through one coordinator and one review server.** Every dispatch, merge and single-writer file goes through me. Managers can't start their own agents. That's F-30, still open with you. There are 3 builders, one shared review server, and the checking runs take 1–7 lessons each.
4. **Building has no supply line.** Only about 100 briefs are ready to build. 10,000 lessons needs about 9,000 more, and nobody is producing briefs in bulk.

## Solution: two lanes, gates by risk, batches

| # | Change | Effect | Needs you? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A factory lane**, like 10-13/14: builders take 20 briefs each from a template format, and checking runs take 50 lessons each, run by machine where possible. Only flagship lessons go through the slower craft lane. | 300–500 lessons/day | Yes: the lane split |
| 2 | **Gates by risk class.** Low-risk lessons (everyday, numbers, organising) get automated checks, one fact check and a sampled learner walk, 1 in 10. High-risk lessons (health, money, chemicals, history and other sensitive topics) keep the full set. | Releases about 200 Life Hacks lessons now; checking cost falls about 5× | Yes: it's a gate change |
| 3 | **One revision round only.** A finding means one fix, then publish or cut the lesson. No v3 or v4. | Ends the polishing loop | Yes |
| 4 | **Managers dispatch their own work** within a budget, and I stop being the hub. Each lane also gets its own review server. | Removes the bottleneck | Yes (F-30) |
| 5 | **Raise builders from 3 to 8**, plus bigger hardware or a second host. 10 GB of free disk and 4 CPUs is the real ceiling. | About 2.5× build rate | Yes (spend) |
| 6 | **Generate briefs in bulk:** category managers produce about 9,000 briefs from their curriculum maps, 200 per run. | Feeds the factory | No |

3. **The biggest queue is review: 256 lessons, 244 of them about 2 days old** (added 10-14).
4. **Only 44 held lessons are gate-clean, not ~250.** publish-ready checks the hold first and never looks behind it. Behind the holds, 33 Life Hacks and 11 others are clean; 162 Life Hacks have a learner `revise` verdict and are waiting on F-36.
5. **The agent cap is not what limits output.** On average 6.1 of 14 agents and 1.28 of 3 builders were running, and no builder was running in 100 of 303 minutes.

F3 reset only claims whose text or fixture changed (evaluation-steward). F4 charge coordination to coordination, then decide top-up or kill per line before 23:59Z; needs the founder and one PE. F5 no more guard rounds without a new incident, and the event spool (tools-lead).
8. **Measurement defects (mine).** About 0.55M may be double-counted. The 11 "stopped" closures at 13:08Z inflate the stop rate.

**Confidence:** high on the occupancy, yield and held-but-clean numbers. Medium on the split (label regex, ±10% per bucket). Low to medium on the lessons/day estimates.

It reads neither the holds nor the learner verdicts. So lifting the rows in bulk would let about 150 `revise` lessons be published by hand. Rows have to lift one by one.

**1. What blocks the pass.** The slate is r1's six wave-1 lessons plus `spaced-beats-cram` as a seventh row, which cm-lifehacks asked for; I accepted it.
- **QA: on file for all 7.** Each has a passing 2026-10-16 record on 6838dba, and I checked with `qa-changed` that none needs a re-run at HEAD. Claims are all verified, and each has a learner `launch` on its current version.
- **Safety attestation: missing for all 7.** No `*-safety-launch.md` exists anywhere. Owner: lifehacks-safety-reviewer (W-1082). At least 5 of 7 rows must be signed.
- **Analytics prediction: missing.** Owner: analytics-steward (W-1083).
- Once both are on file, Life Hacks becomes active with no new sitting. The founder ratifies that in OP.

**2. W-1087 (mine): do not wait for the aria-disabled fix.**
- The visible defect is already fixed on main: TP-1 (d995f70, merged in 9302c25) draws the chosen mode as selected, and QA passed the slate after that merge.
- What remains is that screen readers announce the chosen button as "pressed, dimmed". The accessibility reviewer ruled that a defect, not a lock-out, and allowed shipping with the item recorded.
- The fix (W-1114) is blocked by W-1128, an amendment to the protected QA contract, so it has no date.
- Conditions: the publish note names W-1114 as a known defect. QA re-runs when the fix lands, with no new safety attestation needed. The slate stops if anyone rules it a barrier.
- W-1085 is out of date (TP-1 superseded it) and should be closed or rewritten.

**3. How the review scales (R7).**
- **Category pass:** decided on the slate.
- **Wave order still binds:** wave 2 opens when the counted five and spaced-beats-cram are published, which can be the same publish. Kitchen lifts nothing.
- **Low-risk lessons (no one-by-one safety review):** class none or quantity-only, plain pass, and no lifting, cord, drying, furniture or similar trigger. The safety reviewer walks a seeded random sample of max(2, ⌈n/5⌉) per strand and wave. One failure sends that group back to per-lesson review.
- **Per-lesson attestation stays for:** kitchen, energy, shopping (money), every warning or review class, every "pass with changes", and every trigger lesson.
- **A row lifts only when all of these hold:** its safety gate is met, the learner verdict is `launch` for the current version, every claim is verified, QA is current, the fact-checker has confirmed the trust sheet matches the stage (W-1078), its wave is open, and it is not parked.
- **Safety work:** 21 sample walks plus 65 per-lesson walks, instead of 159 one-by-one reviews.

**How many lessons can lift, and when: 33 of 200 in the next cycle.**

| Group | Rows | When |
|---|---|---|
| Slate | 7 | As soon as W-1082 and W-1083 are on file; no build needed |
| Wave-1 low-risk | 7 | After the 14-walk sample, the in-flight recall fix (B3), re-verification and re-QA |
| Wave-2 low-risk | 2 | After wave 2 opens |
| Wave-2 per-lesson | 17 | After wave 2 opens: 3 can lift at once, 14 after re-QA |

The other 167 are not held mainly by this review:
- 133 wait for a learner `launch` on their current version. That is the fix waves and the founder's F-36 reading of the kill rule.
- 30 are parked for retirement review.
- 4 are kitchen and wait for wave 3.

The record's appendix lists every group by name.

- **cm-lifehacks' D9 objection:** accepted. For the five held lessons, the recall moves onto the stage's own numbers. The cost, recall instead of transfer, is accepted for the first publish.
- **Objections:** 7 are in the record, each with what happened to it.

**Asks for the chief of staff to dispatch:**
- **A1, lifehacks-safety-reviewer:** W-1082, sign the 7 slate rows, walking all of them on one build version.
- **A2, analytics-steward:** W-1083, the recall prediction, in the same format as the 2026-10-16 r5 launch review (P1/P2).
- **A3, lifehacks-safety-reviewer:** the random-sample checks (14 wave-1 walks, then 7 wave-2), then the 17 wave-2 per-lesson rows.
- **A4, fact-checker:** check trust sheet against stage for the 33 rows, including shoes-opposite-ends. Re-verify B3's five recall claims.
- **A5, qa-tester:** re-QA the rows marked as needing it, on the build the safety reviewer walks. Re-run the slate after any engine merge, and again when W-1114 lands.
- **A6, release-manager:** publish only the signed slate rows, naming W-1114 in the publish note. Any deploy needs the founder's approval of that deploy.
- **A7, design-lead (optional):** should the trust sheet label a recall that uses new numbers as "a new example"?

- **A9, chief of staff:** board moves (W-1087 done, W-1171 done, W-1085 closed or rewritten). Lift rows only as R7 allows.
- **A10, founder (information):** the binding constraint on Life Hacks output is learner verdicts, not this review.

**Offboarding (head-of-product, 2026-10-16):** I chaired DLR r2 and decided W-1087. I wrote R7, the scaling rule, with 33 rows liftable. Lesson learned: check the size of a requested lift against the W-843 learner-verdict rule, not against `company status`'s "Ready to publish" list. `company publish` ignores both holds and learner verdicts. The mailbox design is better than F-30 as written, and it's being built now. I've recorded it as **F-42** (`company/decisions/2026-10-16-founder-mailbox-dispatch.md`, pushed).

**How it works:**
- **Mailboxes:** every role gets a mailbox folder, and each message is its own file, so agents writing at the same moment never overwrite each other.
- **Requests:** managers decide what their lane needs and write a dispatch request to the dispatcher mailbox. They never need the power to start agents, which removes F-30's biggest unknown.
- **Dispatch:** on every turn and every incoming report, I empty the dispatcher mailbox: check each request against the gates, then start it. I don't re-choose or run a manager round. That step is mechanical, so it can later run on a timer.
- **Reports:** each agent's report goes to the mailbox of the manager who asked, and a manager with unread reports gets a short turn to decide what comes next.
- **Lane rules:** the tool enforces them. A manager can request only roles in its own lane, only the quality lane can request checkers, and nobody can request publishing or a deploy. Caps still go through the seat count.

The tools lead is building it on its own branch: the mailbox tool, the lane checks and their tests, plus a one-page runbook. It's being built separately from agent memory, so both can merge.

**Floor plan:** the tests, the full check and the typecheck have passed, and the production build is running. Leonie's director consultation is in: she moved one seat (the pattern librarian goes to my room, matching its lane) and that fix goes onto the branch. She also listed four floor-level questions for you; none is urgent, so they can wait for the weekly review on 10-19. Her objections are inferred from records, not from the directors themselves.

body:
## F-39 agent memory: report from tools-lead

Every role now has onboarding, a personal memory and offboarding. The start and finish steps are in the generated agent template itself, so a dispatch brief cannot skip them. One caveat: the `npm run check` warning line is in `package.json`, which is tier 2, so it sits in its own commit and needs principal-engineer-ops' approval before it ships.

**Branch:** `f39-agent-memory`, in the worktree `/home/user/s3c-mem`, based on 4b1eb81. Every commit is authored by tools-lead and was committed by explicit paths. Nothing was pushed, pulled, rebased, stashed or reset. I did not write `board.json`, `progress.md`, `events.jsonl`, `founder-inbox.json` or `publish-holds.json`.

**Commits:**
- **09c3ecd** (tier 1): `tools/memory.mjs`, `tools/org/memory-policy.mjs`, `tools/org/generate.mjs`, `tests/memory/memory.test.mjs`, 98 regenerated `.claude/agents/*.md`, 99 regenerated `company/roles/*.md` and 99 memory files from the template.
- **c7b9c22** (tier 2, held): in `package.json`, `"check": "node tools/company.mjs check && node tools/memory.mjs check"` plus a `test:memory` script. Revert this commit alone to drop the warning. Until it is approved, the warning runs only as `node tools/memory.mjs check`.
- **8314d54**: the seeds, plus `company/roles/memory/README.md`, which documents the method.
- **9fa0c95**: the readiness record `/home/user/s3c-mem/company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-f39-agent-memory.md`, with an `## Objections` section answering each F-39 objection, and a line in `company/ops/changelog.md`.
- **79634af**: my own offboarding entry, written with the new tool.

**Checks:**
- `npm run check` passes: 969 lessons, 99 roles, 5 warnings, all pre-existing Life Hacks ones. It then prints `memory: 99 role memory file(s) within 50 KB`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. The worktree has no `node_modules`, so I linked the main checkout's for the run and removed the link; it was never committed.
- The memory tests pass, 7 of 7, in about 5 s.
- Running the generator a second time changes nothing.

### How memory is read and written
- **The rule:** one policy constant for every role, in `tools/org/memory-policy.mjs`. It holds the founder's latest values: compact past 50 KB with no line limit, a target of 25 KB or less after compaction, and at most 12 lines per offboarding entry.
- **Start of a run:** read the onboarding doc, then run `node tools/memory.mjs read <role>`. That shows the memory file plus any run entries not yet merged, and compacts first if the memory is past 50 KB. The prompt says the memory is testimony, not truth.
- **End of a run:** `node tools/memory.mjs add <role> --run=<key> --did/--learned/--mistake/--know/--open/--closed`. Learned, mistake, know and open lines must cite a file, a W-number or a commit, or `add` refuses them.
- **Parallel writes:** `add` never touches the shared file. Each run gets its own file, `company/roles/memory/<role>/<date>-<runkey>.md`, created with O_EXCL, with a suffix on a clash. In the test, 8 parallel runs with the same key produced 8 files. Across worktrees each branch adds a different file, so merges don't conflict.
- **Merging (`compact`):** `node tools/memory.mjs compact <role>|--all` takes a per-role lock, appends the run files to the memory in name order and writes it by rename. Only then does it delete the run files it merged.
- **Compaction:** past 50 KB, compaction archives the oldest entries until the memory is at or under 25 KB. It first lifts each archived entry's learned, mistake, know and open lines, dated and with their citations, into the four kept sections. Narrative and closed items go to `<role>.archive-<date>.md` beside the memory file; nothing is deleted.
- **Enforcement:** past the threshold, `add` compacts first, and `--no-compact` refuses with "compact first". `check` only ever warns, on a missing file or one over the threshold, and always exits 0.

### Seed coverage
98 of 99 roles have at least one cited line, 365 lines in all, at most 5 per role. Every line is dated and cites a record on disk that names the role: retros, COEs, rulings, reviews, decisions, the POC map, WBRs. Every cited file exists. The founder's file has no seed because it is a human role. The 36 strand managers have little real context on disk, so their seeds are mostly their briefs file, their charter line and WBR context, plus NCM or sign-off lines where a record names them.

### Roles I could not wire
- **Press roles** (`vp-books`, `*-system-3`, `review-*`): they are not in this repo's `roles.mjs`. They live in the sibling repo `/home/user/System3` (`press/org/roles.mjs` and its own generator at `press/org/generate.mjs`), which is outside this worktree and my scope. The same edits apply there. Owner: vp-books, through chief-of-staff-ceo-office.
- **Sibling roles:** none exist in `roles.mjs` here; `company/sibling/` holds only the Press snapshot and a founder brief.
- **Illustrator** (the external role's stand-in agent): wired through its own template text.

### What I believe
- The mechanism and the parallel-write method are correct and tested; I'm highly confident.
- I wrote the seed lines from record lines, but 365 lines by one author are testimony; medium-high confidence.
- My branch's copy of the F-39 decision predates points 5–6 (3be6878, 5555556 on the main line). Merging brings them in.

### Open risks
1. Nothing detects a run that skipped offboarding. I proposed this as a risk for principal-engineer-ops to register.
2. If two branches compact the same role, `<role>.md` conflicts at merge. Nothing is lost, but the rule should be that only the integrator on main runs `compact`.
3. Unmerged run files grow until someone runs `compact`. They do count toward the threshold, so the memory still compacts at 50 KB.
4. The 50 KB cap is about 12k tokens per read at worst, roughly 4 times the "~150 lines" in the reading-cost objection. Today's average is about 2.3 KB.
5. Nothing checks that a cited file still says what its memory line says.

### Next moves
- principal-engineer-ops: approve or refuse c7b9c22, and register the risk.
- chief-of-staff-ceo-office (Leonie): the F-39 review.
- chief-of-staff: merge the branch, add `node tools/memory.mjs compact --all` to the integration step and the checklist, and add the board items. My brief barred me from writing `board.json`.
- vp-books: the Press repo wiring.
- analytics-steward: a ledger cut of tokens per run against memory size, after a week.

### My offboarding entry
Committed as `company/roles/memory/tools-lead/2026-10-16-tools-f39-agent-memory.md`:
```
### 2026-10-16 · tools-f39-agent-memory · tools-lead
- did: Built F-39 memory: tools/memory.mjs, one policy constant, agent template start/finish steps, 99 memory files (98 seeded, 365 cited lines), tests (branch f39-agent-memory)
- learned: Per-run O_EXCL files make parallel appends safe across worktrees; only compact rewrites the shared file (company/roles/memory/README.md)
- know: npm run check is tools/company.mjs (protected); the memory warning rides on package.json, tier 2, held in its own commit c7b9c22 (company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-f39-agent-memory.md)
- know: New worktrees have no node_modules: link it for tsc, never commit the link; node_modules/ in .gitignore does not match a symlink (company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-f39-agent-memory.md)
- open: Press roles not wired: sibling repo /home/user/System3 press/org/generate.mjs (company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-f39-agent-memory.md)
- open: No meter for runs that skip offboarding; risk proposed to principal-engineer-ops (company/engineering/readiness/2026-10-16-f39-agent-memory.md)
```

1. I wrote the draft founder brief for F-08 (W-091). It is marked as a draft for the founder to correct, not a decision. It covers the learner problem (a miss is never followed up, a success is never built on, and the opposite risk of a bubble). The first version is rule-based ordering: due revisits first, a "repair" lesson after a wrong prediction plus a missed revisit, a "build on it" lesson after a success, and the learner's stated choices. It sits behind a default-order holdout experiment, with guards G1 to G5. G3 is my anti-bubble proposal: at least 1 in 3 new cards stay in the default order. 1 in 3 is a guess and is labelled as one.
2. Data: it lists the inputs it needs (W-706 events, accounts, a `settings` table that isn't built yet, the curriculum prerequisite graph) and what it must never use (engagement, ad data, demographics including the age band, device, inferred scores), all tied to AMD-008 P2 and privacy-gate rows P3.1 to P3.4. Success measure for analytics-steward to freeze: Surface Value #4, first-revisit recall per learner over all lessons, so no rule can win by serving easier lessons. #5 completion and subject breadth are guardrails; engagement is reported but never counts as success. It also asks for a minimum detectable effect before anything starts.
3. It sets out 8 privacy and child-safety constraints for privacy-reviewer (13 to 15 teen mode, anonymous personalization stays in the browser, no profiling, no use by the ad path), says what can be built before real learners and what can't, gives 7 open questions for the founder, and has `## Objections` O1 to O7.
4. What I believe: the design is consistent with AMD-008 and the privacy gate as drafted (high confidence, about 85%). Whether it is what the founder means by personalization is unknown; O1 and question 1 ask him. Two points are unverified: how many lessons in the curriculum have prerequisite edges (O6), and whether the experiment can get enough learners to show a result (O3).
5. `npm run check` passed with 5 warnings, all on lifehacks lessons with disputed claims, not from this change. I committed only the brief, by explicit path, as personalization-lead. 1. **What I did:** I wrote a draft ads policy for the founder, at /home/user/system-3-company/company/marketing/2026-10-16-draft-ads-policy.md. It is marked as a draft and is not in force. It covers six things:
   - **What a card may be:** house cards only. A card can feature a published lesson whose claims are all verified, a live category, or a "how we work" message.
   - **What a card may not be:** no outcome claims, no engagement framing, no asks (sign-up, share, donate), no outbound links, no "no ads" line, and nothing chosen by tap rate.
   - **Placement and frequency:** the Ruling 3 and AMD-008 rules, plus three new proposals: the first possible slot is after the 6th lesson of a session, no repeats, and a fixed contextual rotation for what a card features.
   - **Labelling:** proposed label "From us · not a lesson". Head-of-product sets the final wording.
   - **Child safety and privacy:** it sticks to the privacy reviewer's rulings (P5 and §6.1): no ad cookies, no stored data, no learner data, aggregate counts only. Under-13s and teen mode see house cards only.
   - **Before any paid or third-party ad:** a list of gates, plus open questions Q1 to Q7 for the founder (F-44, F-17, F-18, F-20, the "no ads" promise) and an `## Objections` table.
2. **W-916:** I tried again today. Domain lookups (RDAP, the public registry lookup) still fail through the proxy, and this session has no Vercel quote tool. So the appendix points to the existing shortlist (Guess First first) and says every price is still unverified. Nothing was registered, bought, posted or signed in to.

4. **How sure I am:** high that the draft matches the existing rule records (Ruling 3, AMD-008 A1 to A10, privacy gate P5 and §6.1). Low on the parts I added myself:
   - The success measure is only my proposal. W-894 is in backlog and no experiment file exists, so nothing is fixed in advance yet.
   - The COPPA and GDPR-K lines are my reading, not legal advice.
5. **Next moves:**
   - **founder:** F-44 (whether ads come after the milestone), then F-17, F-18 and F-20.
   - **head-of-product:** the label wording, the "no ads" promise (Q3) and the featured-lesson rule (Q4).
   - **analytics-steward:** register the experiment for W-894 before any data exists.
   - **privacy-reviewer and counsel:** confirm §4 (W-892, F-25).
